papers.title: Physical activity partly inhibits autonomic imbalance, immune dysfunction and quality of life induced by chronic shiftwork in policemen.
papers.abstract: Chronic shiftwork can impair autonomic cardiovascular regulation and immune homeostasis. However, the interaction between occupational status and physical activity level in military police officers remains incompletely understood. This cross-sectional factorial study included 102 men stratified according to occupational status and physical activity level: physically active military police officers (PMP; n = 26), physically inactive military police officers (PMNP; n = 26), physically active civilians (CVP; n = 25) and physically inactive civilians (CVNP; n = 25). Quality of life, perceived stress, sleepiness, haematological parameters, cytokines and heart rate variability were assessed. Physical activity improved several Short-form questionnaire (SF-36) domains, particularly Physical Functioning and General Health. Military police officers demonstrated lower mean normal-to-normal intervals and lower high-frequency power than civilians, indicating differences in resting autonomic cardiovascular modulation associated with occupational status. Serum interleukin-10 concentrations were significantly lower in military police officers, whereas interleukin-2, interleukin-17 and interferon-γ did not differ significantly according to occupational status. Haemoglobin levels and platelet counts demonstrated significant occupational status × physical activity interactions. Perceived stress scores were lower in military police officers than in civilians. Chronic occupational exposure to shiftwork was associated with altered autonomic cardiovascular regulation and immune regulation in military police officers. Regular physical activity improved quality of life somewhat; however, several physiological alterations remained predominantly associated with occupational status, reinforcing the importance of occupational strategies targeting circadian health and physiological resilience. These findings highlight the physiological complexity of chronic shiftwork exposure in tactical occupational populations.

papers.title: KCNH1 variants associated with neurodevelopmental disorders exhibit prominent gain of function.
papers.abstract: Pathogenic variants in KCNH1, encoding the human ether-á-go-go voltage-gated potassium channel (EAG1, KV10.1), are associated with the neurodevelopmental disorders Temple-Baraitser syndrome (TBS), Zimmermann-Laband syndrome (ZLS), epileptic encephalopathy, and other undefined neurodevelopmental disorders. Investigating the functional consequences of KCNH1 variants can provide information about molecular and cellular pathophysiological mechanisms and help guide therapeutic directions. In this study, we determined the functional properties of 26 disease-associated KCNH1 variants including three recurrent and six that were previously unpublished. Findings were compared to the wildtype (WT) channel along with six rare population variants. Our approach used automated patch clamp recording of heterologously expressed KCNH1 variants in both the homozygous state (variant alone) and the clinically-relevant heterozygous state (variant co-expressed with WT channels). We also examined the impact of alternative splice isoforms on functional consequences of specific variants. We demonstrated that the majority of disease-associated KCNH1 variants exhibit features consistent with gain-of-function including hyperpolarized voltage-dependence of activation, accelerated activation kinetics, or both that promote hyperpolarization of the resting membrane potential. By contrast, one unique variant discovered previously in an autism cohort had a depolarized voltage-dependence of activation and was associated with a depolarized resting potential in cells. Pharmacological testing of KCNH1 variants demonstrated differences in potency for channel block by imipramine and an investigational non-selective potassium channel blocker (LY97241) for specific variants. Collectively, our findings support gain-of-function as the most common, albeit not exclusive, molecular mechanism underlying KCNH1-related disorders and suggest opportunities for potential therapeutic drug repurposing strategies for these conditions.

papers.title: Age-Adjusted Exploratory Analysis of Spectral, Aperiodic, and Microstate EEG Features in Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) can characterize functional brain alterations in multiple sclerosis (MS), but many EEG features vary with age. We therefore examined resting-state EEG associations with MS using age-adjusted models while explicitly accounting for the severe age imbalance in the available dataset. Resting-state 128-channel EEG data from the BrainLat dataset were analyzed. Demographic files included 32 patients with MS and 32 healthy controls (HC); global-feature models included 29 patients with MS and 32 HC, and channel-level sample sizes varied by feature. Diagnosis and age were entered in linear models. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied separately to five global spectral/aperiodic tests, 16 global microstate tests, and the 128 channel-wise tests within each feature. Within-MS continuous age regression and exploratory age-stratified ANOVA were evaluated with the same family definitions. After correction, diagnosis coefficients were significant for global bandwidth (β = 1.928, q = 0.0287), global aperiodic offset (β = 1.816, q = 3.29 × 10⁻⁷), and offset at all 128 channels (β range = 1.52-2.41; q range = 3.56 × 10⁻⁸ to 7.43 × 10⁻⁵). Global central frequency, exponent, PSD, and all 16 microstate measures did not survive FDR correction. No within-MS continuous-age or age-stratified result survived FDR correction. Aperiodic offset showed the strongest diagnosis association under the specified age-adjusted model. However, the MS and HC age ranges did not overlap (21-55 vs 56-83 years), so the diagnosis coefficient depends on extrapolation and cannot establish an MS-specific effect. The findings are exploratory and require age-matched replication with detailed clinical, vigilance, site, sex, and MRI characterization.

papers.title: "Tired but wired" - First-time parents lived experiences of sleep loss, tiredness and wellbeing during the first six months postpartum.
papers.abstract: Sleep loss is a common experience amongst first-time parents and can result in postpartum fatigue. There is a lack of research on first-time parents' lived experiences of sleep and sleep loss, and its associated effects on mental health, parental relationships, and overall wellbeing as new parents. We examined first-time parents' perceptions, experiences and attitudes to sleep loss, tiredness and wellbeing during the first six months postpartum in Ireland. One-to-one semi-structured interviews were conducted with fourteen first-time parents (female n = 10, male n = 4) from October to December 2025. The interviews took place online. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Four themes were identified: 1) the gendered experience of sleep as a new parent, 2) (in)ability to sleep, 3) postpartum wellbeing struggles and 4) resilience and adapting. These themes highlighted how first-time parents navigate their sleep in their new role as a mother or father, their difficulty getting adequate sleep, complex wellbeing struggles as a result of sleep loss, and the discovery of new ways to function when dealing with sleep loss in the postpartum period. These findings highlight the need for healthcare professionals to recognise postpartum sleep loss as both a physiological and psychological experience, and to incorporate holistic, routine discussions of sleep into postnatal care.

papers.title: Dexmedetomidine effects on metabolic rate over 5 days in humans.
papers.abstract: The alpha-2-adrenergic agonist drug dexmedetomidine induces sleep-like sedation and reduces global metabolic rate. Drug-induced metabolic suppression sustained over days in humans could be a strategy for reducing energy expenditure (EE), oxygen consumption (VO2), and carbon dioxide production (VCO2) during prolonged rescue or austere conditions with limited life-support. We tested the feasibility of reducing EE, VO2 and VCO2 measured with intermittent indirect calorimetry using subcutaneous infusion of dexmedetomidine 1 µg/kg/hour for 18 hours per day over five days in healthy adults. Five participants received multiple days of dexmedetomidine in a laboratory setting, and five separate participants received placebo for one or five days. Relative to resting metabolic rate, dexmedetomidine infusion reduced VO2 (effects, 95%CI, at 6-hour time epoch: -0.084 L/min, -0.145 to -0.023), VCO2 (-0.067 L/min, -0.130 to -0.005) and EE (-577 kcal/day, -1016 to -137). Relative to placebo, dexmedetomidine produced light sedation (Richmond Agitation Sedation Score: -1.25; 95%CI -1.70 to -0.80 relative to placebo), with lower heart rate (-15 beats/minute; 95%CI -23 to -7) and core body temperature (-1.3ºC; 95%CI -1.7 to -0.8). Dexmedetomidine effects on all physiological variables decreased over time and were absent after day 2. Maximum and minimum plasma drug levels did not change over days. Participants reported rebound anxiety and insomnia after the study. Administering a sedating level of dexmedetomidine that reduces VO2, VCO2, and EE for 2 days was feasible in healthy adults. However, tolerance to drug effects develops by 3 days, which is a critical limitation for long-term use of this drug regimen.

papers.title: Reduced cognitive empathy and differences in EEG activity in low-achieving adolescents.
papers.abstract: Students with low academic achievement tend to display more maladaptive behaviours in interactions with peers and teachers. Empathy plays a key mediating role in these interactions and is also linked to academic performance. In particular, facial emotion recognition is one component of socioemotional processing that may contribute to empathic responding. To explore the relationship between empathy, emotion recognition, and academic achievement, a comparative study was conducted with 40 students aged 14-17, divided into two groups: one with low academic achievement enrolled in a school support programme, and a control group with adequate academic performance. A multimethod approach was applied, including the Basic Empathy Scale, a facial expression recognition test, and electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings. Results showed significantly lower cognitive empathy in the low-achieving group in the primary between-group analysis. The overall between-group difference in facial emotion recognition accuracy was not statistically significant. EEG analyses identified exploratory between-group differences in source-level oscillatory activity estimates during facial-expression processing. These electrophysiological findings provide complementary information about task-related activity patterns but should not be interpreted as specific neural markers of empathy or as confirmation of a behavioural facial emotion recognition deficit. Overall, the multimethod approach offers complementary perspectives on socioemotional functioning in low-achieving adolescents, although the exploratory EEG findings require cautious interpretation and replication in larger, independent samples.

papers.title: Clinical and genetic characteristics of patients with early-onset or familial parkinsonism: A retrospective single-center cohort.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder after Alzheimer's disease. Hereditary causes account for 10-15% of cases but present considerably more complex clinical manifestations than idiopathic cases. It is therefore imperative to enhance clinicians' recognition of hereditary forms. This study enrolled 29 patients with early‑onset or familial parkinsonism. 17 cases were identified with reportable genetic findings using PD-targeted or movement disorders gene panels. Clinical data and genetic data were collected. Among 17 patients, PARK2/PRKN (n = 9) and PARK8/LRRK2 (n = 5) were predominant subtypes, with two cases of PARK14/PLA2G6, and one case of PARK18/EIF4G1. Clinically, bradykinesia affected 17/17 patients, rigidity 15/17, tremor 13/17, and dystonia 7/17 (including one oculogyric crisis). Hyperreflexia occurred in 6/17, cognitive impairment in 2/17, pyramidal signs in 2/17, ataxic dysarthria 1/17, and pes cavus in 1/17. Diurnal fluctuation and sleep benefit occurred exclusively in PARK2/PRKN and PARK14/PLA2G6 patients. Among patients with PRKN, 7/9 exhibited diurnal fluctuations: five had exon rearrangements, one had a splicing mutation, and one had a homozygous variant. Conversely, the two PARK2/PRKN patients without diurnal fluctuations showed no exon deletions/duplications. PARK18/EIF4G1 mutations may manifest incomplete penetrance. Among PARK2/PRKN patients in our cohort, a potential association between diurnal fluctuation and exon rearrangements may exist, although this observation requires cautious interpretation. Furthermore, these variants appear to cluster within the N-terminal region of the protein (the start of the RING1 domain and preceding regions). Beyond the common PARK2/PRKN subtype, PARK14/PLA2G6 may also be linked to diurnal fluctuation and sleep benefit.

papers.title: EEG reflects subjective but not behavioral hearing in noise performance.
papers.abstract: Ever since the first description of the "cocktail party problem" in 1953, much effort and progress have been devoted to understanding the factors that contribute to hearing difficulties in noise. Hearing difficulties in noise are multifold, and as such have been assessed using a range of objective and subjective measures. Here, we explored three distinct measures of hearing in noise: tone-in-noise (TIN) detection, speech reception threshold (SRT) in noise, and the self-reported Speech, Spatial and Qualities of Hearing Scale (SSQ). We evaluated how these measures relate to auditory brainstem response, cortical electroencephalogram (EEG), behavioral (e.g., frequency modulation, FM detection), and self-reported factors. FM detection threshold emerged as a common factor across the predictive models for TIN, SRT, and SSQ, consistent with the possibility that temporal fine structure sensitivity is broadly related to different aspects of hearing in noise. In contrast, EEG P3 amplitude was only retained in the SSQ model and not in the TIN or SRT models, suggesting that cortical EEG measures may be more closely related to subjective than objective hearing in noise outcomes. Together, these findings suggest that different measures of hearing in noise capture partially distinct aspects of auditory function.

papers.title: Pancreatic δ cells are resistant to auto- and paracrine inhibition in human type-2 diabetes.
papers.abstract: Somatostatin secretion from pancreatic δ cells inhibits nearby α- and β cells and tunes the body's glycemic set-point. The role of δ cells in diabetes remains unclear, in part due to the difficulty separating intrinsic regulation from intraislet paracrine effects. Here, we compared the function of isolated δ cells of cadaveric nondiabetic and type-2 diabetic donors by single cell total internal reflection microscopy, electrophysiology, and secretion measurements. Elevated glucose stimulated exocytosis of somatostatin, which was further amplified by glucagon, exendin-4, or forskolin, independent of diabetic status. gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) enhanced exocytosis and electrical activity, while insulin had no detectable effect. Adrenaline and somatostatin strongly inhibited δ cell activity, leading to autocrine feedback inhibition of somatostatin exocytosis. In type-2 diabetes, δ cell inhibition by somatostatin and adrenaline was impaired, together with a marked reduction in somatostatin receptor (SSTR2) surface expression. The data suggest that selective loss of inhibitory control of δ cells may dysregulate intraislet somatostatin signaling in type-2 diabetes.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: A voltage-gated porin PPE1 regulates secretion and drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) remains a formidable clinical hurdle, compounded by the fact that the pathways by which antibiotics penetrate its multilayered cell envelope remain incompletely mapped. We identify PPE1 as a voltage-gated outer-membrane porin that mediates the secretion of kupyaphores while also facilitating the uptake of the frontline anti-tubercular drug isoniazid (INH). Genome-wide association analysis of 38,038 clinical isolates links ppe1 mutations with INH resistance, highlighting its clinical relevance. Consistent with this, the Mtb Δppe1 mutant shows increased tolerance to INH, accompanied by markedly reduced intracellular accumulation of INH compared with the wild-type strain. The Δppe1 strain exhibits attenuated infection, impaired growth, and reduced virulence in a murine infection model. Electron microscopy, molecular modeling, and single-channel electrophysiology reveal that PPE1 assembles into an unusual pentameric α-helical channel, distinct from classical β-barrel bacterial porins. Together, our findings identify PPE1 as a key determinant of mycobacterial membrane permeability that coordinates metallophore secretion and also antibiotic influx. This work uncovers a previously unrecognized mechanism governing Mtb physiology, virulence, and drug susceptibility, providing a potential target for therapeutic intervention.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: Sleep quality, perceived stress, and dry eye disease among university students in Ghana: A cross-sectional study of individual and joint associations.
papers.abstract: Dry Eye Disease (DED) is highly prevalent among university students and may be influenced by modifiable factors such as psychological stress and sleep disturbance. The primary objective of this study was to investigate the associations of sleep disturbance and perceived stress with DED, while the secondary objective was to evaluate their potential interaction. This analytical cross-sectional study included a random sample of university students aged 18-34 years. Perceived stress was assessed using the Perceived Stress Scale, and sleep quality was evaluated using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. DED was diagnosed according to TFOS DEWS II criteria using the Ocular Surface Disease Index, tear break-up time, corneal staining, and Schirmer testing. Robust Poisson regression models were used to estimate relative risks (RRs) for DED associated with sleep disturbance and stress. Interaction effects were assessed on both additive and multiplicative scales. The prevalence of DED was 77.9%. Sleep disturbance was present in 75.9% of participants, while 21.3% reported high perceived stress. In univariate analyses, both sleep disturbance and stress were significantly associated with DED prevalence (sleep disturbance: χ²(1, 403) = 14.57, p < 0.0001; stress: χ²(1, 403) = 4.20, p = 0.040). After adjustment for sex and the alternate exposure, poor sleep quality (adjusted RR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.05-1.18; p = 0.001) and high perceived stress (adjusted RR = 1.06, 95% CI: 1.01-1.11; p = 0.015) remained independently associated with increased DED risk. Participants with both poor sleep quality and high stress exhibited the highest DED risk (RR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.10-1.27; p < 0.0001), although no significant interaction. Sleep disturbance and perceived stress were independently associated with an increased risk of DED in this student population. However, there was no evidence that stress modified the association between sleep disturbance and DED.

papers.title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea Detection via a Physiology-Informed Superlet-Ridge Framework for Cardiopulmonary Coupling.
papers.abstract: Accurate and practical screening of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) from single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) remains challenging, partly because conventional cardiopulmonary coupling (CPC) analysis does not fully capture the band-specific dynamics associated with apnea-related cardiorespiratory interactions. We propose a Physiology-Informed Superlet-Ridge Framework (PISRF), in which CPC is represented using a Physiology-Informed Superlet Transform (PISLT) with a multiplicative mode in the low-frequency (LF) band and an additive mode in the high-frequency (HF) band. This band-specific design is intended to better preserve pathological LF modulation and physiological HF coupling. Building on the resulting CPC representation, ridge-based decomposition is further used to extract the normalized HF ridge energy (HFRn) as a discriminative feature. On the PhysioNet Apnea-ECG dataset, PISLT-based CPC outperformed CPC derived from the continuous wavelet transform and wavelet synchrosqueezing transform, achieving 84.40% average accuracy and 80.17% average F1-score across classifiers. By further incorporating the HFRn ridge feature, PISRF improved performance to 85.01% average accuracy and 81.33% average F1-score. These results support PISRF as an interpretable and practically deployable ECG-based framework for OSA screening.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

papers.title: A Physiology-Informed Deep Learning Approach for Sleep-EEG Brain Age Estimation.
papers.abstract: Sleep electroencephalography (EEG) contains rich signatures of biological aging, but deep-learning brain-age models often provide limited physiologic readouts. This study presents a physiology-informed deep learning framework that estimates brain age from whole-night polysomnography (PSG) and provides spectral-band-level and sleep-stage-level readouts of the features associated with age predictions. Trained and evaluated on approximately 10,000 PSG recordings across four cohorts (SHHS, MrOS, STAGES, and CFS), the model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 5.89 $\pm$ 5.01 years. External validation in an independent cohort (HomePAP) yielded an MAE of 5.41 $\pm$ 4.57 years. The brain age gap (BAG; predicted minus chronological age) was associated with mortality risk. Specifically, each 10-year increase in BAG was associated with a 19% increase in all-cause mortality risk (hazard ratio (HR)=1.19 [95% CI: 1.11-1.28]; p<0.001) and a 25% increase in cardiovascular mortality risk (HR=1.25 [1.07-1.46]; p=0.006) after adjustment for covariates. A trainable Gabor filter bank provides explicit center-frequency and bandwidth parameters for the learned spectral representation. Spectral features extracted using the learned filter bank explained additional variance in age beyond features computed from canonical EEG bands (incremental $\triangle \rm{R}^{2}$=4.7%; p<0.001). Attribution analysis with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) revealed age-dependent shifts in spectral importance, including decreased delta and increased beta contributions with age. The model also reflected known age-related changes in sleep stages (increased wake, reduced N3/REM). Collectively, these findings provide brain-age estimates with explicit spectral-band-level and sleep-stage-level readouts that align with established sleep neurophysiology.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

papers.title: Metabolic Syndrome in Adults with Polysomnography-Confirmed Obstructive Sleep Apnoea: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) and metabolic syndrome (MetS) are prevalent cardio-metabolic conditions which frequently coexist. Growing evidence indicates a positive association between OSA and MetS, but up-to-date global data are lacking, leaving the true strength of the association uncertain. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to provide an updated and comprehensive synthesis of evidence on the risk of MetS in adults with polysomnography (PSG)-confirmed OSA. A systematic review and three-level random-effects meta-analysis were conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Searches were performed of the Ovid MEDLINE (Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online), CINAHL (Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature), Cochrane and Embase databases, yielding 8072 records. Studies reporting either odds ratios (OR) for MetS in adults with PSG-confirmed OSA compared to those without OSA, or with data to calculate these, were eligible for inclusion. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoBANS (Risk of Bias Assessment tool for Non-randomised Studies) tool. Subgroup analyses and meta-regression were performed to explore sources of heterogeneity. A total of 68 studies from 24 countries with 74 relevant effect sizes were included (24,663 adults with PSG-confirmed OSA; 11,423 without OSA). Adults with OSA had over threefold higher odds of MetS compared with those without (odds ratio 3.33, 95% confidence interval 2.86-3.87; p < 0.0001). Substantial heterogeneity was noted (I2 = 73.8%). Study design, geographic region, MetS definition/criteria, Apnoea-Hypopnea Index OSA diagnostic threshold and publication year significantly moderated the pooled estimate (all p < 0.05). A larger body mass index difference between groups was associated with higher odds of MetS (β = 0.14, t = 4.03, p < 0.001), whereas a higher proportion of male participants was associated with lower odds of MetS (β = - 0.01, t = - 2.81, p < 0.010). Adults with PSG-confirmed OSA have over threefold higher odds of having MetS, consistently across diverse populations. Thus, early and routine metabolic screening is recommended for all adults with OSA. Future research should incorporate longitudinal and genetic data to explore causal links between OSA and MetS. CRD420251073055.

papers.title: After the Spasms: Long-Term Outcomes Following Pulsatile Dexamethasone Therapy for Infantile Epileptic Spasms Syndrome: A Retrospective Observational Study.
papers.abstract: Dexamethasone pulse therapy is a novel, individualizable treatment option for infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS). Whereas its safety and efficacy was demonstrated in the short term, follow-up data beyond the first months post-therapy remains limited. We present a comprehensive long-term outcome analysis of the cohort of 66 infants with IESS treated with pulsatile dexamethasone. Clinical, demographic and electroencephalogram (EEG) data of the 66 infants included in the original publication was assessed retrospectively. Time period between last dexamethasone pulse and last follow-up until March 2026 was included. Mortality data, developmental status, seizure control and relapse characteristics, and use of pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic epilepsy treatment modalities were extracted from the medical records. Sixty-three infants with a 60% male prevalence, all treated with pulsatile dexamethasone for IESS, were followed up for an average of 6.3 years. Seizure relapse occurred in 54% of patients 1.7 years post-therapy on average, with 50% of relapses within 2.7 months after last dexamethasone pulse. Number of pulses and interval between them showed no association with seizure relapse timing or semiology; sustained seizure freedom was achieved among infants receiving 4-7 pulses. Structural and unknown IESS etiology was associated with highest (76%) and lowest (30%) relapse rate, respectively. Among children with structural etiologies, early seizure relapse was associated with subsequent epilepsy surgery. Developmental abnormalities affected 75% of subjects at last follow-up. Only patients with unknown IESS etiology presenting with developmental delay at diagnosis regained normal neurocognitive status. Pulsatile dexamethasone for IESS treatment shows long-term outcomes comparable with other corticosteroids; patients achieving seizure freedom in the examined population received 4-7 pulses. Majority of seizure relapses occur within the first year after therapy, highlighting the importance of close follow-up, and early relapse in structural IESS may warrant prompt referral for epilepsy surgery evaluation.

papers.title: Red and near-infrared photobiomodulation in precision medicine: mechanisms, dosimetry, and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Phototherapy is a non-invasive therapeutic modality that uses specific wavelengths of light to modulate biological processes and treat disease. Driven by advances in photobiology, regenerative medicine, and clinical technology, phototherapy has evolved from empirical heliotherapy into a mechanism-based intervention with expanding medical applications. This review places the biological effects, therapeutic indications, and safety profiles of ultraviolet, blue, and green light in comparative context, while focusing primarily on the mechanisms, dosimetry, and clinical translation of red and near-infrared photobiomodulation (PBM). Although ultraviolet and blue light therapies have established roles in dermatology and neonatal jaundice, their clinical use is limited by concerns such as photocarcinogenesis, retinal phototoxicity, and circadian disruption. In contrast, red and near-infrared light offer deeper tissue penetration and, when appropriately dosed, a comparatively low risk of direct photochemical injury. Through mitochondrial, redox, inflammatory, and other context-dependent signaling pathways, red/NIR PBM has been investigated in wound repair, chronic pain, osteoarthritis, musculoskeletal disorders, neurological conditions, and dermatological applications. As a representative quantitative example, a 2024 meta-analysis of 10 placebo-controlled randomized trials involving 542 participants with knee osteoarthritis found a moderate reduction in pain at rest with PBM compared with placebo (standardized mean difference, - 0.70; 95% confidence interval, - 1.10 to - 0.20), although the certainty of evidence was very low. However, broader clinical translation remains constrained by heterogeneous dosimetry, insufficiently standardized treatment protocols, and uneven evidence maturity across indications. To address these limitations, we propose a precision-oriented framework that links clinical target, tissue-optical context, wavelength selection, patient- and site-specific modifiers, dosimetric implications, measurable endpoints, and evidence maturity. This framework is intended to support treatment planning, parameter reporting, and prospective validation rather than to prescribe currently validated individualized dosing algorithms.

papers.title: [Three-dimensional electroanatomic mapping in the electrophysiology lab: when, how and why? : A practical introduction for early-career electrophysiologists].
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional electroanatomic mapping has become an integral part of modern invasive electrophysiology. It combines catheter localization, patient-specific cardiac anatomy, local electrograms, activation timing, voltage information, and ablation lesion documentation within a spatial working model. For early-career electrophysiologists, however, the interpretation of these maps can be challenging. This review provides a practical introduction to three-dimensional (3D) mapping for young electrophysiologists during their first steps in the electrophysiology laboratory. It addresses when 3D mapping is useful or necessary, how a map is created, what information can be derived from different map types, and which pitfalls should be avoided. The article summarizes technical principles and clinical applications of 3D electroanatomic mapping based on current expert consensus documents, review articles, and practical electrophysiological concepts. 3D mapping is particularly valuable in atrial fibrillation ablation, atypical atrial tachycardias, ventricular tachycardias, redo procedures, congenital or postsurgical anatomy, and low-fluoroscopy workflows. Activation maps help visualize the temporal sequence of electrical propagation, whereas voltage maps provide information on scar, low-voltage areas, and potential arrhythmogenic substrate. The quality of a map depends on stable rhythm, reliable temporal and spatial references, catheter contact, signal quality, adequate point density, and correct annotation. 3D mapping is a powerful tool for navigation, mechanism analysis, substrate characterization, and ablation documentation. Nevertheless, it does not replace electrophysiological reasoning. Every map must be interpreted critically and validated using intracardiac electrograms, surface ECG, anatomy, pacing maneuvers, and defined procedural endpoints.

papers.title: Impact of Epileptiform Abnormalities on Functional Phenotype in a Cohort of Autism Spectrum Disorder Patients With or Without Epilepsy: A Monocentric Retrospective Study.
papers.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and epilepsy frequently co-occur, suggesting shared neurobiological underpinnings. While no specific seizure type or epilepsy syndrome is consistently associated with ASD, Epileptiform Abnormalities (EAs) are commonly observed in affected individuals, though their clinical significance remains unclear. This study examined the impact of EAs and epilepsy on the functional phenotype of 338 individuals with ASD, assessed through video-EEG (v-EEG) and standardized psychometric tools (ADOS-2, Leiter-R, WISC-IV, VABS). Results showed that ASD individuals with epilepsy exhibited significantly lower cognitive performance compared to those with ASD alone or with EAs. Additionally, greater symptom severity was observed in the ASD-+EA group. However, no significant differences emerged in adaptive functioning or language abilities. These findings highlight the potential influence of epileptiform activity on cognitive and behavioral outcomes in ASD. Further longitudinal research is warranted to elucidate the prognostic implications of EAs in ASD and better characterize its impact on functional profile.
papers.journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

papers.title: Supporting sciatica: a qualitative evidence synthesis of the needs and preferences of people with lumbar radicular pain when self-managing their condition.
papers.abstract: To synthesise qualitative evidence on the self‑management needs, preferences and coping strategies of adults living with lumbar radicular pain (LRP), and to identify content for supported self‑management. A systematic qualitative evidence synthesis was conducted using Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and the ConQual approach. MEDLINE, CINAHL and PsycINFO were searched from inception to 26 December 2025, with additional citation searching. Eligible peer‑reviewed qualitative studies included adults with clinically diagnosed LRP and reported self‑management needs, preferences, coping strategies or rehabilitation‑relevant experiences. Study findings and participant quotations were extracted and synthesised thematically. Nine studies involving six UK NHS cohorts and 117 participants were included. Six interconnected themes described self‑management experiences: making symptoms predictable, coping day‑to‑day, adapting to physical limits, managing emotional burden, optimising sleep and evolving a new identity. People with LRP need self‑management support that goes beyond generic activity advice. Effective interventions should help individuals understand fluctuating pain and neurological symptoms, create personalised flare‑up and medication strategies, modify daily activities and work demands, address sleep disruption, and receive support for emotional distress and identity changes. These findings can guide clinical practice and inform the design and content of future self‑management interventions.

papers.title: Infant Sleep Consolidation Assessed by Maternal Perception and Actigraphy.
papers.abstract: This study aims to (1) compare three different subjective and objective measures in assessing the proportion of infants sleeping through the night and (2) identify which sleep variables contribute to maternal appraisal of sleeping through the night. Fifty-six mothers of 6-months-old infants completed the Sleep Practices Questionnaire (SPQ), assessing at what age their infant started to sleep through the night. Infants were dichotomized as sleeping through the night or not at 6 months. Total nocturnal sleep duration, longest consecutive sleep duration, and total duration of nocturnal awakenings were measured with sleep diaries and actigraphy (12 nights). The proportion of infants sleeping through the night was assessed using the SPQ, sleep diaries and actigraphy. Forward binary logistic regression was used to determine which diary or actigraphy variables contributed to maternal appraisal. Less than half of infants were sleeping through the night when using the SPQ (44.2%) and sleep diaries (39.5%), while this proportion increased to 90.7% with actigraphy. Sleep-diary consecutive sleep duration was the only variable contributing to maternal appraisals of sleeping through the night. While the type of measurements yielded different proportions, sleep-diary derived longest consecutive sleep duration was highly associated with maternal appraisal.

papers.title: Fatigue links sociodemographic risk to pain intensity and spread in 2 surgical cohorts.
papers.abstract: Why some surgical patients develop pain that extends beyond the original site of injury while others do not remains poorly understood. The recently proposed Risk of Pain Spread (ROPS) framework integrates multiple psychosocial risk factors associated with widespread pain, but its generalizability to surgical populations has not been established. Using 2 large presurgical cohorts of participants undergoing total knee arthroplasty or thoracic surgery, we evaluated the generalizability of the ROPS framework and examined relationships among psychosocial and sociodemographic factors, surgical-site pain, nonsurgical-site pain, and widespread pain using complementary latent-variable, regression, Bayesian network, and mediation analyses. Across cohorts and analytical approaches, fatigue emerged as the most consistent correlate of pain outcomes, independent of other measured risk factors. Fatigue also occupied a central position within the conditional dependency structure of psychosocial and pain variables and accounted for substantial shared variance linking sleep disturbance, depressive symptoms, neuroticism, adverse childhood experiences, and socioeconomic disadvantage with pain intensity. Nonsurgical-site pain consistently occupied a position linking pain intensity with widespread pain across complementary analyses. Together, these findings externally validate the ROPS framework in clinically relevant surgical populations and identify fatigue as a central correlate linking biopsychosocial vulnerability with pain burden.

papers.title: Statistical Characterization of Received Signal Power for Spectrum-Based GNSS Interference Detection.
papers.abstract: This paper presents methods for accurate signal characterization in Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) interference detection systems based on spectral analysis of received signals. It specifically characterizes the power variability of signals observed at monitoring stations within such systems. The study is conducted in the context of the currently developed Real-Time GNSS Monitoring System for Poland (RTGMS), whose pilot version was successfully deployed in 2025. The analysis focuses on the impact of power variability of multiple uncorrelated signal components of the received GNSS signals. The results are based on a series of simulations which are validated against measurements collected over several months, encompassing multiple satellite navigation frequency bands. The findings contribute to an improved characterization of signal power variability and highlight its relevance for the design and operation of practical interference detection systems.

papers.title: Overt and Covert Speech-State Classification from Tripolar Concentric Ring Electrode EEG: A 4 mm and 10 mm Configuration Study.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) speech-state classification is a noninvasive method to identify the brain's overt and covert behavior. The EEG achieved through the scalp is contaminated by artifacts and volume conduction and suffers from poor spatial resolution. We present the first application of small 4 mm tripolar concentric ring electrodes (TCREs) to record the overt and covert EEG signals. In addition, EEG signals were recorded for overt and covert behavior using a 10 mm TCRE as a reference. Data were recorded from 16 participants (4 mm, n=8; 10 mm, n=8). Each participant completed 200 picture-naming trials (100 overt and 100 covert). The analysis includes task-to-baseline root mean square ratios, power spectral density, time frequency representation analysis and participant-wise overt and covert classification using linear discriminant analysis, support vector machines, and EEGNet. The overt speech produced higher task-to-baseline ratios than covert speech. In addition, EEGNet achieved the highest mean accuracy (84.06±15.57%), followed by SVM (81.56±14.23%) and LDA (76.56±15.30%).

papers.title: A Comparative Review and Benchmarking Evaluation of Step Detection Methods for Longitudinal Gait Assessment.
papers.abstract: Gait analysis based on inertial measurement units (IMUs) enables scalable longitudinal gait assessment, with step detection as a foundational component. However, an understanding of available step detection methods and their comparative performance across sensor placements, clinical populations, and real-world environments remains limited. This paper addresses this gap through a twofold contribution. First, a structured taxonomic review organises the landscape into six families-rule-based heuristics, phase portrait, template matching, time-frequency analysis, adaptive oscillators, and machine learning-characterising the trade-offs of each in terms of noise robustness, generalisability, and computational efficiency. Second, nine algorithms drawn from five of these families, all but phase portrait, are benchmarked across three large datasets encompassing healthy adults and people with mobility-impairing conditions such as Parkinson's disease and multiple sclerosis, at multiple sensor placements under both controlled laboratory and free-living conditions. Accuracy depended on sensor placement, gait pathology and recording environment: step detection proved reliable in structured laboratory settings across most sensor locations and clinical cohorts, whereas unsupervised free-living monitoring produced a substantial degradation for most algorithms. Over all conditions, the three evaluated time-frequency methods obtained the best average ranks for detection accuracy, step-duration error and cadence error.

papers.title: A Novel Adaptive Synchrosqueezing Transform Based on Enhanced STFT Scheme for Wind Turbine Bearing Fault Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of the instantaneous frequency (IF) of multi-component non-stationary signals is crucial for the fault diagnosis of wind turbine transmission systems under variable speed. Current methodologies exhibit several key limitations, such as unsatisfied accuracy of instantaneous parameter estimation due to the inadequate time-frequency representation, poor time-frequency energy concentration and multimode separation effects caused by a single post-processing technique, and the inability of non-adaptative window parameters to dynamically accommodate the local time-varying frequency characteristics of signals. These deficiencies degrade time-frequency plane interpretability and the accuracy of extracting time-varying fault features. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Improved Short-Time Fourier Transform-based Adaptive Synchrosqueezing Transform (ISTFT-ASST) and demonstrates its application in wind turbine bearing fault diagnosis. Firstly, to achieve the precisely parameter estimation of multi-component non-stationary signals, an improved Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) sparse observation model integrated with the Finite Rate of Innovation (FRI) is innovatively constructed. Secondly, Synchrosqueezing Extraction Transform (SET), a time-frequency post-processing technique, is incorporated to further enhance the time-frequency concentration. Finally, drawing on the idea of local Rényi entropy-based window parameter estimation, an adaptive Synchrosqueezing algorithm is designed to dynamically accommodate the time-varying frequency characteristics. Through the analysis of numerical simulation signals and measured wind turbine vibration signals, the effectiveness of the proposed ISTFT-ASST in extracting time-varying features is verified, establishing a novel approach for wind turbine fault diagnosis.

papers.title: Detection and Classification of Physiological Activation States Through Biosignal Analysis Using Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Monitoring autonomic nervous system responses offers significant potential for personalized health applications and early intervention. This study presents a machine learning framework for binary classification of physiological activation states using electrocardiogram (ECG) and respiratory (RESP) signals from the WESAD dataset. Stress and amusement were grouped as Activation, whereas baseline and meditation were grouped as Non-Activation. The processing pipeline incorporates R-peak detection, temporal segmentation, handcrafted feature extraction, and subject-independent evaluation. Conventional machine learning classifiers and deep learning architectures were evaluated, together with a proposed Hybrid Multi-Scale Temporal Convolutional-Conformer (MST-Conformer) combining temporal representations learned from ECG and RESP waveforms with handcrafted physiological features. Performance was assessed using 15-fold Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation. Adding respiration-derived features to ECG-derived features improved conventional machine learning performance, increasing the highest balanced accuracy from 0.752 to 0.807 and AUC from 0.802 to 0.886. The complete Hybrid MST-Conformer incorporating 27 physiological features achieved a mean accuracy of 0.825, balanced accuracy of 0.820, F1-score of 0.763, and AUC of 0.904. Subject-level analysis also revealed substantial physiological heterogeneity. These results support the potential of combining learned temporal representations with handcrafted physiological information for subject-independent physiological activation classification.

papers.title: Closed-Loop Acoustic Stimulation of Slow Oscillations Using a Wireless EEG Headband: A Polysomnography-Validated Feasibility Study.
papers.abstract: Acoustic stimulation precisely timed during sleep can enhance slow oscillations (SOs), a hallmark of deep sleep that is critical for restorative sleep. To date, this approach has largely been restricted to laboratory settings using high-density electroencephalography (EEG). Wearable EEG systems featuring closed-loop acoustic stimulation could enable scalable, home-based approaches to modulating slow-wave sleep. Here, we tested whether a real-time modeling approach (M-CLNS) could be implemented using a wireless EEG headband with forehead electrodes in healthy participants. Acoustic stimulation was delivered during a single night of sleep in alternating stimulation and sham conditions. We evaluated the accuracy of SO phase targeting utilizing the EEG headband and assessed whether it could be used to detect stimulation-induced changes in oscillatory dynamics. The findings were validated against simultaneous polysomnographic (PSG) recordings as an independent reference. We found that SO phase was targeted consistently near the intended phase using the headband, despite reduced amplitude and signal quality compared with simultaneous PSG. Acoustic stimulation produced an immediate enhancement of SO dynamics, as well as sustained increases in SO density and power spectral density within the SO and delta frequency range (0.75-5 Hz) during deep sleep. These effects were apparent both in the EEG headband and PSG signals. These results demonstrate the feasibility of closed-loop acoustic stimulation using a wireless EEG headband, providing a foundation for future home-based and clinical applications.

papers.title: Tablet-Camera Iris Landmarks and EEG/PPG-Derived Arousal Indices During Naturalistic Reading: Geometric Confounding and Exploratory Within-Subject Associations.
papers.abstract: Arousal, the activation dimension of the valence-arousal circumplex, indexes alertness and engagement independently of pleasantness. We evaluated whether MediaPipe FaceLandmarker iris landmark distances from a tablet camera estimate electroencephalography (EEG)- and photoplethysmography (PPG)-derived arousal markers during naturalistic reading. Recordings from 48 participants yielded 43,923 thirty-second windows. Raw iris distances correlated with EEG alpha (r=+0.118) and theta (r=+0.076), but face scale explained 93% of their variance. After face-width normalisation, alpha remained associated (r=+0.076), whereas theta was not statistically significant. Further adjustment for ocular luminance and head pose rendered alpha nonsignificant (r=+0.021, p=0.33). Circular-shift testing identified alpha coupling in 11/48 participants under full control, versus 28/48 using uncorrected Pearson tests. Within-subject Ridge regression, with no raw sample shared between the training and test windows, yielded a nonsignificant group mean correlation (r=+0.078, p=0.07); 13/48 participants had individually significant prediction-reference associations (11 positive), fewer when the PPG term was restricted to filter-consistent beats. Both counts are exploratory, nominal and uncorrected across participants, and come from different analyses. Neither establishes prospective monitoring performance, and the study does not validate the landmark distance as a pupil measure.

papers.title: Multimodal Sensing and Digital Biomarkers in Virtual Reality-Based Cognitive Rehabilitation: Clinical Validation, Adaptive Systems, and Real-World Translation.
papers.abstract: Virtual reality (VR) is evolving from a platform for cognitive exercises into an instrumented rehabilitation environment capable of simultaneously delivering treatment and quantifying behavior. This critical narrative review examines how behavioral, ocular, kinematic, physiological, and neurophysiological signals can be transformed into clinically meaningful digital measures, candidate biomarkers, adaptive interventions, and real-world functional outcomes. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore were searched from database inception to 20 September 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation searching and targeted searches. Clinical, methodological, validation, and directly relevant technical studies were considered, including studies in healthy participants when methodologically informative. Of 690 records identified, 145 duplicates were removed; 545 unique records were screened and 303 formed the candidate evidence pool for critical narrative appraisal. Behavioral and interaction-derived measures are the most established, while eye tracking, kinematic sensing, autonomic monitoring, EEG, and fNIRS provide complementary information on attention, strategy, workload, and engagement. Quantitatively, combined hand- and eye-tracking features distinguished mild cognitive impairment from healthy controls with 93.3% accuracy, 100% sensitivity, and 83.3% specificity, while immersive VR life-skills training produced real-world functional gains of d = 1.00 post-training and d = 1.12 at 1-week follow-up. However, most sensor-derived variables remain digital measures or candidate biomarkers rather than clinically validated biomarkers; physiology-informed closed-loop adaptation is uncommon, and evidence that such adaptation produces sustained ADL or assisted-living benefits is lacking. Progress now depends on standardized reporting, external and multicenter validation, clinically interpretable adaptive models, and objective demonstration of real-world transfer.

papers.title: Agentic EEG Pipeline Synthesis Using Large Language Models and the Model Context Protocol.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography analysis typically requires multistage processing pipelines for which configuration depends on recording characteristics and the intended analytical objective. Although automated pipelines improve reproducibility, they generally implement predefined processing sequences. We present an agentic framework in which a large language model (LLM) orchestrator synthesizes and executes task-specific EEG processing workflows by selecting, parameterizing, and ordering established signal processing components accessed through Model Context Protocol interfaces. Computational EEG processing and analysis operations are performed using established EEGLAB (version 2026.0.0) implementations running in MATLAB (R2026a), while structured execution results and quality control information are returned to the orchestrator to support adaptation during execution. The framework is evaluated by examining tool-layer execution fidelity, independent pipeline synthesis, and the quality of the resulting EEG output relative to the established DISCOVER-EEG workflow. In an evaluation using eight resting state EEG recordings from four participants, mean epoch retention was 0.845 for the agent-generated pipeline and 0.843 for DISCOVER-EEG, while mean spectral entropy was 4.87 and 4.84 bits, respectively. Mean signal-to-noise ratio was 13.92 dB for the agent-generated pipeline and 11.14 dB for DISCOVER-EEG; however, this difference should be interpreted cautiously because the pipelines used different upper filter boundaries. A secondary analysis examined whether EEG processed using the generated pipeline retained features relevant to Alzheimer's disease versus healthy control classification. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of coupling LLM-based orchestration with EEG processing software to generate executable task-specific workflows with structured execution records and provenance. Further evaluation across larger datasets, independent synthesis runs, and additional EEG paradigms is required in order to establish repeatability and generalizability.

papers.title: FPGLNet: A Lightweight Frequency Prior-Gated Network for EEG Emotion Recognition.
papers.abstract: Although deep learning-based electroencephalography (EEG) emotion recognition methods have achieved promising performance, they generally depend on complex network architectures and high computational costs, which limits their deployment in resource-constrained scenarios. Meanwhile, existing approaches mainly focus on local spatiotemporal feature extraction while insufficiently exploiting global frequency-domain dependencies and dynamic information selection during feature propagation, resulting in inadequate spectral information utilization and redundant feature representations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Frequency Prior-Gated Lightweight Network (FPGLNet) for EEG emotion recognition. First, a Mixed Aggregation Convolution (MAC) module is introduced at the input stage to jointly encode EEG spatiotemporal characteristics through temporal and spatial convolutions. Subsequently, a Fused Fourier Convolution Mixer (FFCM) module is developed to model global frequency-domain dependencies through Fourier transform and integrate multi-scale depthwise convolutions for collaborative frequency-spatial feature representation. Furthermore, a Prior-Gated Feed Forward Network (PGFN) is proposed to dynamically generate prior-guided gating weights based on feature responses, enabling adaptive selection and recalibration of discriminative features across different brain regions and temporal segments. This mechanism enhances emotion-related representations while suppressing noise and redundant information. Owing to the lightweight architecture design, FPGLNet achieves an effective balance between feature representation capability, model complexity, and computational efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that FPGLNet achieves classification accuracies of 96.22% and 92.69% on the public SEED-IV and SEED-V datasets, respectively. These results validate the effectiveness of the proposed frequency prior-gated strategy in improving EEG feature representation while maintaining competitive recognition performance and deployment efficiency.

papers.title: MTFNet: A Lightweight Multi-Scale Time-Frequency Neural Network for Multi-Class Event Recognition in DAS-Based Perimeter Security.
papers.abstract: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) has emerged as a pivotal technology for perimeter security. However, existing DAS event recognition methods have inherent limitations. Single-domain modeling has limited feature representation, while conventional multi-domain fusion methods require converting one-dimensional signals into two-dimensional images. This conversion adds computational overhead and may discard part of the original phase and amplitude information. In addition, the robustness of lightweight recognizers under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions remains insufficiently examined. This paper proposes a lightweight multi-scale time-frequency network (MTFNet) for direct processing of one-dimensional DAS signals. The model adopts a parallel time-frequency dual-branch architecture. The time-domain branch utilizes a lightweight 1D Inception-ResNet variant to capture short-term impulse features and long-range temporal dependencies via multi-scale parallel convolutions and residual connections. The frequency-domain branch performs multi-scale segmented spectral analysis to extract complementary discriminative information at diverse time and frequency resolutions, followed by a lightweight attention-free fusion module for effective time-frequency feature fusion. Experimental results on a self-built dataset covering Wind, Facility Noise, Hammering, Sawing, and Walking events show that MTFNet achieves a recognition accuracy of 99.55% with 0.12 M parameters, outperforming SVM, 1D-CNN, TCN, MS 1D-CNN, CNN-BiLSTM, and attention-based multimodal fusion methods. It maintains an accuracy of 94.06% at an SNR of 0 dB, demonstrating its robustness against additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and practical engineering application potential.

papers.title: Multi-Tissue Transcriptomic Profiles of Tarim and Tianshan Red Deer Under Common Conditions.
papers.abstract: We profiled 132 RNA-sequencing libraries representing 11 tissues from six Tarim and six Tianshan adult male red deer maintained under common feeding and management. Tissue identity dominated expression structure among 16,308 expressed genes. Across three differential-expression model specifications, 1253 robust group-associated gene-tissue pairs were identified, involving 1184 genes and concentrated in rumen and rectum. Directional enrichment returned 77 terms meeting both within-set and study-wide false-discovery thresholds. Tianshan-group rumen genes were enriched for cytoskeletal, adhesion, ion-transport and circadian annotations, whereas Tarim-group reticulum genes were enriched for cell-surface and immune-signaling annotations. Cross-tissue recurrence was uncommon and identified a small set of annotated genes and provisional loci for follow-up. Complementary whole-genome principal component analysis (PCA) separated the recorded groups across two genotype-depth filters; weighted Weir-Cockerham FST was 0.341 and 0.325. These results describe tissue-resolved expression patterns and genetic structure in the sampled cohort. Functional, taxonomic and population-wide interpretations require independent validation.

papers.title: Design of a Textile-Integrated Piezoelectric Braided Cord Sensor for Sleep Apnea Monitoring.
papers.abstract: Piezoelectric braided cords composed of poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA) fibers can be integrated into textiles to detect mechanical signals without requiring sensors to be attached directly to the body. In this study, we investigated the potential of a bed-sheet-integrated piezoelectric braided cord sensor for unobtrusive physiological monitoring during sleep, using sleep apnea as an example of its possible applications. Finite element method (FEM) analysis was performed to qualitatively examine the directional characteristics of the piezoelectric response. Guided by these qualitative findings, a bed-sheet sensor with a multi-orientation stitching configuration was developed through iterative prototyping and experimental evaluation. Piezoelectric braided cord signals were recorded from 23 participants during their routine clinical polysomnography (PSG) examinations. The developed sensor enabled the detection of respiration- and pulse-related mechanical signals during sleep. During the initial analysis of data from a small number of these participants, we observed that a pulse-related periodic component remained detectable in the respiratory signal when respiratory motion decreased during apnea. Based on this observation, an apnea-related signal detection algorithm was developed and subsequently applied to the complete dataset of 23 participants. The sensor-based analysis was performed independently of the physicians' PSG-based assessments. For the 18 participants with available physician-based apnea event assessments, the sensor-detected event counts were compared with PSG-based counts within 5-min intervals, without event-by-event temporal matching. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed sensing approach and provide a basis for future clinical investigations.

papers.title: Transformer Models in Vibrational Spectroscopy: A Review.
papers.abstract: Transformer models have attracted increasing interest in vibrational spectroscopy because of their ability to capture long-range dependencies in spectral data. These models have been applied to analytical tasks including spectral preprocessing, classification, quantitative analysis, multimodal data fusion, and spectra-to-structure prediction. Their flexible architectures support applications in Raman, infrared (IR), near-infrared (NIR), and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), with examples across chemistry, biology, and materials science. Transformer-based models also offer opportunities to integrate chemical, physical, and biological information in spectral analysis and support interdisciplinary research involving chemometrics, deep learning, and experimental spectroscopy. In this review, we elucidate the fundamental principles of Transformer models and their wide-ranging applications in vibrational spectroscopy, spanning from baseline correction and deconvolution to molecular identification, disease diagnosis, food authentication, and quantitative property prediction. Finally, as Transformer models may not be suitable for every analytical task or consistently outperform simpler approaches, we discuss current challenges and future trends in Transformer models in vibrational spectroscopy and related analytical sciences.

papers.title: Preliminary Evaluation of Dietary Partially Hydrolyzed Guar Gum on Work Motivation and Quality of Life of Office Workers: An Open-Label, Single-Arm Study.
papers.abstract: Office workers often experience gastrointestinal problems such as constipation, which can reduce labor productivity and quality of life. This study investigated the effects of continuous partially hydrolyzed guar gum (PHGG) intake on the gut microbiome, health status, and labor productivity of Japanese office workers. In this open-label, single-arm trial, 136 employees of Yoshinoya Holdings Co., Ltd. consumed 6 g of PHGG daily for two months. Outcome measures included gut microbiome composition (16S rRNA sequencing), body composition (InBody 380N), gastrointestinal symptoms (Izumo scale), sleep quality (OSA-MA), and labor productivity (WHO-HPQ). PHGG intervention was accompanied by specific genus-level alterations in the gut microbiome characterized by the enrichment of beneficial taxa including Bifidobacterium, Faecalibacterium, and Prevotella, despite no significant overall shift in beta-diversity. Notably, exploratory subgroup analysis indicated shifts in enterotypes from profiles previously associated with disease risks toward those more prevalent in healthy populations. Physiologically, whole-body phase angle, an indirect parameter associated with cellular status and fluid distribution, slightly increased during the study period. Furthermore, favorable changes were observed in absolute presenteeism, gastrointestinal symptoms and subjective sleep quality. Although verification with a more robust study design is necessary, these findings suggest that PHGG may be associated with positive shifts in the well-being and labor productivity of office workers.

papers.title: Pediatric Microbiota: Evidence and Future Perspectives-A Conference Report.
papers.abstract: During early life, the human microbiota contributes to the development of immune, metabolic, and neurological functions. Antibiotic exposure, inflammation, and dietary changes can alter microbial community structure and function, with potential implications for pediatric health. In April 2026, the symposium "Pediatric Microbiota: Evidence and Future" was held in Mexico City, bringing together experts to discuss current advances in pediatric microbiome research. This conference report summarizes the major topics and perspectives presented during the symposium. Several presentations examined how microorganisms and microbial metabolites are transferred from mother to infant. The speakers also discussed the contribution of colostrum immunoglobulins, particularly IgA, to early microbial colonization. Sessions reviewed evidence supporting probiotic use in pediatric gastrointestinal disorders and explored the microbiota-gut-brain axis in autism spectrum disorder and sleep regulation. In addition, speakers discussed the interactions among diet, starch digestion, microbial fermentation, and metabolic health, and their associations with obesity, insulin resistance, and cardiometabolic risk. Important knowledge gaps were identified in pediatric oncology, where evidence remains limited regarding the microbiome's influence on cancer susceptibility, immune responses, treatment outcomes, and therapy-related toxicities. Participants agreed that the field would benefit from longitudinal studies in well-characterized pediatric cohorts, particularly in Latin America, as well as from studies examining biological mechanisms through multi-omics approaches. This research could eventually inform precision nutrition and microbiome-based interventions, but the evidence discussed at the symposium was not considered sufficient to support their routine clinical use.

papers.title: Novel Benzimidazol-2-Acetamide Derivatives as Submicromolar Casein Kinase 1δ Inhibitors with Favourable Predicted Drug-like Properties.
papers.abstract: Background/Objective: Casein kinase 1δ (CK1δ) plays a central role in regulating circadian rhythms, DNA repair, apoptosis, and cell proliferation, and its dysregulation is associated with both cancer and neurodegenerative diseases, making CK1δ an attractive therapeutic target. This study aimed to develop novel CK1δ inhibitors with favourable drug-like properties through the synthesis and biological evaluation of benzimidazol-2-acetamide derivatives. Methods: A novel series of benzimidazol-2-acetamide derivatives was synthesized, incorporating different substituents on the benzimidazole core (5-chloro, 5,6-dichloro, 5-nitro, and 5-cyano) and various saturated cyclic amines on the acetamide moiety. Compounds were evaluated for CK1δ inhibitory activity, while molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate their binding mode. In silico ADME predictions assessed pharmacokinetic properties, and cytotoxicity was evaluated in SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells. Results: The 5,6-dichloro derivatives 20 and 24, bearing piperidin-4-ylmethanamine and morpholine moieties, respectively, displayed the highest CK1δ inhibitory activity (IC50 = 0.172 and 0.223 μM). The 5-cyano analogue 22 also exhibited a good potency (IC50 = 0.224 μM). Computational studies confirmed an ATP-competitive binding mode and highlighted the dynamic behaviour of the solvent-exposed substituents within the CK1δ binding site. Predicted pharmacokinetic properties suggested favourable oral absorption and blood-brain barrier penetration. Compounds 20, 22, and 24 showed no cytotoxicity in SH-SY5Y cells at concentrations up to 10 μM. Conclusions: The new benzimidazol-2-acetamide derivatives exhibited good inhibitor activity against CK1δ, favourable predicted ADME properties, and low cellular toxicity. The combined experimental and computational findings provide valuable insights for the further optimization of this scaffold toward the development of therapeutics for CK1δ-related diseases.

papers.title: Interventional Effects and Neurometabolic Regulation of a Panax quinquefolius-Containing Herbal Extract (JYF) in Diazepam Withdrawal Syndrome in Mice.
papers.abstract: Background: Long-term benzodiazepine use can lead to dependence and clinically significant withdrawal following discontinuation, highlighting the need to identify effective interventions for withdrawal-associated abnormalities. Methods: High-resolution mass spectrometry was used to characterize the constituents of a Panax quinquefolius-containing herbal extract (JYF) and evaluate their in vivo exposure in rats. Sixty-five C57BL/6 mice were randomly assigned to control, model, and low-, medium-, and high-dose JYF groups. Diazepam withdrawal was induced after 28 days of subcutaneous diazepam administration (12 mg/kg), and JYF was administered orally during the peri-withdrawal period for 7 days, beginning 4 days before diazepam discontinuation. Behavioral assessments, electroencephalographic/electromyographic (EEG/EMG) recordings, histopathological analysis, and neurochemical measurements were performed. Network proximity analysis, widely targeted metabolomics, targeted neurotransmitter quantification, and integrated pathway analysis were subsequently performed. Results: A total of 61 constituents were identified in JYF, of which 44 were detected in serum and 34 in brain tissue. Network proximity analysis highlighted genistein, columbamine, jatrorrhizine, and berberine as candidate constituents associated with withdrawal, anxiety/depression and sleep-related modules. JYF attenuated diazepam withdrawal-associated weight loss, anxiety-like behavior, sleep fragmentation, abnormal EEG activity, and elevations in corticosterone and orexin A. Metabolomic analyses revealed disturbances in lipid, energy, and amino acid metabolism, with tryptophan and phenylalanine metabolism emerging as prominent pathways associated with JYF intervention. Diazepam withdrawal also disrupted cerebral monoamine homeostasis, as reflected by increased serotonin and norepinephrine and decreased dopamine levels; these alterations generally shifted toward control levels after JYF intervention. Conclusions: JYF alleviates behavioral and sleep-related abnormalities associated with diazepam withdrawal. Its effects may be associated with alterations in brain metabolic homeostasis, including tryptophan- and phenylalanine-related metabolism and monoaminergic neurotransmission. Genistein and berberine were identified as candidate active constituents that warrant further experimental validation.

papers.title: Indirect Skin Homeostasis Modulation by an Essential Oil Blend in Mice with Insomnia Comorbid Anxiety: Sensitivity of Dermal Fibroblasts to Exogenously Applied Circulating Molecules.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Studies have confirmed that essential oils extracted from aromatic plants exert mood-regulating and skin-beneficial effects. Although the concept of "emotional skincare" has attracted growing research interest, experimental evidence supporting the indirect skin-protective effects of essential oils through emotional regulation remains limited. This study investigates the indirect effect of an essential oil blend (EOB) on skin homeostasis in mice with insomnia comorbid anxiety (ICA, a pharmacologically validated emotional stress model induced by para-chlorophenylalanine) and aims to profile the sensitivity of dermal fibroblasts to candidate circulating molecules identified from EOB-treated ICA mice, thereby laying a mechanistic foundation for emotional skincare research. Methods: An essential oil blend (EOB) comprising lavender, Kushui rose, sweet orange, Roman chamomile, sandalwood, and clary sage essential oils was prepared. An ICA mouse model was established using para-chlorophenylalanine. Behavioral phenotypes, as well as neurotransmitter and hormonal indices, were measured to validate the anxiolytic and sleep disturbance-alleviating effects of EOB administered via intraperitoneal injection at 300 mg/kg per injection (two injections overall). Skin histological alterations and circulating biomarker profiles were evaluated, and selected differentially altered circulating molecules were exogenously applied to cultured dermal fibroblasts in vitro to assess their effects on fibroblast functions. Results: EOB significantly alleviated ICA-like behaviors and ameliorated abnormal levels of brain neurotransmitters and hormones in mice. Although only mild histological variations were observed in the skin after EOB intervention, significant alterations in cortisol, melatonin, 5-hydroxytryptamine, interleukin-10, and type I collagen were detected in serum or skin tissues. Exogenous application of these circulating molecules elicited differential responses in dermal fibroblasts, affecting oxidative stress, inflammatory responses, and extracellular matrix synthesis in a molecule-specific manner. Notably, these fibroblast assays only demonstrate cellular sensitivity in vitro and do not prove that these circulating molecules directly mediate the in vivo effects observed in mice. Conclusions: EOB intervention ameliorates insomnia- and anxiety-related behaviors and concurrent favorable changes in skin-associated molecular profiles in ICA mice. These changes are accompanied by alterations in circulating bioactive molecules to which dermal fibroblasts exhibit measurable sensitivity in vitro. These observations are consistent with, but do not definitively establish, a brain-skin axis-mediated mechanism. These findings provide preliminary experimental evidence for the emotional skincare concept and identify candidate circulating molecules for future causal validation; the in vivo regulatory roles of these molecules and the precise signaling pathways involved remain to be established in dedicated mechanistic studies.

papers.title: Cold Tolerance in Alfalfa: Physiological Mechanisms, Regulatory Networks, and Molecular Breeding Prospects.
papers.abstract: Alfalfa (Medicago sativa L.) is a perennial legume forage whose winter survival determines stand persistence, spring green-up, and long-term yield in cold regions. Low-temperature stress causes membrane phase transitions, cellular dehydration, impaired photosynthetic electron transport, and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation. Tolerance depends on coordinated antioxidant protection, osmotic adjustment, membrane stabilization, photosynthetic maintenance, and carbon-nitrogen allocation to the root crown. At the molecular level, this process is mediated by calcium ion signaling, phytohormone pathways, and the cold-responsive ICE-CBF/DREB-COR regulatory cascade. Reported molecular resources include calmodulin-like protein modules (MsCML10 and MsCML50), CBF/DREB factors, autophagy and circadian regulators, sugar-metabolism genes, and genes from yellow-flowered alfalfa. This review integrates low-temperature injury, physiological responses, molecular regulatory networks, evaluation methods, genetic resources, and breeding progress. It emphasizes that evidence strength differs among cultivated-alfalfa functional studies, heterologous validation, and omics-based candidate discovery. Major gaps include inconsistent phenotyping, insufficient root-crown and overwintering-bud characterization, limited validation under natural overwintering, and weak translation of candidate genes into breeding populations. Future research should combine standardized multi-environment phenotyping with multi-omics, functional validation in alfalfa, marker development, genomic selection, and multi-trait improvement of cold tolerance, yield, forage quality, and stress adaptation.

papers.title: Ketones and Sleep: A Narrative Review of Mechanisms, Preclinical Models, and Human Evidence.
papers.abstract: Sleep is a metabolically dynamic state, and ketone bodies may interact with sleep physiology as both oxidative substrates and signaling metabolites. β-Hydroxybutyrate (BHB), acetoacetate (AcAc), and acetone rise during fasting, carbohydrate restriction, ketogenic diets used for therapeutic or non-therapeutic purposes, prolonged exercise, selected pathological states of insulin deficiency, and after consumption of exogenous ketones. This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic, preclinical, and human evidence linking endogenously generated ketosis and ketosis generated from exogenous ketone consumption to sleep architecture, sleep quality, sleep-disordered breathing, and sleep-relevant metabolic pathways. We reviewed studies involving ketogenic diets, fasting or caloric restriction, and consumption of exogenous ketones, prioritizing investigations with polysomnography, electroencephalography (EEG), sleep architecture, respiratory, or validated sleep-questionnaire outcomes, while also considering mechanistic studies of neuronal excitability, inflammation, epigenetic regulation, circadian timing, and brain energetics. The most direct preclinical evidence indicates that AcAc, but not BHB, increases slow-wave activity (delta power 0.5-4 Hz) during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep and suppresses glutamate release in mice, supporting a potential role for ketone metabolism in sleep homeostasis. Dietary, fasting, and aging models further suggest that lipid/ketone metabolism can alter NREM/rapid eye movement (REM) balance, circadian metabolic rhythms, and sleep-wake responses to energetic stress, with aged-rat data showing sex-specific REM and cognitive effects of ketogenic interventions. Human studies are suggestive but heterogeneous: acute carbohydrate restriction can increase slow-wave sleep and reduce REM sleep in healthy adults; ketogenic therapies may improve subjective sleep in selected neurological and metabolic populations; and ketone ester ingestion can improve sleep efficiency after strenuous evening exercise, but not during hypoxia-induced sleep disruption. Ketones are sleep-relevant metabolic signals, but their effects are conditional rather than universally sleep-promoting. They may also indirectly affect sleep by enhancing wakefulness quality. The ketone concentration range associated with optimal sleep outcomes remains undefined, and potential dose-, timing-, and context-dependent effects on sleep require further study.
