Conclusions: The available evidence does not consistently establish that OT interventions improve occupational performance or reduce physical and cognitive fatigue in adults with MS. Larger, adequately powered RCTs using clearly defined OT interventions, standardized outcomes, and longer follow-up periods are required.

papers.title: Beyond the Apnoea-Hypopnoea Index: Towards Personalised Care of Patients with Suspected Obstructive Sleep Apnoea Through Clinical Phenotyping and Physiological Stratification.
papers.abstract: The apnoea-hypopnoea index (AHI) remains central to the diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), but it incompletely captures both clinical heterogeneity and the physiological burden of respiratory events. We propose a phenotype-guided framework with a common initial clinical assessment followed by two complementary pathways according to the patient's predominant clinical need: a symptom-oriented pathway based on pre-test clinical phenotyping, and a cardiovascular risk-oriented pathway in which directly measured hypoxic burden (HB), complemented by the respiratory event-related pulse-rate response, may eventually support physiological stratification. In our single-centre cohort of 5385 referrals, three predominantly symptomatic phenotypes accounted for 56.5% of patients and two paucisymptomatic phenotypes (A and E) for 43.5%; these groups had overlapping AHI distributions but different clinical profiles and needs. The reported AUC of 0.87-0.95 reflects supervised reproduction of internally derived cluster labels, not prediction of clinical outcomes or CPAP benefit. HB and pulse-rate response remain candidate physiological markers: evidence for treatment-effect modification derives from post hoc analyses and does not establish validated treatment-allocation criteria. Pre-test phenotyping is sufficiently developed to justify prospective, external, multicentre validation, whereas physiological integration requires methodological standardisation and prospective evaluation before individual treatment decisions can be guided by these markers.

papers.title: Persistent Post-Concussion Syndrome After Its Withdrawal from DSM-5 and ICD-11: Definitional Disagreement and the Neurocognitive Gap.
papers.abstract: A substantial minority of patients do not recover fully after mild traumatic brain injury. Persistent post-concussion syndrome includes both cognitive and non-cognitive manifestations, yet DSM-5 and ICD-11 withdrew the syndrome as a distinct diagnosis and reorganized its persistent sequelae exclusively within neurocognitive categories. While this reorganization addresses the cognitive component of the syndrome, it provides no single category for its non-cognitive consequences, including vestibular, oculomotor, headache-related, autonomic, sleep, and pain-related manifestations. In some patients, these may be the most disabling consequences of the injury. This narrative review examines the resulting diagnostic gap and other continuing disagreements. Published criteria differ in symptom count, duration, and other requirements, yielding an unacceptably wide range of prevalence estimates, from 11.4% to 38.7%. We review the current status of this syndrome and propose an approach that separates diagnosis from attribution. Finally, we discuss the interactions between cognitive and non-cognitive consequences through shared neural substrates, so abnormalities in one domain may influence function in another. Because cognitive and non-cognitive manifestations may dissociate, a patient may have normal or minimal findings in one domain and functionally significant abnormalities in the other; therefore, evaluation confined to one domain alone (as reflected in the new classifications) cannot exclude the syndrome.

papers.title: Six-Month Trajectories of Symptoms, Perceived Recovery, and Functional Health in Ecuadorian Adults with COVID-19.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Most longitudinal evidence on post-acute COVID-19 comes from hospitalized patients in high-income countries and less is known about community samples in low- and middle-income settings. This study examined changes in perceived recovery, symptom burden, general health perception, and functional difficulties over six months in Ecuadorian adults with confirmed COVID-19. Methods: In a prospective observational cohort in Quito, Ecuador, 120 adults with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 were assessed at baseline (within four weeks of diagnosis) and again three and six months after the baseline assessment; 91 completed all three assessments. The Spanish-language ISARIC follow-up survey covered 39 symptoms, perceived recovery, the EQ-5D-5L and EQ-VAS, and six Washington Group functioning items rated retrospectively for the pre-COVID period and currently. Analyses were exploratory and descriptive, and all p-values are nominal and unadjusted for multiple comparisons. Results: Participants' perceived complete recovery improved (χ2 = 15.24, p < 0.001), as did perceived general health (F(2, 178) = 5.80, p = 0.004). Chest pain, palpitations, muscle weakness, confusion, tinnitus, and diarrhea declined over follow-up. At six months, 37.4% still reported headaches, 35.2% fatigue, 35.2% confusion or inattention, and 25.3% sleep disturbance. Among EQ-5D-5L domains, only pain/discomfort improved (p = 0.012). Vision, walking, memory, and communication declined from pre-COVID to baseline and improved between baseline and six months; pre-COVID and six-month levels were not compared directly. Conclusions: Recovery over six months was gradual but incomplete, with a substantial minority reporting ongoing or recurrent symptoms at six months. These findings describe post-acute symptom burden following confirmed COVID-19 rather than formally diagnosed post-COVID-19 condition.

papers.title: Depressive Symptoms, Sleep Quality, and Anhedonia in Patients with Primary Biliary Cholangitis: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background and aim: This study assessed depressive symptoms, sleep quality, and anhedonia in patients with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), compared them with healthy controls (HCs), and explored their associations with UDCA treatment response, established prognostic scores, and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) in patients with PBC. Methods: In this single-center cross-sectional study, 103 patients with PBC and 50 HCs were evaluated using three validated patient-reported outcome (PRO) instruments: the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Snaith-Hamilton Pleasure Scale (SHAPS). PRO measures were compared between patients with PBC and HCs, and associations between PROs and UDCA treatment response, prognostic scores, and LSM were explored in the PBC group. Results: Moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms, poor sleep quality, and anhedonia were observed in 45%, 62%, and 36% of patients with PBC, respectively, compared with 18%, 38%, and 18% of HCs. The age- and sex-adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for PBCvs. HC were 3.889 (95% CI 1.695-8.926), 3.442 (95% CI 1.636-7.238), and 2.678 (95% CI 1.158-6.193), respectively. Younger age was independently associated with poor sleep quality (OR per year 0.946, 95% CI 0.898-0.997; p = 0.039). No statistically significant associations were identified between PROs and UDCA response, prognostic scores, and LSM in patients with PBC. Conclusions: Patients with PBC reported a substantial and interrelated burden of depressive symptoms, poor sleep quality, and anhedonia compared with HCs.

papers.title: Depressive Symptoms in Adults with Obesity and Their Associations with Sociodemographic, Health and Lifestyle Factors: A Secondary Analysis of a Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Research indicates a bidirectional association between obesity and depression. The co-occurrence of both disorders has serious clinical implications. The aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of self-reported depressive symptoms (DS) in a group of men and women with obesity and to identify the health factors, sociodemographic factors and lifestyle elements associated with the severity of DS among these persons. Methods: The participants in the study were a group of 3742 persons aged 42-65 years with a BMI ≥ 30.0 kg/m2. A multivariate negative binomial regression analysis was performed in order to determine the expected number of DS. Results: Almost 28% of the participants with obesity showed at least four DS. The factors with the strongest associations with the number of DS were experiencing stressful events over the past year (IRR = 1.28, 95% CI: 1.23-1.33, p < 0.001), gender (IRR = 0.82, 95% CI: 0.79-0.85, p < 0.001) and multimorbidity (IRR = 1.10, 95% CI: 1.06-1.14, p < 0.001). The prevalence of DS was also associated with some socioeconomic factors (place of residence, education and marital status) and lifestyle factors (smoking, TV-viewing time, sleep duration and regular participation in organised groups or associations). Conclusions: Further longitudinal and intervention studies are necessary in order to better understand the factors related to the prevalence of DS in persons with obesity.

papers.title: Patent Foramen Ovale Closure Alleviates Long-Term Drug-Refractory Epilepsy: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Background: Drug-refractory epilepsy (DRE) poses a persistent clinical burden, and the identification of reversible extracranial contributing factors represents a promising strategy to improve seizure control. Patent foramen ovale (PFO) with right-to-left shunt (RLS) has been recognized as a potential modifiable driver of epileptic seizures, yet clinical data on patients with extremely long-standing DRE exceeding 40 years remain exceedingly scarce. Methods: We report a 46-year-old female patient with a 44-year history of DRE, who experienced daily secondarily generalized tonic-clonic seizures (GTCSs) despite sequential treatment with six mechanistically distinct antiseizure medications. Systematic workup was performed and the patient underwent percutaneous transcatheter PFO closure, with a follow-up period of 14 months. Results: Systematic workup confirmed severe PFO-related RLS (grade III by contrast transthoracic echocardiography, grade IV by contrast transcranial Doppler), while brain MRI revealed no definite structural epileptogenic lesions other than an old ischemic infarct in the right corona radiata. At the latest follow-up, the patient had achieved complete freedom from GTCS with a markedly reduced antiseizure medication burden, retaining only infrequent mild focal absence-like seizures. Follow-up video electroencephalography unmasked previously occult focal epileptiform discharges in the left temporal region. Conclusions: This case suggests that severe PFO-related RLS may serve as a reversible aggravating factor even in decades-long refractory epilepsy, and provides electroclinical evidence supporting a hypothetical two-hit model of seizure generalization. PFO screening may be considered in selected patients with cryptogenic drug-refractory epilepsy, particularly those with non-lesional MRI, non-localizing EEG, and morning-predominant seizures.

papers.title: Responses of Processed Electroencephalographic Indices to Ascending and Descending Simulated Remimazolam Effect-Site Concentrations: A Prospective Exploratory Interventional Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Temporal characteristics of concentration-response loops for processed electroencephalographic indices during changes in remimazolam effect-site concentration (Ce) remain unclear. Therefore, this prospective, exploratory interventional study aims to compare the magnitude of concentration-response loops between the ascending and descending phases of simulated remimazolam Ce for the bispectral index (BIS) and patient state index (PSI). Methods: Twenty patients were administered remimazolam at a constant infusion rate of 3.5 mg/kg/h for 5.5 min, followed by infusion discontinuation. BIS and PSI values were continuously recorded from initiation of remimazolam infusion until 16 min, and remimazolam Ce was simulated using the Schüttler-Eisenried pharmacokinetic model. The area between the ascending and descending concentration-response curves (ABC) was calculated for each index within the overlapping Ce range. ABC was compared between BIS and PSI using a paired analysis, and a patient-level bootstrap was used to estimate the 95% confidence interval (CI) for the paired difference. Results: All 20 patients were included in the final analysis. The mean paired difference in ABC (BIS - PSI) was -6.254 (95% CI: -7.945 to -4.563), with a bootstrap median difference of -6.241 (95% CI: -8.752 to -4.133). The gap between the ascending and descending concentration-response curves was greater for PSI than for BIS. Conclusions: BIS and PSI showed different concentration-response patterns during changes in simulated remimazolam Ce, with PSI showing greater separation between the ascending and descending phases. These exploratory findings do not establish direct pharmacodynamic hysteresis or indicate superiority of BIS for assessing hypnotic state.

papers.title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Pulmonary Embolism: Prevalence, Severity and the Association of Sleep-Disordered Breathing with Thromboembolic Disease.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and pulmonary embolism (PE) share several risk factors, while emerging evidence suggests a potential pathophysiological link beyond these common determinants. We aimed to characterize the prevalence and severity of OSA in patients with acute PE and to investigate whether the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) is independently associated with PE and its clinical course. Methods: In this prospective, single-center, case-control study, 128 consecutive patients with acute PE and 252 outpatient controls with other respiratory diseases underwent home respiratory polygraphy. In patients with PE, the sleep study was performed at least three months after the acute event. OSA was diagnosed and graded according to international consensus criteria. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations between AHI and PE, acute PE severity, chronic deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and venous thromboembolism (VTE) recurrence. Results: OSA was present in 55.5% of patients with PE, with severe OSA in 28.9%, compared with 42.1% and 13.9%, respectively, among controls (p = 0.013 and p = 0.001). Patients with PE had a higher AHI (21.21 ± 19.29 vs. 14.81 ± 14.26 events/h; p = 0.007) and oxygen desaturation index (19.86 ± 18.77 vs. 13.30 ± 13.79; p = 0.003). Each 10-events/h increase in AHI was independently associated with PE after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, and established VTE risk factors (OR 1.205, 95% CI 1.019-1.426; p = 0.029). AHI was not independently associated with intermediate-high/high-risk PE or chronic DVT. Among patients who discontinued anticoagulation, VTE recurrence was higher in those with OSA (36.0% vs. 13.3%; p = 0.049). Conclusions: OSA is highly prevalent and frequently severe in patients with acute PE. Increasing AHI is independently associated with the presence of PE, supporting a clinically relevant association between sleep-disordered breathing and thromboembolic disease. Because OSA was not systematically reassessed after documented resolution of PE, persistence of OSA independently of residual thromboembolic disease cannot be definitively established. Whether the observed association between OSA and recurrent VTE after anticoagulation withdrawal is confirmed in larger prospective studies remains to be determined.

papers.title: The Influence of Neurotic Disorders and Neurobiological Basis on Eating Behavior in a 21-Year-Old Patient: A Case Study-Diagnostic Difficulties: Is It PANDAS/PANS in Relation to an Elevated ASO Level and the Diagnosis of OCD?
papers.abstract: Background: Anxiety and obsessive-compulsive disorders can co-occur with disordered eating behaviors and difficulties in emotional regulation. This article presents the clinical case of a 21-year-old female student whose complex neuropsychiatric profile required the simultaneous consideration of psychological, psychosocial, and somatic factors. The aim of this case report was to examine the coexistence of psychopathological symptoms, eating disturbances, psychosocial experiences, and somatic findings, while considering the potential role of post-infectious factors. Methods: A retrospective analysis of the patient's medical and psychiatric history was conducted, including childhood infections, psychiatric diagnoses, psychosocial experiences, eating behaviors, and available laboratory findings. The assessment also included quantitative electroencephalography (QEEG) brain mapping performed under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. Particular attention was given to the retrospective hypothesis of PANDAS/PANS (Pediatric Autoimmune Neuropsychiatric Disorders Associated with Streptococcal Infections/Pediatric Acute-onset Neuropsychiatric Syndrome), while distinguishing documented clinical findings from unconfirmed etiopathogenetic hypotheses. Results: Retrospective history revealed recurrent upper respiratory tract infections and bilateral pneumonia in early childhood, followed by increasing anxiety and social withdrawal from peers. The patient was diagnosed with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) at the age of 13, while psychiatric records from 2023 also documented depressive disorders and social phobia. Within the family system, the patient experienced relational trauma, including systematic verbal and psychological abuse by her father. Blood tests performed on 11 June 2025 revealed an elevated antistreptolysin O (ASO) level of 436 IU/mL, which may indicate previous streptococcal exposure but does not confirm active infection, PANDAS/PANS, or a causal relationship with neuropsychiatric symptoms. The available documentation lacked microbiological confirmation of streptococcal infections or evidence substantiating a PANDAS/PANS diagnosis. QEEG brain mapping revealed elevated fast HiBeta activity in the frontal regions under both recording conditions; however, incomplete methodological documentation precluded definitive interpretation of this finding as evidence of persistent cortical overactivity or specific cognitive deficits. Somatic and metabolic findings included morning cortisol of 7.7 µg/dL, dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-SO4) of 163 µg/dL, prolactin of 513.0 mIU/L, and total cholesterol of 138 mg/dL. A previously recorded glycemic value of 45 mg/dL was also noted, although insufficient information was available to confirm reactive hypoglycemia. The patient reported a dichotomous eating pattern characterized by appetite suppression during acute stress, followed by episodes of increased food intake aimed at regulating emotional tension. However, the absence of standardized assessment prevented confirmation of formal binge-eating episodes. Food avoidance and restriction were associated with contamination fears and obsessive-compulsive rituals. The patient also expressed marked body image dissatisfaction and a desire for an extremely thin physique, although no formal diagnosis of body dysmorphic disorder was documented. Conclusions: This case highlights the complex coexistence of obsessive-compulsive and anxiety symptoms, disordered eating behaviors, psychosocial trauma, and somatic findings. Although retrospective clinical history and elevated ASO levels raise the possibility of a post-infectious contribution, the available evidence does not establish an autoimmune mechanism or confirm PANDAS/PANS. The findings emphasize the importance of distinguishing documented clinical observations from etiopathogenetic hypotheses and support an interdisciplinary approach integrating psychiatric care, psychotherapy, nutritional assessment, and appropriate somatic diagnostics.

papers.title: Advancing Sleep Testing for Children: In-Laboratory Validation of a Type 2 Sleep-Monitoring System Designed for Home-Based Pediatric Assessment.
papers.abstract: Comprehensive Type 2 sleep-monitoring systems designed to support home-based assessment may improve access to pediatric sleep assessment while preserving evaluation of sleep architecture and respiratory events. This study evaluated the clinical performance of a wearable Type 2 sleep monitoring system compared with standard in-laboratory polysomnography in children. Children referred for overnight sleep evaluation underwent simultaneous recordings using the Dormotech wearable Type 2 system and in-laboratory polysomnography (Nox A1). Recordings were manually scored according to American Academy of Sleep Medicine guidelines. Primary outcomes were apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) and severity classification; secondary outcomes included global sleep-wake and respiratory parameters, usability, and safety. Twenty-four children completed supervised in-laboratory recordings and were included in the analysis (median age, 10.5 years; 25th-3.6) events/h with polysomnography (p = 0.808). AHI severity classification showed high agreement (κ = 0.896), with a med75th percentiles, 8.8-13.3; 50.0% female). Median AHI was 2.2 (25th-75th percentiles, 0.9-3.4) events/h with Dormotech and 1.3 (0.6-3.6) events/h with polysomnography (p = 0.808). AHI severity classification showed high agreement (κ = 0.896), with a median Bland-Altman paired difference (Nox - Dormotech) of -0.2 events/h and empirical 95% limits of agreement of -1.9 to 6.7 events/h. No significant differences were observed across secondary sleep or respiratory parameters. User experience was favorable, with no device-related adverse events. The comprehensive Type 2 system demonstrated strong agreement with in-laboratory polysomnography across respiratory and global sleep-wake measures in children. These findings demonstrate agreement under supervised laboratory conditions and provide a foundation for future studies evaluating the system's performance in unsupervised use settings.

papers.title: Sleep Habits and Maternal Anxiety in Children with Growing Pains: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Growing pains commonly present as recurrent evening or nocturnal musculoskeletal pain in childhood. Evidence on associated sleep disturbance and maternal anxiety is limited. We compared affected children with healthy controls and examined sleep-related factors. Methods: A total of 138 children aged 4-12 years were included in this single-center study, comprising 71 children with growing pains and 67 age- and sex-comparable healthy controls. Growing pains were diagnosed using the Peterson criteria. Pain severity was assessed using age-appropriate self-report instruments, while sleep habits and maternal anxiety were evaluated with the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), respectively. Multivariable regression identified factors associated with CSHQ total scores. Results: Children with growing pains had higher CSHQ total scores than healthy controls [49.0 (33.0-81.0) vs. 42.0 (31.0-79.0), p < 0.001], and scores above the screening cut-off were more frequent (76.1% vs. 52.2%, p = 0.003). Maternal GAD-7 scores did not differ between groups (p = 0.531). After multivariable adjustment, growing pains (p = 0.020) and higher maternal GAD-7 scores (p = 0.003) were independently associated with higher CSHQ scores in the overall sample. Among children with growing pains, greater pain severity was independently associated with higher CSHQ scores (p = 0.033), whereas maternal GAD-7 score was not. Conclusions: Children with growing pains had greater sleep disturbance than healthy controls after multivariable adjustment. Higher maternal GAD-7 scores were associated with sleep disturbance overall, but not within the growing-pains group. Greater pain severity was independently associated with sleep disturbance in affected children. These findings support sleep assessment in this population.

papers.title: Post-Pandemic Trends of 24-Hour Movement Behaviours and Mental Health Outcomes in Youth.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted youth movement behaviours and mental health, but evidence on post-pandemic trends remains limited. Therefore, this study examined differences in compliance with the 24-h movement behaviour guidelines and their association with mental health outcomes among Portuguese children and adolescents between 2022 and 2024. Methods: This repeated cross-sectional study included two independent samples of Portuguese children and adolescents from the 2022 and 2024 waves of the Health Behaviour in School-aged Children study (2022: n = 2775; 2024: n = 2381). The 24-h movement behaviours (physical activity, sleep and screen time) and mental health outcomes, assessed by Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21), were self-reported. Prevalences of attaining the 24-h movement guidelines and DASS-21 categories were calculated and compared between 2022 and 2024 using chi-square tests. Adjusted logistic regression models were used to examine the associations between movement behaviour compliance and mental health outcomes. Results: From 2022 to 2024, the proportion meeting physical activity (7.5% to 13.7%; p < 0.001) and screen-time (12.8% to 28.2%; p < 0.001) guidelines increased, while adherence to sleep recommendations did not differ significantly (42.4% to 41.2%; p = 0.365). The proportion meeting two or more guidelines was also higher in 2024 (9.5% to 20.1%; p < 0.001). The prevalence of mild-to-extremely severe symptoms was lower in 2024 than in 2022 for depression (34.2% to 43.9%; p < 0.001), anxiety (38.1% to 43.2%; p = 0.001) and stress (23.6% to 31.0%; p < 0.001). Meeting screen-time and sleep guidelines was associated with at least 31% lower odds of having depressive, anxiety and stress symptoms (p < 0.001). Conclusions: More favourable prevalence estimates for movement behaviours and mental health outcomes were observed in 2024 than in 2022. Compliance with screen-time and sleep guidelines was associated with lower odds of depressive, anxiety and stress symptoms.

papers.title: Early Serum S100B and Neurophysiological and Structural Brain Abnormalities in a Prospective Cohort of Preterm Infants.
papers.abstract: Background: Early identification of brain dysfunction in preterm infants remains challenging because cranial ultrasonography (CUS) may not capture early neurophysiological abnormalities. Serum S100B has been proposed as a marker of neonatal brain injury, but its relationship with electroencephalographic (EEG) abnormalities in preterm infants remains unclear. Objectives: Our objectives were to evaluate the association between early neonatal serum S100B concentrations and EEG abnormality severity in preterm infants and to determine whether similar associations are observed with structural brain injury detected by CUS. Methods: This prospective observational cohort included 116 preterm infants from 281 prospectively enrolled neonates. Serum S100B was measured within the first 24 h of life. Conventional multichannel EEG was performed at 10-14 days of life, and CUS was performed serially to assess intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) and periventricular leukomalacia (PVL). Associations with EEG severity were evaluated using correlation analysis and ordinal logistic regression. A sensitivity analysis was restricted to infants with a postmenstrual age (PMA) ≤ 36 weeks at EEG and used a preterm-specific EEG grading system. Results: Higher log10(S100B) concentrations were associated with greater EEG abnormality severity (Spearman's ρ = 0.49, p < 0.001) and remained independently associated after adjustment for gestational age and Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) (adjusted OR 19.95, 95% CI 4.97-80.16; p < 0.001). No significant associations were observed between S100B concentrations and IVH or PVL severity. In the PMA-restricted sensitivity analysis (n = 89), the association between S100B and EEG abnormality severity remained significant using the preterm-specific grading system (ρ = 0.54, p < 0.001). Conclusions: During the early neonatal period, higher serum S100B concentrations were associated with greater neurophysiological abnormality severity in preterm infants, whereas associations with ultrasound-defined IVH or PVL were not demonstrated. The persistence of the S100B-EEG association in the PMA-specific sensitivity analysis supports the robustness of this finding across EEG grading approaches.

papers.title: The Smartphone-Not So 'Smart' for Teenagers' Health.
papers.abstract: Smartphones have become indispensable tools for communication, entertainment, and information access among children and adolescents. Excessive smartphone use may interfere with daily activities and contribute to problematic smartphone use. This study aimed to investigate age-related differences in smartphone use patterns and their impact on health among children and adolescents. A cross-sectional, online questionnaire-based study was conducted between March and May 2021 among 415 smartphone users aged 7-18 years. Participants were divided into two age groups (group 1: 7-12 and group 2: 13-18 years). Sociodemographic characteristics, smartphone use patterns, lifestyle factors, and health-related outcomes were assessed. Statistical analyses were performed in R version 4.3.3. In group 1, daily smartphone use was mostly 1-3 h (40.35%), whereas in adolescents it was 3-5 h (40.85%). Female adolescents spent significantly more time using smartphones than males (p < 0.0001), whereas boys had higher odds of using their smartphone for gaming than girls (aOR = 3.55, 95% CI 1.83-7.09). Approximately two-thirds of adolescents in both age groups reported excessive daily smartphone use and perceived themselves as "addicted". Ocular complaints were among the most frequently reported somatic symptoms, particularly among adolescents. Prolonged smartphone use was significantly associated with disturbing dreams OR = 1.89, 95% CI (1.30-2.81) and insufficient sleep OR = 1.60, 95% CI (1.11-2.34) in adolescents; smartphone use before bedtime was significantly associated with daytime sleepiness in both groups (group 1 p = 0.041, group 2 p = 0.040). Anxiety-related symptoms were reported by nearly all participants, while emotional symptoms/experiences suggesting eventual depression appeared more prevalent among younger children. Excessive smartphone use is highly prevalent among children and adolescents and is associated with sleep disturbances, somatic symptoms, and psychological complaints, highlighting the need for targeted preventive interventions.

papers.title: Language and Cognitive Performance in Children with Well-Controlled Asthma: Associations with Serum pNF-H and Neurogranin.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Childhood asthma is increasingly viewed as a systemic condition that may also affect neurodevelopmental processes. We examined language and cognitive performance and their associations with serum biomarkers of neuroinflammation, neuroaxonal integrity and synaptic function in school-aged children with clinically well-controlled asthma. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 67 children (33 with asthma and 34 healthy controls) underwent the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children-Revised (WISC-R), the Turkish Nonword Repetition Test (TAST), the Turkish School-Age Language Development Test (TODİL), sleep and psychosocial scales, and audiometric screening. Serum interleukin-4 (IL-4), IL-13, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 13 (CXCL13), brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), nerve growth factor (NGF), chitinase-3-like protein-1 (YKL-40/CHI3L1), triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2), monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), synaptosomal-associated protein 25 (SNAP-25), neurogranin, and phosphorylated neurofilament heavy chain (pNF-H) were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Groups were compared with Mann-Whitney U and chi-square/Fisher tests and with age- and sex-adjusted regression using HC3 robust standard errors, with Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction within predefined outcome families; within the asthma group, biomarkers were related to language and cognitive outcomes in exploratory multiple regression. Results: Serum pNF-H was higher in the asthma group (p = 0.001; pFDR = 0.012), remained higher after age and sex adjustment (p = 0.002), and was robust to outlier handling. Neurogranin was higher in the unadjusted comparison (p = 0.012), marginal after panel-level FDR (pFDR = 0.065), and significant after adjustment (p = 0.003). Several WISC-R indices, most clearly full-scale IQ, were lower in the asthma group, favoring controls. Within the asthma group, neurogranin was positively associated with WISC-R vocabulary and picture completion and TODIL organizing. Conclusions: Even in well-controlled asthma, specific language and cognitive domains may differ from those of healthy peers, alongside higher peripheral biomarkers related to neuroaxonal and synaptic processes. These findings are exploratory and require confirmation in larger, longitudinal samples.

papers.title: Beyond the Skin: An Integrated Biopsychosocial Framework for Childhood Atopic Dermatitis.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a common chronic inflammatory skin disease in childhood characterized by pruritus, skin barrier dysfunction, and a relapsing-remitting course. Beyond its cutaneous manifestations, AD may substantially affect the psychosocial well-being of children and their families. To synthesize current evidence on the psychosocial burden of pediatric AD and integrate biopsychosocial and burden-of-disease frameworks into a clinically oriented approach, with particular relevance to pediatric allergy practice. A narrative review of literature published from January 2013 through May 2026 was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science. Evidence addressing health-related quality of life, sleep disturbance, emotional and behavioral outcomes, social functioning, treatment-related burden, and caregiver and family burden was synthesized narratively, prioritizing pediatric populations. Pediatric AD is associated with multidimensional burden involving health-related quality of life, sleep, emotional well-being, social functioning, and family life. Physician-assessed disease severity and patient- or family-perceived burden show imperfect correspondence, supporting the complementary use of patient- and caregiver-reported outcomes. Nocturnal pruritus and sleep disruption may contribute to bidirectional interactions among skin symptoms, emotional distress, and family burden. Visible lesions may contribute to stigma and social difficulties, while caregivers may experience sleep loss, stress, treatment burden, and concerns regarding topical corticosteroid use. Current guidance increasingly supports assessment of patient- and family-reported burden alongside objective disease severity. Integrating biopsychosocial and burden-of-disease perspectives may support a more comprehensive approach to pediatric AD. Routine care should include discussion of sleep, emotional well-being, social functioning, and family burden, with further assessment or multidisciplinary support considered when clinically relevant concerns are identified.

papers.title: Beyond the Headache: Sleep-Related Symptom Burden in Children and Adolescents with Migraine and Episodic Tension-Type Headache.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are frequently reported in children with primary headache disorders, but differences in sleep-related symptom profiles between pediatric migraine and episodic tension-type headache (TTH) remain unclear. This study aimed to compare Pediatric Sleep Questionnaire (PSQ) total and domain scores among children and adolescents with migraine, episodic TTH, and healthy controls and to examine whether these patterns differed according to sex and age. This analytical cross-sectional study included 197 participants aged 6-18 years recruited in Mersin, Türkiye, between 1 March 2022 and 31 December 2023. Primary headache disorders were diagnosed according to the International Classification of Headache Disorders, third edition. The headache group comprised 76 patients with migraine and 27 with episodic TTH, while 94 healthy students constituted the control group. Parents completed the validated Turkish extended PSQ. A PSQ total score ≥ 6 was considered indicative of clinically relevant sleep-related symptoms. Headache characteristics and intensity, measured using a 0-10 numerical rating scale, were also recorded. A PSQ total score ≥ 6 was observed in 60/103 participants with headache (58.3%) and 26/94 healthy controls (27.7%; p < 0.001). Compared with controls, participants with headache had higher median PSQ total scores (6 [interquartile range, 4-8] vs. 4 [2-6]; p < 0.001), Breathing Problems scores (2 [1-3] vs. 1.5 [1-3]; p = 0.022), Awakening and Developmental Symptoms scores (2 [1-2] vs. 1 [0-2]; p < 0.001), and Behavioral Problems scores (1 [0-3] vs. 0 [0-1]; p < 0.001). Snoring Problems scores did not differ (p = 0.659). Both migraine and episodic TTH groups had higher PSQ total and Behavioral Problems scores than healthy controls, without significant differences between the two headache diagnoses. Compared with episodic TTH, migraine was associated with a longer headache history (p = 0.011), more frequent attacks (p = 0.021), and greater headache intensity (p = 0.013). Children and adolescents with migraine or episodic TTH exhibit a substantially greater burden of clinically relevant sleep-related symptoms than healthy controls. This burden is primarily reflected in overall, awakening/developmental, and behavioral symptoms rather than snoring. Sleep screening should therefore be incorporated into the clinical assessment of both pediatric migraine and episodic TTH.

papers.title: Sleep Patterns Across the Transfusion Cycle in Children with Transfusion-Dependent β-Thalassemia: A 14-Day Prospective Controlled Study Using Sleep Diaries and Repeated Questionnaires.
papers.abstract: Sleep across the transfusion cycle remains understudied in children with transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia (TDT). We assessed sleep patterns and hematologic correlates before and after transfusion. This prospective, controlled, repeated-measures study included 27 children with TDT and 30 controls who had been frequency-matched at recruitment on age, sex, and school-attendance category; no fixed one-to-one patient-control pairs were formed. Participants completed 14-day sleep diaries spanning the pre- and post-transfusion weeks and repeated Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ) and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) assessments. The three primary outcome domains were sleep-diary measures (including sleep regularity, daytime nap frequency, sleep-duration variability, and nocturnal awakenings), continuous CSHQ total and subscale scores, and the continuous modified PSQI global score. Threshold classifications, individual questionnaire items, and laboratory/MRI associations were exploratory. Multiplicity was controlled within the diary and questionnaire families using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR). Within the primary sleep-diary domain, weekday sleep irregularity was greater in patients pre-transfusion (16.3 vs. 10.2 min; q = 0.014) but not post-transfusion (q = 0.220); sleep-duration variability was greater before and after transfusion (both q = 0.026), and diaries recorded more daytime naps and more and longer nocturnal awakenings across 14 days (q < 0.05). Within the primary questionnaire domains, the continuous modified PSQI global score and CSHQ total, sleep-behavior, and daytime-sleepiness scores were higher in patients pre-transfusion (all q < 0.001). In exploratory, unadjusted analyses, lower pre-transfusion hemoglobin correlated with greater daytime sleepiness (ρ = -0.425; p = 0.027). Multiplicity-adjusted findings across the three primary outcome domains suggest differences in reported sleep timing, regularity, continuity, daytime napping, and questionnaire scores in children with TDT. However, the small sample, the number of component outcomes and contrasts, and the absence of actigraphy require cautious interpretation.

papers.title: Psychotropic Polypharmacy in a 5-Year-Old Boy with a SHANK3 Variant and Complex Mental Health Problems.
papers.abstract: Dysfunction of the SHANK3 gene has been linked to several neuropsychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders, such as attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder, and epilepsy. SHANK3 haploinsufficiency is the known etiology of Phelan-McDermid syndrome. This report presents a five-year-old boy in whom the c.2062G>C; p.Val688Leu variant was identified in a mosaic state in the SHANK3 gene (40% of heterozygous cells) and classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS). The patient was diagnosed with complex mental health problems, which, analogous to typical SHANK3 disruption, included ADHD, oppositional defiant disorder, developmental coordination disorder, Non-REM sleep arousal disorder, insomnia disorder, and avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder. Starting at the age of three years, his psychiatric treatment had included various medication trials over the course of two years. Ultimately, a substantial reduction in emotional outbursts, externalizing behaviors, and parental stress occurred following a multimodal treatment approach comprising psychotropic polypharmacy (PP), i.e., lisdexamfetamine, melatonin, and risperidone, along with behavioral therapy interventions, speech therapy, and occupational therapy. Under this PP, constipation was documented as the only adverse reaction. At the 15-month follow-up, improvements had been quite stable, despite risperidone medication being stopped about 19 weeks after initiation. As shown in this case report, even very young children with complex neuropsychiatric problems and SHANK3 variants might not be treated sufficiently by therapeutic interventions alone, but might require a combination of therapeutic and psychopharmacological interventions to achieve a substantial symptom reduction. However, PP must be approached with a high degree of caution and subjected to close monitoring in children with SHANK3 variants, who are susceptible to an elevated risk of adverse outcomes. Moreover, given the paucity of research in this population, it seems advisable to follow prevailing general guidelines in child and adolescent psychiatry.

papers.title: Hemimegalencephaly in Children: A Systematic Review of Diagnosis, Management, and Outcomes in 161 Reported Cases.
papers.abstract: To describe the clinical and genetic features of hemimegalencephaly in pediatric patients, and to highlight treatment outcomes in this population. This is a systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines. We used PubMed, Google Scholar, and Scopus for this systematic literature review as databases. Clinical data, imaging findings, EEG patterns, genetic variants, associated syndromes and treatment modalities and outcomes were reviewed, analyzed and summarized in tables. A total of 161 pediatric patients with hemimegalencephaly are described. A risk of bias and sensitivity analysis was conducted. Hemimegalencephaly is more frequently reported in males. The most common subtype was isolated hemimegalencephaly followed by the syndromic subtype, in particular the association with Ito's hypomelanosis. The most common seizure type was focal onset with impaired awareness. Genetic analysis showed variants in TSC1, TSC2, NPRL3, and PIK3CA, supporting mTOR pathway involvement. Drug-resistant epilepsy was present in approximately 73.2% (118/161) of the sample size. Hemispherectomy, especially functional, in our sample was more frequently reported and the current limited available literature suggests potentially comparable seizure outcomes compared to anatomical hemispherectomy in terms of seizure reduction. Our biggest limitation is the lack of long-term neurological follow-up in the existing literature. Hemimegalencephaly presents with a wide clinical and genetic spectrum and frequently results in drug-resistant epilepsy and developmental impairment. Although surgery may offer seizure relief, outcomes vary and the optimal approach remains individualized. Early diagnosis is essential to enable timely intervention and coordinated care. A multidisciplinary team including neurology, genetics, radiology and neurosurgery is key to optimizing outcomes. Broader studies including milder cases and long follow-up are needed to fully understand disease progression and guide management.

papers.title: Prefecture-Level Mean Elevation, Sleep Duration, and Depressive Symptoms Among Middle-Aged and Older Adults in China: A Cross-Sectional CHARLS Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Prefecture-level mean elevation, as an area-level proxy of residential altitude, has been associated with sleep disturbance and depressive symptoms, but it may also reflect broader regional differences in social conditions. The roles of sleep duration and regional context remain uncertain among long-term community residents. Objectives: To examine these associations among adults aged 45 years or older in China. Methods: This cross-sectional study linked nationally representative China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study Wave 4 data from 15,562 adults aged 45 years or older with prefecture-level mean elevation. Linear regression with province fixed effects assessed sleep duration and CESD-10 scores. Altitude-by-sleep interactions, generalized additive models, restricted cubic splines, and exploratory bootstrap mediation analyses were conducted. Results: Moderate and high altitude were associated with higher CESD-10 scores in unadjusted models, but not after adjustment for sleep category, individual covariates, and province fixed effects. They were associated with 0.280 and 0.363 h longer self-reported sleep. The altitude-by-sleep interaction was significant, and predicted CESD-10 scores were highest among short sleepers across altitude groups. Nonlinear patterns were observed, whereas indirect effects through continuous sleep duration were not significant. Conclusions: The apparent association between higher altitude and depressive symptoms was not robust after regional adjustment. Sleep duration did not show evidence of mediation, although sleep category was associated with differences in the observed altitude-depressive symptom pattern.

papers.title: Depressive Symptoms, Insomnia-Related Difficulties and Self-Rated Health Among Community-Dwelling Adults Aged 40 Years and Older in Western China: A Cross-Sectional Structural Equation Modelling Study.
papers.abstract: This study examined the associations of depressive symptoms, medical help-seeking attitudes and perceived neighbourhood built environment with self-rated health, including statistical indirect associations through an Insomnia Severity Index (ISI)-derived sleep construct, among community-dwelling adults in western China. This secondary cross-sectional analysis included 433 adults aged ≥40 years in Gaoping District, Nanchong, China. Self-rated health was assessed using the SF-36 General Health subscale. PHQ-9 and ISI indicators were reverse-coded so that higher values represented lower depressive symptom burden and fewer insomnia-related difficulties, respectively. Structural equation modelling estimated direct and indirect associations, with 5000 bootstrap resamples. Multi-group analysis compared the ISI-self-rated health path between family-functioning groups. Model fit indices were CFI = 0.955, TLI = 0.953 and RMSEA = 0.037. The ISI-derived construct had the largest standardised direct coefficient for self-rated health (β = 0.383, p < 0.001). Reverse-coded PHQ-9 was associated with ISI (β = 0.544, p < 0.001) and self-rated health (β = 0.164, p = 0.009). Medical help-seeking attitudes were directly associated with self-rated health (β = 0.193, p = 0.001). The PHQ-9-ISI-self-rated health indirect estimate was 0.208 (95% CI, 0.134-0.294). Corresponding indirect associations for help-seeking attitudes and neighbourhood environment were not supported. NEWS-A direct paths and the family-functioning group difference were not statistically significant. The findings supported an ISI-related statistical indirect association between depressive symptoms and self-rated health within the specified model. They do not establish causal mediation or intervention effectiveness.

papers.title: Psychological Distress Indicators Among Pregnant Women Reporting Intimate Partner Violence in Primary Care: Implications for Trauma-Informed Antenatal Care in Nigeria.
papers.abstract: Background: Intimate partner violence (IPV) during pregnancy is a significant public health concern in low-resource settings. Primary care antenatal clinics are often the first point of contact for pregnant women and provide important opportunities to identify both violence and related psychological distress. This study examined the prevalence of IPV during pregnancy, the reporting of psychological distress indicators (low self-esteem, sleep disturbance, and suicidal ideation) among women reporting IPV, and the association between IPV and timing of antenatal care (ANC) initiation in a low-resource primary care setting in Nigeria. Methods: We analyzed cross-sectional data from 463 pregnant women receiving routine antenatal care at a primary health center in Abuja, Nigeria (February-July 2024). IPV during the index pregnancy was assessed via an interviewer-administered survey. Psychological distress indicators were measured using single-item self-report questions assessing perceived self-esteem, sleep disturbance, and suicidal thoughts attributed to violence. Multivariable logistic regression models examined associations between IPV and late ANC initiation (>12 weeks' gestation), adjusting for sociodemographic and partner-related characteristics. Additional analyses examined the associations between late ANC initiation and perceived psychological distress indicators among women reporting IPV. Results: IPV during the index pregnancy was reported by 68.7% of participants. Among women reporting IPV, high proportions also reported psychological distress indicators, including low self-esteem (77.1%), sleep disturbance (67.3%), and suicidal thoughts (approximately one-third). Women reporting IPV had significantly lower odds of delayed ANC initiation (aOR = 0.37; 95% CI: 0.19-0.69). Individual psychological indicators were not independently associated with ANC timing after adjustment. Conclusions: Although women reporting IPV were more likely to initiate ANC early, they frequently also reported psychological distress indicators, highlighting routine ANC visits as important opportunities for trauma-informed identification, assessment, and referral.

papers.title: Screen Culture's Association with Generation Z Adolescents' Posture and Well-Being in Egypt: Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Egyptian Generation Z adolescents are heavily engaged with screens for several purposes, including education, entertainment, social media, and gaming. This raises red flags about how screen culture may affect sleep quality, posture-related habits, and health-related quality of life. Objectives: To examine how different types and amounts of weekday and weekend screen time are associated with symptoms of insomnia, body awareness of postural habits, and health-related quality of life among Egyptian Generation Z adolescents. Materials and Methods: A cross-sectional English-language online survey was completed by a self-selected convenience sample of Egyptian adolescents aged 13-18 years from multiple governorates; 530 participants were included in the analysis. Participants reported total screen time, the Insomnia Severity Index, Body Awareness of Postural Habits questionnaire, and the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory. Multiple linear regression models were adjusted for age, gender, body mass index, level of education, and place of residence. Results: After false-discovery-rate adjustment across 30 comparisons, 13 activity-specific associations met the significance threshold. Higher ISI scores were associated with weekday job or internship-related use, weekday and weekend entertainment use, and weekday and weekend social-media use. Lower Q-BAPHYP scores were associated with weekday and weekend entertainment and social-media use. Lower PedsQL scores were associated with weekday job or internship-related use, weekday entertainment use, and weekday and weekend social-media use. The models explained limited variability in the outcomes. Conclusions: The screen use of Egyptian Generation Z adolescents is associated with insomnia, postural awareness, and overall quality of life; additional unmeasured factors probably influence such outcomes as well.

papers.title: Comparison of Sleep Quality Across Different Sagittal Skeletal Patterns in Orthodontic Patients.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sagittal skeletal patterns are associated with upper airway dimensions, which may influence breathing during sleep and potentially relate to sleep quality. We hypothesized that global Thai-Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (Thai-PSQI) scores would differ among skeletal Class I (Sk-I), Class II (Sk-II), and Class III (Sk-III) groups. Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted at the Department of Orthodontics, Faculty of Dentistry, Thammasat University, from June 2023 to March 2024. Ninety-three patients aged 18-50 years presenting to initiate orthodontic treatment were classified by ANB angle as Sk-I (0.5-5.1°), Sk-II (>5.1°), or Sk-III (<0.5°), with 31 participants per group. Sleep quality was assessed using the Thai-PSQI; scores > 5 indicated poor sleep quality. Sex, age, and BMI were analyzed as demographic variables. Results: Mean global PSQI scores were 6.42 ± 2.71, 6.68 ± 3.39, and 6.26 ± 2.46 for Sk-I, Sk-II, and Sk-III, respectively. Global PSQI scores did not differ significantly among skeletal groups (H = 0.024, p = 0.988, ε2 < 0.001). Overall, 55.9% of participants were poor sleepers, and the distribution of good and poor sleepers did not differ among groups (χ2 = 1.134, p = 0.567, Cramer's V = 0.110). No significant associations were observed between global PSQI and sex, age, or BMI (p = 0.279, 0.848, and 0.948, respectively). Conclusions: No statistically significant differences in subjective sleep quality were identified among the three sagittal skeletal groups in this sample.

papers.title: True Versus Sham Thread Embedding Acupuncture for Spasticity-Related Symptoms and Disabilities in Multiple Sclerosis: Study Protocol of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Introduction: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease and one of the most common causes of non-traumatic disability in young adults, with over 2.8 million individuals worldwide. Spasticity affects nearly 80% of people with MS (PwMS), contributing to pain, gait disturbance, bowel/bladder dysfunction, sleep/mood disorders, and impaired quality of life. The complex condition known as Spasticity-Plus syndrome is gaining attention. Current pharmacological treatments are limited by side effects and short duration of benefits. Thread Embedding Acupuncture (TEA), which involves embedding absorbable polydioxanone (PDO) sutures into acupoints, offers prolonged stimulation and has shown promise in managing spasticity, particularly after stroke. Several randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have reported positive effects in MS. This is a study that protocol aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of True TEA (TTEA) compared with Sham TEA (STEA) in reducing spasticity and improving mobility and related symptoms among PwMS. Methods: This is a protocol of a randomized, sham-controlled, patient-, assessor- and analyst-blinded, superiority clinical trial. Thirty-eight eligible PwMS with moderate-to-severe spasticity will be randomized 1:1 to either TTEA or STEA. Both groups will undergo puncture at the same 30 acupoints but only the TTEA group will receive PDO thread implantation. The primary outcome is change in disability (EDSS). Secondary outcomes are Numeric Rating Scale for Spasticity (NRS-S), walking ability (MSWS-12), activities of daily living (Barthel Index), pain (McGill Pain Questionnaire), fatigue (MFIS), sleep quality (PSQI), urinary symptoms (ABSST), mood (HADS), quality of life (EQ-5D-5L), overall treatment satisfaction, willingness to repeat and recommendation to others. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, 4 weeks, and 12 weeks post-intervention. Intention-to-treat analysis will be performed. Perspective: To our knowledge this trial will be the first RCT to evaluate TEA in spasticity-related symptoms in PwMS. By using a sham-controlled design, it will determine whether TEA confers benefits beyond needle puncture alone. Findings may provide evidence for incorporating TEA as a complementary option in MS symptom management and inform future larger-scale trials. Trial registration: IRCT20121228011912N8 (22 March 2024; Updated: 13 July 2026).

papers.title: Quality of Life and Patient-Reported Outcomes During First-Line Chemotherapy in Older Patients with De Novo Metastatic Gastrointestinal Cancers: A Prospective Longitudinal Study.
papers.abstract: This study was conducted to prospectively evaluate quality of life (QoL), patient-reported outcomes, and geriatric domains during the first 3 months of first-line systemic therapy in older patients with de novo metastatic gastrointestinal cancers. This prospective longitudinal study included 90 patients aged ≥65 years receiving first-line chemotherapy-based systemic therapy. Assessments were performed at baseline, Month 1, and Month 3 using validated QoL, sleep, anxiety, cognitive, and nutritional instruments. The primary endpoint was change in EORTC QLQ-C30 Global Health Status/QoL from baseline to Month 3. Treatment tolerability, initial radiologic response, and exploratory survival outcomes were also assessed. Mean Global Health Status/QoL increased from 68.1 at baseline to 71.0 at Month 3; the model-estimated mean change was +3.0 points (95% CI, -0.3 to 6.2; p = 0.071). Fatigue and appetite loss improved significantly, and normal nutritional status increased from 31.1% to 62.2% (p < 0.001). Clinically meaningful QoL improvement and deterioration occurred in 38.9% and 18.9%, respectively. Treatment intolerance occurred in 46.7%. Disease control was associated with more favorable QoL change than progressive disease (difference, 17.8 points; 95% CI, 6.0-29.7; FDR-adjusted p = 0.008). Baseline nutritional impairment (adjusted HR, 3.58) and poor sleep quality (adjusted HR, 3.30) were associated with shorter progression-free survival. Mean global QoL did not change significantly during the first 3 months, while several symptom and nutritional domains improved. More favorable QoL trajectories were observed with disease control, and baseline nutritional impairment and poor sleep quality were associated with shorter progression-free survival.

papers.title: Eating Behavior, Body Appreciation, and Sleep Quality in Italian Blind Baseball Athletes: A Cross-Sectional Exploratory Survey.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Visual impairment is associated with poor sleep quality, psychological distress, and unhealthy lifestyle behaviors. Adapted sports, such as blind baseball (BXC), may help promote healthy lifestyles and overall well-being. However, evidence regarding eating behavior, sleep quality, body appreciation, and lifestyle habits among regular BXC players remains scarce. This cross-sectional study provides an exploratory multidimensional characterization of these domains in competitive Italian BXC athletes according to sport participation and visual impairment characteristics, comparing findings descriptively with normative data from the Italian general population. Methods: Fifty-three competitive Italian BXC players (mean age 39.3 ± 13.1 years; representing a response rate of 49.1% of the national league) completed an anonymous online survey assessing eating behavior (Adult Eating Behavior Questionnaire, AEBQ), body appreciation (Body Appreciation Scale-2, BAS-2), sleep quality (Brief Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, B-PSQI), and lifestyle habits. Group differences were assessed using chi-square tests for categorical variables and Mann-Whitney U tests for continuous variables, reporting medians, interquartile ranges, effect sizes (rank-biserial r), and 95% confidence intervals. Results: BXC athletes demonstrated BMI, sleep quality, eating behavior, and body appreciation profiles comparable to those of the Italian general population. BAS-2 scores were high (3.7-3.8), while B-PSQI scores (4.0-5.6) and the proportion of poor sleepers (~40%) remained within normative ranges despite visual impairment. Eating behavior showed no significant dysregulation. However, in exploratory subgroup analyses, multisport athletes displayed lower Satiety Responsiveness than BXC-only athletes (2.30 ± 0.79 vs. 2.78 ± 0.71; p = 0.02), poorer sleep quality (B-PSQI: 6.05 ± 3.12 vs. 4.70 ± 3.73; p = 0.05), and a higher prevalence of poor sleep (55.0% vs. 30.3%). Athletes with acquired visual impairment showed higher Emotional Overeating and Emotional Undereating scores than those with congenital impairment, although these differences did not reach statistical significance. Conclusions: BXC athletes displayed an overall favorable lifestyle profile. Though the cross-sectional design prevents causal inferences, these exploratory findings indicate that participation in BXC is compatible with healthy lifestyle habits and positive body appreciation, hence supporting adapted team sports as an inclusive framework for multidimensional health promotion. Future studies using objective physiological assessments and longitudinal designs are needed to clarify dose-response relationships and long-term health outcomes.

papers.title: Physical Performance Outcomes and Programme Delivery Costs of ELDERPLAY, a Community-Based Multicomponent Exercise and Recreational Intervention for Older Adults: A Non-Randomized Controlled Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study examined the association between participation in a community-based multicomponent physical and recreational programme (ELDERPLAY) and changes in physical performance and frailty-related outcomes in adults aged 65 years and older, and estimated programme delivery costs. The study was designed as a quasi-experimental, non-randomized controlled evaluation conducted in a community setting. Methods: Community-dwelling older adults (n = 184) were allocated to an intervention group (n = 103) or a control group (n = 81) through voluntary enrolment and geographic matching. Participant enrolment and data collection were carried out between July 2022 and December 2023, after ethics approval had been obtained. The intervention consisted of 20 supervised sessions (two per week) combining Vivifrail-based multicomponent exercises with simple recreational activities. Primary outcomes were physical performance and frailty-related function, assessed using the Short Physical Performance Battery and the Timed Up and Go test. Secondary exploratory outcomes included actigraphy-derived daily step count, heart rate, and sleep parameters, recorded over seven consecutive days at a single intermediate assessment point. Analyses were conducted using analysis of covariance and generalized estimating equations adjusted for cholesterol, COVID-19 vaccination and Barthel Index score. Programme costs were estimated using an activity-based costing approach. Results: Compared with the control group, participants in the intervention group showed greater improvement over time in balance, gait performance, chair-stand performance and overall physical performance (time × group interaction: gait performance p < 0.001, partial eta squared 0.450; chair-stand performance p < 0.001, 0.306; SPPB total score p < 0.001, 0.361; Timed Up and Go p < 0.001, 0.224). At 10 weeks, the adjusted mean SPPB total score was 9.62 (95% CI 9.25-10.00) in the intervention group and 7.80 (95% CI 7.37-8.23) in the control group, and the adjusted mean Timed Up and Go was 8.85 s (95% CI 8.08-9.62) versus 12.04 s (95% CI 11.15-12.92). Higher daily step counts were also observed in the intervention group; heart rate and sleep parameters were recorded cross-sectionally at a single intermediate assessment point that coincided with the delivery of the programme and are reported only as descriptive values. The programme was delivered at a mean cost of €92.3 per participant, or €62.3 per participant when the research monitoring devices are excluded. Conclusions: Participation in a community-based multicomponent exercise programme incorporating recreational activities was associated with improvements in clinically relevant physical performance outcomes in community-dwelling older adults. The programme was delivered in full at a mean delivery cost of €92.3 per participant in a real-world community setting. Because allocation was not randomized, the groups differed at baseline, and outcome assessment was carried out by a single unblinded assessor who designed and coordinated the programme but did not deliver the sessions, these findings are associative and require confirmation in a randomized trial. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07864831 (retrospectively registered).

papers.title: Weighted Blanket Load and Sleep Outcomes During Daytime Napping and Overnight Sleep: Two Randomized Crossover Studies.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Weighted blankets provide deep pressure stimulation and may support relaxation, sleep initiation, and sleep continuity. However, the optimal acute blanket load across different sleep contexts remains unclear. This study examined the acute effects of 7 kg, 9 kg, and 14 kg weighted blankets on daytime napping and overnight home sleep in healthy adults. Methods: Two complementary randomized crossover protocols were integrated into one manuscript. In Protocol A, 20 healthy young adults completed four randomized 30-min laboratory nap conditions: control/sham blanket, 7 kg, 9 kg, and 14 kg weighted blankets. In Protocol B, 20 healthy young adults completed four randomized overnight home sleep conditions: personal blanket control, 7 kg, 9 kg, and 14 kg weighted blankets. All conditions were separated by one-week washout intervals. Portable EEG/EOG polysomnography was used to assess nap and sleep architecture. Relaxation state, handgrip strength, blood pressure, heart rate, and skin/ambient temperature were also assessed where applicable. Results: During daytime napping, no statistically significant differences were observed across conditions for sleep outcomes. During overnight home sleep, the original gender-adjusted repeated-measures model indicated a significant condition effect on sustained sleep efficiency [F(1.929, 9.646) = 14.223, p = 0.001, η2p = 0.740], with higher values under the 9 kg and 14 kg conditions compared with control. However, a sensitivity analysis excluding gender, using the same seven complete cases, did not confirm a significant overall condition effect [F(3, 18) = 0.630, p = 0.605]. Systolic blood pressure decreased after overnight sleep with the 9 kg blanket, while skin and ambient temperatures remained unchanged. Conclusions: Weighted blankets did not significantly affect objective sleep outcomes during the daytime nap protocol. During overnight sleep, the original gender-adjusted model suggested a potential effect on sustained sleep efficiency; however, this finding was based on only seven participants with complete data and was not reproduced in either the sensitivity analysis excluding gender or the non-parametric Friedman analysis. The remaining objective sleep outcomes did not differ significantly across conditions. Accordingly, the sustained sleep efficiency finding should be considered exploratory and model-dependent rather than confirmatory evidence of an effect of weighted blanket load on overnight sleep. Larger and longer-term studies are needed before conclusions regarding the overall effectiveness of weighted blankets for sleep can be drawn.

papers.title: Adherence to the 24 h Movement Guidelines and Associated Factors Among First-Year University Students in Spain: UNILIFE-M Study at Universidad Loyola Andalucía.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: University students are at a critical stage for establishing healthy lifestyle habits, yet little is known about their adherence to integrated 24 h movement guidelines that include physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep. We examined the proportion of students meeting the Canadian 24 h movement guidelines and associated factors among first-year students at a single Spanish university (UNILIFE-M). Methods: This cross-sectional analysis included 671 first-year students from Universidad Loyola Andalucía (Spain) participating in the UNIversity Students' LIFEstyle Behaviours and Mental Health (UNILIFE-M) study. Combined guideline adherence used complete cases (n = 646). Behaviors were assessed with the Spanish Physical Activity Scale 2.1 (PAS-2.1S). Adherence required ≥150 min/week of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, ≤8 h/day of total sedentary time including ≤3 h/day of recreational screen time (both sedentary criteria required), and 7-9 h/night of sleep. Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (complete cases on covariates, n = 644). Results: Overall, 137/646 students (21.2%) met all three guidelines, while 54 (8.4%) met none. Male sex was associated with higher odds of adherence (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.65; 95% confidence interval [95% CI] 1.10 to 2.47), and a lifetime mental health diagnosis was associated with lower odds (aOR = 0.28; 95% CI 0.08 to 0.72). Age > 18 years (aOR = 0.64; 95% CI 0.39 to 1.03) and non-health sciences enrollment (aOR = 0.69; 95% CI 0.46 to 1.03) showed borderline associations that were not robust across sensitivity analyses. Conclusions: In this single-university first-year sample, adherence to the 24 h movement guidelines was relatively low. Associations should be interpreted as cross-sectional correlates, not causal determinants.

papers.title: Long-Term Secondary Prevention Gaps Among Young Survivors of Acute Myocardial Infarction in China: A Hospital-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Premature acute myocardial infarction (AMI) has become an important public health challenge. Young survivors face prolonged residual cardiovascular risk, yet real-world implementation of long-term secondary prevention across medication use, health behaviors, and risk-factor monitoring remains insufficiently characterized in China. Methods: In this hospital-based cross-sectional study, we included 1377 young AMI survivors aged 18-44 years who attended follow-up at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between 2023 and 2025. Current use of major secondary prevention medications, achievement of four health-behavior targets (smoking abstinence/cessation, physical activity, diet, and sleep), and lipid monitoring during the preceding 12 months were assessed using standardized interviews and medical records. Recurrent myocardial infarction (MI) and repeat coronary revascularization occurring between discharge after the index AMI and the study visit were retrospectively identified. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine associations between secondary-prevention implementation domains and recurrent events. Results: Participants had a mean age of 39.1 years, and 95.9% were male. Recurrent MI occurred in 9.2% and repeat revascularization in 13.7%. The proportion concurrently using four major medication classes decreased from 50.0% at discharge to 25.9% at follow-up. Overall, 45.1% achieved good behavioral implementation, defined as meeting at least three of four ideal behaviors. In fully adjusted models, good behavioral implementation was associated with lower odds of recurrent MI (odds ratio [OR] 0.49, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.32-0.73) and repeat revascularization (OR 0.72, 95% CI 0.52-1.00). Concurrent use of all four medication classes and frequent lipid monitoring were not independently associated with recurrent outcomes. Conclusions: Among young AMI survivors in China, substantial gaps in long-term secondary prevention were observed, particularly for healthy behaviors. These findings support the public health importance of strengthening lifestyle-oriented and multidisciplinary follow-up strategies for young survivors of AMI. Because exposure and outcome periods overlapped partially, findings should be interpreted as associational rather than causal.

papers.title: Night Shifts and Occupational Fatigue Among Nurses Who Work 12-Hour-Shifts in Jeddah.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Night-shift work is essential for continuous nursing care but may disrupt circadian rhythms, impair well-being, and contribute to occupational fatigue. This study assessed the impact of night-shift work and occupational fatigue among nurses working 12 h shifts at King Abdulaziz University Hospital (KAUH) in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Methods: A quantitative, descriptive-correlational, cross-sectional design was used. A convenience sample of 234 registered nurses with more than one year of night-shift experience participated. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing sociodemographic and work-related characteristics; the physiological, psychological, and social impacts of night-shift rotation; and occupational fatigue using the Occupational Fatigue Exhaustion/Recovery (OFER) Scale. Results: Most nurses experienced physiological (82.1%), psychological (66.2%), and social (73.9%) impacts of night-shift work. Mean OFER scores were 49.6 ± 28.1 for chronic fatigue, 54.9 ± 16.2 for acute fatigue, and 49.2 ± 12.3 for intershift recovery. Night-shift impacts were positively associated with chronic and acute fatigue and negatively associated with intershift recovery. Social and psychological impacts were independently associated with chronic fatigue and intershift recovery, while social impact and the number of night shifts were independently associated with acute fatigue. Conclusions: Twelve-hour night-shift work was associated with substantial physiological, psychological, and social impacts and with higher occupational fatigue and lower intershift recovery. Organizational strategies that limit excessive night duties, protect recovery time, and strengthen staff support may improve nurses' well-being and performance.

papers.title: Enzyme-Assisted Bacteria-Yeast Co-Fermentation of Ganoderma lucidum: Metabolomic Reprogramming, Sensory Evolution, and Sleep-Promoting Effects.
papers.abstract: To enhance the extraction efficiency and bioactivity of Ganoderma lucidum, this study developed a novel enzyme-assisted bacteria-yeast co-fermentation system utilizing Lactobacillus acidophilus and Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Following optimization using response surface methodology, the maximum yields of polysaccharides and triterpenoids reached 2.07% and 3.55%, respectively, substantially exceeding those obtained by direct extraction. Structural characterization revealed that the integrated process induced substantial changes in the polysaccharides, including increased homogeneity, mannose enrichment, and a more porous microstructure. Furthermore, untargeted metabolomics demonstrated that co-fermentation significantly altered the small-molecule profile, characterized by the differential regulation of specific triterpenoids and the enrichment of peptides and amino acids. These metabolic shifts were associated with the evolution of the sensory profile, particularly increased taste richness. In vivo evaluations using a mouse model of PCPA-induced insomnia revealed that the fermented extract exhibited greater sleep-promoting activity than the direct extract. The fermented extract increased hypothalamic 5-HT and GABA levels and was accompanied by modulated gut microbiota composition by increasing the abundance of Lactobacillus and reducing that of Prevotella. These findings suggest that the combined enzymatic-fermentation strategy alleviates insomnia, potentially involving modulation of the microbiota-gut-brain axis, offering preliminary insights into the potential application of Ganoderma lucidum in functional foods.

papers.title: Hemerocallis citrina Baroni (Daylily): A Comprehensive Review of Flavonoids and Phenolic Compounds-Extraction, Phytochemistry, Biological Activities, and Food Applications (2000-2026).
papers.abstract: Hemerocallis citrina Baroni, commonly known as daylily or "Huang Hua Cai," is a well-established traditional medicinal and edible plant widely cultivated in East Asia for more than two millennia. Its flower buds, stems, leaves, and roots are rich in flavonoids and phenolic compounds, which constitute the principal bioactive phytochemicals responsible for a wide range of pharmacological effects, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, neuroprotective, antidepressant, and sleep-improving activities. Although several studies have investigated the chemical composition of Hemerocallis citrina Baroni, a comprehensive and up-to-date review specifically focused on the flavonoids and phenolic compounds of this plant remains lacking. In this review, we systematically summarize the research progress from 2000 to 2026 on the extraction methods, structural identification, phytochemical profiles, and biological activities of flavonoids and phenolic compounds from H. citrina flower buds, stems, and leaves. Advanced analytical techniques, such as UPLC-PDA/MS, UHPLC-QQQ-MS/MS, and HPLC-Q-TOF-MS, have revealed a diverse array of these compounds, including quercetin, kaempferol, and isorhamnetin glycosides, as well as various caffeoyl- and p-coumaroylquinic acids. The health-promoting effects of these polyphenols, together with current knowledge on their mechanisms of action and potential applications in functional foods and traditional Chinese medicine, are critically discussed. By consolidating recent phytochemical and pharmacological findings, this review provides a scientific foundation for the further development and utilization of H. citrina flavonoids and phenolic compounds as valuable resources for functional foods, nutraceuticals, and natural therapeutics.

papers.title: Association of Total Atherosclerosis Burden of Baroreceptor-Resident Arteries with Heart Rate Variability and Its Circadian Rhythm in Patients with Ischemic Stroke.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Post-stroke cardiac autonomic dysfunction is associated with poor neurological recovery and cardiovascular events. However, its association with vascular disease remains incompletely understood. We evaluated associations of atherosclerotic burden in baroreceptor-resident arteries (BRAs), including the carotid sinus (CS) and aortic arch (AA), with heart rate variability (HRV) and its circadian rhythm after ischemic stroke. Methods: This cross-sectional study consecutively enrolled 253 patients with first-ever ischemic stroke within 30 days of onset. Total atherosclerosis burden of baroreceptor-resident arteries (TAB-BRA) was assessed using computed tomography angiography (CTA), and patients were categorized based on TAB-BRA tertiles.
