In the common complete-case sample (n = 1573), the crude inverse association between SAS and total A-OBS was markedly attenuated after district adjustment and was not statistically significant in the fully adjusted model (B = -0.027, 95% CI -0.057 to 0.003; β = -0.055; p = 0.078). Small inverse associations were observed for Rest and Sleep (β = -0.086), Occupational Variations and Adaptation (β = -0.099), and Occupational Meaning and Value (β = -0.071), but not for Temporality; all three significant domain associations remained below 0.05 after Holm correction. Sensitivity analyses produced broadly similar patterns. Overall, PSU was not robustly associated with total occupational balance after contextual adjustment, while selected dimensions showed small associations requiring cautious interpretation and longitudinal confirmation.

papers.title: Smartphone Dependence, Sleep Quality, and Suicidal Ideation Across Adolescence: A Six-Year Longitudinal Study.
papers.abstract: Suicide is a leading cause of death during adolescence, and both smartphone dependence and poor sleep have been associated with suicidal ideation. However, it remains unclear whether these associations reflect stable differences between adolescents or year-to-year changes within adolescents. This study examined the developmental trajectories of smartphone dependence, sleep quality, and suicidal ideation over six years spanning the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic and tested whether sleep quality accounted for the association between smartphone dependence and suicidal ideation at the between-person and within-person levels. Data were drawn from six annual waves (2018 to 2023) of the Korean Children and Youth Panel Survey 2018 middle school first-grade cohort (N = 2590; 54.2% boys). A parallel piecewise latent growth curve model (LGCM) and random-intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) were estimated. Smartphone dependence increased before the pandemic onset (B = 1.47 per year) and declined slightly thereafter (B = -0.16), sleep quality declined after the onset (B = -0.05), and suicidal ideation decreased before the onset (B = -0.10) and increased gradually thereafter (B = 0.03), with no immediate shift at the onset. In the LGCM, the indirect effect of smartphone dependence on suicidal ideation through sleep quality was significant for usual levels (B = 0.005, p < 0.001) and pre-onset change (B = 0.008, p = 0.001) but not for post-onset change (B = -0.001, p = 0.570); Wald tests indicated that the path from sleep quality to suicidal ideation (p = 0.001) and the indirect effect (p = 0.004) differed between the two periods. In the RI-CLPM, higher-than-usual smartphone dependence predicted higher-than-usual suicidal ideation one year later (β = 0.05, p < 0.001), whereas no within-person lagged paths involving sleep quality were significant. Smartphone dependence, poor sleep quality, and suicidal ideation thus co-occurred between adolescents, but annual within-person changes did not show a pathway through sleep quality. Because period differences cannot be separated from age-related development in a single cohort, they should not be interpreted as pandemic effects. These findings support attending to adolescents with high smartphone dependence and poor sleep within existing school-based screening systems, whereas the mechanisms through which risk is transmitted require studies with shorter measurement intervals.

papers.title: How Aesthetic and Economic Factors Affect Consumers' Purchasing Decisions: Evidence from EEG.
papers.abstract: Consumer theory identifies cultural and economic factors as key influences on purchasing decisions. Artworks, as material carriers of culture, are shaped by these factors in a particularly pronounced way. This study proposes that consumers' artwork purchasing decisions are jointly determined by aesthetic and economic considerations. Using event-related potential (ERP) technology, artworks were classified into a 2 by 2 matrix of aesthetic valence and price. Seventy students from a university in western China made purchase or rejection decisions while their electroencephalogram was recorded. Results showed that both aesthetic and price factors jointly influenced artwork purchasing decisions. Aesthetic valence had a larger effect (F(1, 69) = 134.98, p < 0.001, ηp2 = 0.662) than price (F(1, 69) = 22.47, p < 0.001, ηp2 = 0.246), and participants were most willing to buy positively rated, low-priced artworks (M = 42.2%, SD = 24.2). The medial frontal negativity (MFN) amplitude and theta-band power were larger during purchase than rejection decisions, and this difference was most pronounced when participants chose to buy negatively rated artworks (t(48) = 4.31, p < 0.001, d = 0.61). Because the sample was drawn from a single university in western China and consisted of young students, the conclusions carry generalisability limitations. This study maps aesthetic and economic considerations during consumer purchasing onto separable neural processes, contributing to the intersection of cultural neuroscience and neuroeconomics.

papers.title: From Exposure to Psychological Harm: A Socioecological and Trauma-Informed Narrative Review of Bullying, School Violence, and Youth Mental Health.
papers.abstract: Bullying and school violence are preventable exposures and potentially modifiable risk factors for adverse youth mental health and educational outcomes. This critical narrative review integrates epidemiological, longitudinal, genetically informed, quasi-experimental, meta-analytic, and intervention evidence on bullying, cyberbullying, selected forms of school violence, and their psychological sequelae. The evidence base available at the original submission was reassessed during revision through a complete structured rerun of PubMed/MEDLINE, APA PsycINFO, ERIC, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, Google Scholar, major publisher platforms, and authoritative organizational sources from 15 to 27 August 2026, followed by a final update on 8 September 2026; reporting was guided by the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA). Evidence supports robust associations with depression, anxiety, trauma symptoms, loneliness, sleep disturbance, self-harm, suicidality, substance use, and externalizing difficulties, although effect estimates differ in design, metric, and certainty. We propose an evidence-informed, not prospectively validated, mechanism-to-action framework. Within the reviewed corpus, direct prospective mediation evidence was identified for interpersonal distrust and school belonging; longitudinal evidence supports a rumination-sleep sequence; and threat appraisal, humiliation/shame, and social defeat remain theory-supported candidate mechanisms. Socioecological theory organizes influences across individual, peer, school, family, community, policy, and digital levels. Trauma-informed principles are used as an interpretive and ethical lens; evidence for whole-school trauma-informed models remains limited. Whole-school anti-bullying programs modestly reduce exposure, but average effects on internalizing symptoms are small and heterogeneous. Systems should therefore coordinate exposure prevention with assessment, treatment, and follow-up of psychological harm. Progress should be judged by safety, equity, belonging, functioning, and recovery, not incident counts alone.

papers.title: Associations Between Interoceptive Awareness, Psychological State, and Physical Performance in Sport-Science Students: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Interoceptive awareness may support stress regulation in sport, but its association with objective physical performance remains unclear. This study examined relationships between self-reported interoceptive awareness, perceived stress, anxiety, sleep quality, and field-based performance in sport-science students. Eighty-five students (54 men, 31 women; 20.65 ± 2.43 years) completed the MAIA-2, PSS-10, STAI, and PSQI and performed handgrip, countermovement-jump, sit-and-reach, and bilateral Y-Balance tests. Analyses included Pearson correlations, Welch tests with false-discovery-rate correction, HC3-robust hierarchical regression, and exploratory age- and sex-adjusted bootstrap indirect-effect models. The MAIA-2 composite was inversely associated with perceived stress (r = -0.461, 95% CI [-0.614, -0.275], p < 0.001) but showed no detectable association with physical performance (r = -0.003 to 0.136; all q ≥ 0.961); equivalence testing indicated that four of the five performance correlations were statistically equivalent to zero within a ±0.30 bound. Women reported higher stress and anxiety, whereas men showed greater handgrip strength and jump height. Individual-sport participants reported higher state anxiety than team-sport participants (g = -0.886, q = 0.004). Interoceptive awareness did not significantly increase explained variance in any performance model, and exploratory indirect-effect confidence intervals all included zero. Self-reported interoceptive awareness was related to perceived stress but was not detectably related to brief field-based performance in this sample. Longitudinal and experimental studies are needed to test temporal and causal mechanisms.

papers.title: Trauma, Hyperarousal, and Sleep: Neurobehavioral Pathways in Affective Disorders.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are common across affective disorders and may coexist with traumatic stress and persistent hyperarousal. This narrative review examines how trauma-related hyperarousal and sleep dysfunction are associated with major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar disorder (BD), while distinguishing observed associations from proposed mechanisms. A targeted search of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar identified clinical, neurobiological, and translational literature on trauma, hyperarousal, insomnia, nightmares, circadian disruption, MDD, and BD. The evidence supports a multidimensional view of hyperarousal involving partly overlapping autonomic, cognitive-attentional, affective, and behavioral domains; however, it does not establish hyperarousal as a unitary mechanism or justify equating trauma-related vigilance with manic activation. Sleep disturbance may function as a symptom, vulnerability factor, or prodromal change, but no single sleep measure is currently a validated individual-level prognostic marker. Clinically, trauma history, sleep phenotype, affective state, comorbidity, medication effects, and current safety should be assessed jointly. Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia and established trauma-focused treatments have the strongest clinical basis within their indicated populations, whereas imagery rehearsal therapy, prazosin, chronobiological strategies, and candidate biomarkers require diagnosis-specific and evidence-graded interpretation. Longitudinal studies integrating objective sleep measures and explicit temporal modeling are needed before proposed pathways or precision approaches can be considered clinically validated.

papers.title: A Component-Level Network Analysis of Emotional Symptoms, Sleep Problems, and Physical Activity Identity at a Chinese University.
papers.abstract: This cross-sectional study estimated a component-level network of depression, anxiety, and stress dimensions, sleep components, and physical activity identity among students at one Chinese university. Using convenience and snowball sampling, 3762 students at Zhejiang University completed the DASS-21, PSQI, and MIPAI-25. Regularized partial-correlation networks were estimated with EBICglasso (gamma = 0.50) using automatic correlation selection. Strength, bridge strength, signed bridge expected influence, and predictability were calculated. Network accuracy and stability were examined with 1000 bootstrap resamples, and sex differences were assessed using a Network Comparison Test with 1000 permutations. Scores above the prespecified screening cutoffs were observed for depression (76.0%), anxiety (79.5%), stress (62.8%), and poor sleep quality (80.2%). In the DASS-PSQI network, hypnotic medication use had the largest overall strength point estimate (1.126), whereas depression and anxiety subscales had the largest bridge-strength point estimates (0.121 and 0.093). In the exploratory three-domain network, hypnotic medication use again had the largest strength estimate (1.131); MIPAI acknowledgment had the highest bridge-strength point estimate (0.134), closely followed by depression (0.130), and remained the highest-ranked MIPAI dimension in the mixed graphical model. Its individual cross-domain edges were small, and their specific pattern was model-dependent. Overall network structure did not differ significantly by sex (M = 0.087, p = 0.117), whereas global strength was higher in males than females (7.11 vs. 6.83; p = 0.012); no individual edge remained significant after Holm correction. These findings describe cross-sectional conditional associations and do not establish causal or protective effects.

papers.title: Breathing-Practice Status and Psychological Outcomes 12 Months After a Structured Program in University Students.
papers.abstract: Evidence regarding long-term breathing-practice maintenance and associated psychological outcomes remains limited. This observational longitudinal follow-up examined psychological outcomes and self-reported breathing-practice status 12 months after a structured program in university students. Thirty-four students from the intervention group of a 14-week breathing study were assessed immediately after the program (T1) and at the 12-month follow-up (T2). At T2, 18 reported occasional or regular practice, and 16 reported no or rare practice. All 13 psychological outcomes were included in the longitudinal analyses. For each outcome, the T2 score was regressed on the corresponding T1 score and T2 practice group using HC3 robust standard errors. Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied across all 13 outcomes. Compared with the no/rare-practice group, the ongoing-practice group had more favorable T2 scores for subjective happiness, general happiness, positive affect, sleep quality, all six dimensions of psychological well-being, and life satisfaction after adjustment for the corresponding T1 scores; all q < 0.001. However, the ongoing-practice group also had higher worry scores (adjusted difference 4.52, 95% CI 1.44 to 7.60; q = 0.006). Negative affect did not differ between groups (-0.50, 95% CI -3.51 to 2.50; q = 0.735). Sensitivity analyses produced the same pattern. Ongoing breathing practice was associated with several favorable psychological outcomes at 12 months, but also with higher worry scores and no difference in negative affect. Because practice status was self-selected and measured concurrently with the outcomes, these findings are associative rather than causal and may be influenced by common-method bias, recall bias, and social-desirability bias.

papers.title: Psychological Profiles, Stress, Sleep Quality, and Psychological Risk Indicators Across Teams and Competitive Levels in Elite Football Players.
papers.abstract: Psychological factors and sleep quality are relevant to athlete well-being and adaptation in high-performance sport, yet their distribution within the same elite football structure remains insufficiently understood. This pooled cross-sectional study described and compared psychological profiles and psychological risk indicators across 11 teams within a single elite football organisation and explored selected contextual variables. Participants were 376 elite football players (245 male and 131 female; aged 14-37 years) from teams competing at U16, U19, amateur, and professional levels. Assessment followed the Psycholight framework and incorporated selected dimensions from the CPRD, MIPS, STAI, DASS-21, and PSQI. Group differences were examined using nonparametric comparisons, Wilcoxon effect sizes, Fisher's exact tests, and odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Psychological profiles and risk distributions varied across the studied teams, with heterogeneous patterns across psychological and sleep-related indicators. Given the close interrelationship between sex, age, team, competitive level, and season, these findings should be interpreted as patterns observed among the teams represented in the present sample rather than as independent effects of sex or competitive level.

papers.title: Identification of CLOCK and MARK2 as Candidate Blood-Based Biomarkers in Type 2 Diabetes: An Integrated Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is often accompanied by nervous system complications. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying T2DM remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify candidate blood-based biomarkers associated with T2DM by screening a neural-related gene set through integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood. The present analysis focused on the systemic expression patterns of the selected genes in peripheral blood as indicators of T2DM-associated immunometabolic dysregulation, rather than on neurological involvement. The neural-related gene set was used only as a predefined screening starting point. Methods: We employed a three-tier validation framework comprising (1) a training cohort (GSE15932, 8 T2DM patients vs. 8 controls) for biomarker discovery using differential expression analysis and machine learning (XGBoost, random forest, and PPI network topology); (2) an independent validation cohort (GSE184050, 50 T2DM patients vs. 65 controls) for cross-dataset diagnostic performance assessment (ROC analysis); and (3) an experimental validation cohort (5 T2DM patients vs. 5 controls) for independent clinical confirmation by RT-qPCR. Additionally, single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE268210) was used to investigate cell type-specific expression and immune regulatory networks. Results: By combining multiple screening methods and cross-dataset validation, we identified CLOCK and MARK2 as key candidate genes from the neural-related gene set. CLOCK and MARK2 showed high discriminatory performance in the discovery cohort, whereas their AUCs were 0.613 and 0.653, respectively, in the validation cohort, indicating limited standalone discriminatory ability. Both genes are highly expressed in peripheral blood monocytes and are associated with MIF-(CD74+CXCR4)-mediated cell communication, TNFA-NFκB inflammatory signaling, and activation of oxidative phosphorylation pathways. Finally, RT-qPCR in clinical samples confirmed that both genes were indeed upregulated (p < 0.05). Conclusions:CLOCK and MARK2 were identified as candidate T2DM-associated blood-based biomarkers with reproducible expression differences across datasets. Their discriminatory performance was more modest in the independent validation cohort, indicating limited standalone diagnostic utility. Single-cell and computational analyses further suggested potential immunometabolic relevance. Because neurological phenotyping, cognitive assessment, and direct measures of nervous system involvement were not available in this study, any relationship between these genes and the neurological manifestations of T2DM remains speculative and hypothesis-generating, and requires prospective validation in cohorts with matched neurocognitive data.

papers.title: Ubiquitin Proteasome System BTB-Adaptor Protein Insomniac Modifies Seizure Severity and Response to the Ketogenic Diet in a Drosophila Model of Mitochondrial Encephalomyopathy.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The ubiquitin proteasome system (UPS) serves critical cellular homeostatic functions that contribute to neurological health, including neuronal metabolism, synaptic plasticity, and the molecular circadian clock. The UPS is tightly regulated to ensure the correct balance of healthy proteins and those targeted for degradation and recycling; malfunction in this quality control process can contribute to disease states such as neurodegeneration and cancer. Target specificity in this system is due in part to ubiquitin ligase adaptor proteins, such as those of the BTB superfamily of proteins, which connect substrates to the larger proteasomal complex. In Drosophila, the BTB family member insomniac (human orthologs KTCD2, 5, and 17) has been shown to regulate sleep, arousal, and synaptic plasticity, but has not been examined for a role in neuronal excitability disease phenotypes. Methods: We utilized a genetic approach to interrogate neurobehavioral dysfunction in mitochondrial encephalomyopathy (ME) and the ability of dietary therapy to modulate this dysfunction. Results: Here, we report that genetic interference with insomniac modifies seizure-like behavior in a neuronal-subtype-specific manner in the ATP61 model of ME, ameliorating seizure severity when knocked down in GABAergic or dopaminergic neurons. Furthermore, while ATP61 typically responds to ketogenic dietary therapy with a robust reduction in seizure phenotype, we report that knockdown of insomniac or its binding partner Cullin RING Ligase 3 (Cul3) in neurons ablates this effect entirely, a previously unreported role for the UPS in downstream neurophysiological effects of the KD. Conclusions: These results implicate UPS BTB adaptor proteins as therapeutic targets in seizure pathology and identify them as a novel contributor to the ketogenic suppression of neuronal hyperexcitability. These two neurological roles are likely to be proceeding via cellular and molecularly distinct pathways, including a non-CRL3-based mechanism of seizure modulation.

papers.title: Divergent Intralesional Enhancement Kinetics in a Primary Ovarian Leiomyoma on Dual-Layer Spectral CT: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Indeterminate solid adnexal masses can remain difficult to characterize on conventional CT. Dual-layer spectral CT provides iodine concentration (IC), effective atomic number (Zeff), and electron density relative to water (EDW) from the same acquisition. We report a histopathologically confirmed primary ovarian leiomyoma and describe its regional multiphasic spectral behavior. Case Presentation: A 37-year-old woman presented with an O-RADS 4 solid right adnexal mass. Retrospective analysis sampled two enhancement-defined intralesional compartments across true noncontrast (TNC), arterial, venous, and delayed phases. On TNC images, ROI-A and ROI-B showed closely similar Zeff (7.39 vs. 7.37) and EDW (103.8% vs. 103.9%). ROI-A showed intense arterial enhancement (102.2 HU; IC 2.95 mg/mL; Zeff 8.78) followed by decline, whereas ROI-B showed low early enhancement and marked delayed fill-in, with delayed values slightly exceeding ROI-A (83.8 vs. 71.3 HU; IC 1.74 vs. 1.54 mg/mL; Zeff 8.25 vs. 8.16). Initial histopathology suggested fibroma; immunohistochemistry established ovarian leiomyoma. Conclusions: The two enhancement-defined compartments showed closely similar baseline spectral measurements but divergent postcontrast behavior. EDW demonstrated substantially lower-amplitude phase-related changes than IC and Zeff. These findings are descriptive and do not establish a diagnostic spectral signature or histologic specificity. When multiphasic dual-layer spectral CT has already been clinically acquired, regional spectral analysis may provide quantitative characterization of intralesional enhancement heterogeneity. In this case, however, spectral CT did not establish the diagnosis or alter management, and definitive diagnosis remained dependent on histopathology and immunohistochemistry.

papers.title: Size Matters: A Large-Scale, Real-World Dataset of Smartphone-Based Obstructive Sleep Apnea Screening in the General Population.
papers.abstract: Background: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a highly prevalent sleep-related breathing disorder that remains substantially underdiagnosed and is causally linked to cardiovascular and metabolic morbidity. Clinical diagnosis relies on the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) derived from polysomnography (PSG) or home sleep apnea testing. Low-threshold, clinically validated screening tools that can be used repeatedly outside a clinical setting may help to reduce underdiagnosis and to capture longitudinal information. Methods: We describe a real-world dataset generated by a medical device-grade, smartphone-only OSA screening application (Snorefox M) that calculates the AHI from nocturnal breathing sounds. All users who provided informed consent for the research use of their anonymized data between March 2023 and December 2025 were included. The diagnostic performance of the application had previously been validated against parallel PSG. Additional post hoc analysis of classification performance at additional AHI thresholds, together with the linear correlation between the app-derived and PSG-derived AHI are described. Results: The dataset comprises 239,132 measurements from 31,647 consenting adults. A total of 14,351 users contributed at least two valid nights, yielding 221,820 nights of longitudinal screening data. Across all attempted measurements, 96.5% yielded a valid analysis result. The mean per-measurement AHI was 14.3 (median 11.8, SD 11.0). Voluntary, self-reported demographic information was available for a subgroup of 8092 users (mean age 54.4 years, mean ESS score 7.2). Against PSG, the application detected moderate-to-severe OSA (AHI ≥ 15) with a sensitivity of 0.91 and a specificity of 0.83, and severe OSA (AHI ≥ 30) with a sensitivity of 0.93 and a specificity of 0.97. The app-derived AHI correlated strongly with the PSG-derived AHI (Pearson r = 0.80, p < 0.001). The app-derived AHI discriminated against the PSG reference with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.951 for severe OSA (AHI ≥ 30), 0.925 for moderate-to-severe OSA (AHI ≥ 15) and 0.877 for the AHI ≥ 10 threshold. Conclusions: This is, to our knowledge, the largest longitudinal dataset of unsupervised, real-world OSA screening from a general adult population using a clinically validated, low-threshold smartphone tool. Smartphone-based screening can complement established diagnostic pathways, support pre-clinical triage and generate longitudinal data not accessible through single-night testing, while self-selection and the unsupervised nature of data capture constrain representativeness. By introducing this resource, this work provides the basis for the in-depth analyses of demographics, symptom-result concordance and night-to-night variability.

papers.title: Peripheral Nerve Conduction and Anthropometric Characteristics in Elite American Football Players: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: American football exposes athletes to repeated collisions and intense physical loading. This exploratory study compared anthropometric characteristics and peripheral nerve conduction parameters between elite American football players and healthy sedentary men. Methods: Thirty-six elite male players and 39 sedentary male controls underwent anthropometric assessment and motor and sensory nerve conduction studies (NCSs) of the upper and lower extremities. Groups were compared with Welch's t-test, and effect sizes (Hedges' g) were reported with 95% confidence intervals. The false discovery rate (FDR) was controlled across all 110 NCS parameters, which were also analysed in linear models adjusted for age, for age, height and body mass index, and for age and local limb circumference. Results: Players had larger shoulder, upper-arm and forearm circumferences, whereas height and limb segment lengths were similar. After age adjustment and FDR control, players had longer accessory nerve motor latencies on both sides (right: 3.70 ± 0.86 vs. 2.74 ± 0.85 ms; left: 3.63 ± 0.94 vs. 2.69 ± 0.75 ms; both q < 0.001), a shorter left musculocutaneous motor latency and a faster left sural sensory conduction velocity. Median, ulnar, sural and tibial response amplitudes were lower in players, but these differences were attenuated after adjustment for age. Conclusions: Elite American football players differ from sedentary controls in a small number of nerve conduction parameters, most consistently in accessory nerve motor latency. Because the controls were sedentary and the design was cross-sectional, these differences cannot be attributed specifically to American football rather than to intensive athletic training in general. They should be regarded as hypothesis-generating findings that require independent replication.

papers.title: Minute-Scale Sleep-Onset HRV as a Candidate Risk-Stratification Biomarker for Diabetic Retinopathy: An Exploratory Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the most common microvascular complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), yet DR screening coverage remains inadequate worldwide. Diabetic autonomic neuropathy typically precedes DR, and heart rate variability (HRV) provides a non-invasive autonomic measure; however, whether HRV can screen for DR remains unexplored. Methods: This pilot study investigated whether sleep-onset minute-scale HRV indices-SDANN1 (standard deviation of 1-min segment means of normal-to-normal intervals) and SDANN2 (2-min segments)-serve as candidate screening biomarkers. Using a public 24-h Holter ECG dataset of T2DM inpatients (N = 39; 11 DR-positive, 28 DR-negative), sleep-onset time-points from cardiopulmonary coupling analysis were used to extract 30 min of post-onset ECG. Results: SDANN1 was significantly lower in the DR group (median 23.6 vs. 44.8 ms, p = 0.028, d = 0.74), with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.731 (95% CI: 0.530-0.901). At the optimal threshold of ≤ 25 ms, the odds ratio was 8.1 (95% CI: 1.7-38.4), with DR prevalence of 58% in the high-risk versus 12.5% in the low-risk group. Among 12 candidates, only the SDANN family reached significance. Conclusions: sleep-onset minute-scale HRV shows promise as a candidate risk-stratification biomarker for DR; prospective longitudinal validation in larger, sex-balanced cohorts is required before any screening application.

papers.title: Pan-immune-inflammation value and sleep disturbances in rheumatoid arthritis: A population-based NHANES study.
papers.abstract: The present study sought to assess the individual and synergistic effects of pan-immunoinflammatory value (PIV) and trouble sleeping on rheumatoid arthritis (RA). We used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey from 2005 to 2020. PIV was computed as: (neutrophil count × platelet count × monocyte count) /lymphocyte count. Trouble sleeping was assessed using a single self-reported question (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey item SLQ050), while RA case ascertainment relied on self-reported diagnosis by a physician. The associations between PIV and sleep-related RA susceptibility were interrogated through multivariable logistic regression models, with restricted cubic splines deployed to unmask potential nonlinear relationships. Effect modification was further evaluated via stratified analyses across demographic and clinical subgroups. The analytical cohort comprised 27,398 participants (2032 RA cases). In fully adjusted models, elevated PIV demonstrated a 14.9% increased RA risk in the highest versus lowest PIV quartile (Q4 vs Q1) (OR = 1.149, 95% CI:1.007-1.312), while trouble sleeping independently conferred 59.8% higher odds (OR = 1.598, 95% CI:1.449-1.761). Interaction analysis revealed that the association between PIV and RA was modulated by trouble sleeping. This study explores the association between elevated PIV, trouble sleeping, and RA. However, due to the cross-sectional nature of the data, causality cannot be inferred. The findings suggest a correlation between PIV and trouble sleeping with RA risk, but further longitudinal studies are required to establish causal relationships.

papers.title: A retrospective comparative study of a full-course precision MDT nursing studio model integrating rational emotive behavior therapy for standardized health management during pregnancy.
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the clinical application of a full-course precision multidisciplinary team (MDT) nursing studio model integrating rational emotive behavior therapy (REBT) during standardized health management in pregnancy and explores its associations with maternal psychological status, antenatal care adherence, implementation-related indicators, and maternal and neonatal outcomes. This single-center retrospective comparative study included 210 pregnant women who received standardized antenatal health management from June 2024 to December 2025. Participants were classified into a conventional care group (n = 102) and an intervention group (n = 108) according to the nursing management model documented in routine clinical records. The intervention group received the MDT-REBT model in addition to routine care. Outcomes included maternal psychological indicators, health management performance, implementation- and acceptability-related indicators, and maternal and neonatal outcomes. Compared with the conventional care group, the intervention group had significantly lower generalized anxiety disorder-7, Patient Health Questionnaire-9, fear of childbirth, and perceived stress scores, as well as lower rates of moderate-to-severe anxiety and depression (all P < .01). Adherence to antenatal visits, gestational weight management, health education compliance, exercise compliance, dietary management compliance, sleep management compliance, self-monitoring compliance, and mean number of antenatal visits were all significantly better in the intervention group (all P < .05). Follow-up completion, attendance at nutritional counseling and psychological support sessions, stage-specific follow-up attendance, management compliance, and satisfaction were also significantly higher, whereas withdrawal/noncompletion was lower (all P < .01). Multivariable analyses showed that the intervention model was independently associated with better antenatal care adherence, improved gestational weight management, and lower generalized anxiety disorder-7 scores. Several maternal and neonatal outcomes showed numerical between-group differences, but most were not statistically significant. The full-course precision MDT nursing studio model integrating REBT was associated with improved maternal psychological status, better antenatal care adherence, enhanced pregnancy health management performance, and more favorable implementation-related indicators during pregnancy. These observational findings do not establish causality, and no clinical effectiveness conclusion can be drawn for maternal or neonatal endpoints that were not statistically significant. Further prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Association between triglyceride glucose-relative fat mass index and obstructive sleep apnea risk: A cross-sectional study from NHANES.
papers.abstract: The triglyceride glucose (TyG) index is correlated with insulin resistance and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), whereas the relative fat mass (RFM) index is linked to obesity and OSA. However, the relationship between the triglyceride glucose-relative fat mass (TyG-RFM) index and OSA has been less studied in the US population. This research was designed to investigate the association between the TyG-RFM index and OSA prevalence. Data for this cross-sectional analysis were drawn from the 2005 to 2008 and 2015 to 2018 cycles of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, including participants aged ≥20 years. Weighted multivariate logistic regression and restricted cubic splines were employed to examine the relationship between the TyG-RFM index and OSA. Stratified and sensitivity analyses were undertaken to test the consistency of the association. Of the 7283 participants, the mean age was 46.9 (standard deviation = 16.7) years, and 48.7% were male. Among them, 3616 individuals exhibited symptoms of OSA. The fitted curve demonstrated a linear positive relationship between the TyG-RFM index and OSA (P for nonlinearity = 0.292). In the fully adjusted model, each 10-unit increase in the TyG-RFM index was associated with a 4% higher OSA risk (odds ratio, 1.04; 95% confidence interval, 1.02-1.06). When analyzed by quintiles, participants in the highest quintile had 95% greater odds of OSA compared with those in the lowest quintile (odds ratio, 1.95; 95% confidence interval, 1.29-2.95). Stratified and sensitivity analyses confirmed the stability of the primary results. This cross-sectional research showed that the TyG-RFM index was associated with OSA risk among US adults. These results may aid in OSA risk stratification and early screening.
keywords: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey

papers.title: Association of triglyceride-glucose and its related indices with circadian syndrome: Evidence from a prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the association of the triglyceride glucose (TyG) index and its related indices, TyG-body mass index, TyG-waist circumference, and TyG-waist-to height ratio (TyG-WHtR), with incident circadian syndrome (CircS) in a middle-aged and elderly Chinese population. This study employed a prospective cohort design using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, collected in 2011 and 2015. We utilized 4 separate logistic regression models to assess the potential impact of each independent variable on CircS. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis is used to examine the linearity assumption and dose-response relationships. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was employed to compare the diagnostic accuracy and efficiency of TyG, TyG-BMI, TyG-WC, and TyG-WHtR in identifying CircS. During the 4-year follow-up period, 796 new cases of CircS were identified among the participants, representing 22.3% of the total cohort. After adjusting for potential covariates, nonlinear associations between TyG, TyG-BMI, TyG-WC, and TyG-WHtR with the risk of CircS were identified, exhibiting a significant dose-response relationship. TyG, TyG-WC, and TyG-WHtR exhibited an inverted U-shaped curve relationship with CircS, while the relationship between TyG-BMI and CircS was close to linear. Meanwhile, receiver operating characteristic analysis indicated that TyG-BMI demonstrated better diagnostic performance. This study provides important evidence that TyG, TyG-BMI, TyG-WC, and TyG-WHtR are significant risk factors for CircS. Moreover, we found that TyG-BMI may serve as an important potential biomarker for diagnosing new-onset CircS.
keywords: China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study

papers.title: Long-term changes in subjective daytime sleepiness following tonsillectomy and uvulopalatopharyngoplasty (UPPP): A prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Diseases of the palatine tonsils may be associated with varying degrees of subjective daytime sleepiness (SDS), a symptom that may affect daily functioning. This study evaluated long-term changes in SDS in patients before and after tonsillectomy or uvulopalatopharyngoplasty (UPPP). The primary aim of this study was to evaluate long-term changes in SDS following tonsillectomy or UPPP. Secondary objectives included the assessment of patient satisfaction and the influence of demographic and clinical factors, including sex, age, chronic diseases, tonsil size, and histopathological findings, on treatment outcomes. A prospective cohort study included 105 adult patients, with an 85% follow-up rate: 89 patients (26 women, 63 men). SDS was assessed using the Epworth Sleepiness Scale before surgery and after a mean follow-up of 6 years. Additional analyses considered demographic and clinical variables. Patient satisfaction was measured using a visual analog scale and willingness to undergo repeat surgery. Both tonsillectomy and UPPP were associated with a significant long-term reduction in SDS. The mean ESS score decreased from 7.29 preoperatively to 4.37 at follow-up (P < .05). A clinically meaningful improvement in ESS of ≥2 points was achieved in 71.9% of patients, and the proportion of patients with normal ESS scores (≤10) increased from 75.3% to 92.1% (P < .001). While the unadjusted ESS reduction was greater after UPPP than after tonsillectomy (4.22 vs 1.81 points), multivariable analysis demonstrated a significant interaction between surgical procedure and baseline ESS, indicating that the magnitude of improvement differed between procedures according to baseline subjective sleepiness. Sex, tonsil size, histopathological findings, and chronic diseases did not significantly influence the outcomes. Tonsillectomy and UPPP were associated with a sustained, long-term reduction in SDS. The magnitude of postoperative improvement increased with baseline subjective sleepiness, with the relative difference between procedures becoming greater at higher baseline ESS values. These findings suggest that upper airway surgery may be associated with durable improvements in patient-reported daytime sleepiness, including among patients with baseline ESS scores within the non-EDS range.

papers.title: Associations of sleep disturbance and emotion regulation with perceived workplace safety and fatigue among male firefighters with prior occupational accidents: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Firefighters bear a high burden of sleep disturbance and occupational accidents, yet how their individual health states relate to their own appraisal of workplace safety and fatigue is unclear. This cross-sectional study examined whether sleep disturbance, sleep quality, and emotion-regulation capacity are associated with perceived workplace safety and fatigue-related status in this group. One hundred five active-duty male firefighters from urban brigades in the Marmara region of Türkiye, all with a documented occupational accident history, completed the Basic Scale on Insomnia Complaints and Quality of Sleep, a single-item Sleep Quality Scale, the Emotion Regulation Skills Questionnaire, and the Perceived Workplace Safety/Fatigue Status tool (PWSFS), an exploratory, author-developed composite scored 20 to 100, with higher scores being more favorable (Cronbach α = 0.71 in this sample). Pearson correlations and a multiple linear regression of the PWSFS total score on the 3 predictors, adjusted for age and fire-service experience, were computed. The mean Basic Scale on Insomnia Complaints and Quality of Sleep was 12.2 (standard deviation 5.0), and the mean PWSFS was 73.2 (standard deviation 11.2). Greater sleep disturbance was associated with less favorable perceived safety and fatigue status (r = -.81, 95% confidence interval - .87 to - .74, P < .001), whereas better sleep quality (r = .52, P < .001) and greater emotion-regulation skills (r = .44, P < .001) showed weaker associations. The model accounted for 67% of the variance (F(5, 99) = 39.74, P < .001), and sleep disturbance was the only unique correlate (β = -.81, P < .001); neither sleep quality (P = .46) nor emotion regulation (P = .47) contributed independently. The association persisted in reduced-content analyses but was attenuated when sleep- and fatigue-related items were removed (safety-awareness subset r = -.58, R2 = .38, β = -.77). Among firefighters with prior occupational accidents, sleep disturbance was the measured individual-level variable most strongly associated with perceived workplace safety and fatigue. Because the design was cross-sectional and relied on single-source self-report, and because the outcome was measured with an exploratory, author-developed composite, these associations are provisional and cannot support causal inference. Sleep may nonetheless warrant attention in occupational safety and fatigue-management efforts; longitudinal, multi-source research is needed to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Association of sleep time with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality among individuals with advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: A NHANES-based prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: To delve into the relationship of sleep time with the onset of all-cause and mortality from cardiovascular disease (CVD) among individuals suffering from advanced Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome. This prospective cohort study collected information from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2005 to 2018 that recruited 4266 adult participants with advanced (Stage 3-4) CKM syndrome. Sleep time was measured as the self-reported sleep hours and classified as <7 hours, 7 to 8 hours (reference group), and >8 hours per night. Mortality outcomes including all-cause and cardiovascular death were ascertained by linking records to the National Death Index (NDI) up to December 31, 2019. Kaplan-Meier survival curves analyzed mortality by sleep time group. In the study, the researchers investigated the relationship between sleep time and mortality utilizing multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Besides, restricted cubic spline analysis was performed to check for possible nonlinear relationship between sleep time and all-cause/CVD death. A total of 1294 all-cause death cases and 465 due to CVD within a median 7.6 years of follow-up. Within the completely adapted model by Cox, comparison with a reference group (7-8 hours), long sleep time (>8 hours) was linked to a significantly increased CVD death risk (Hazard Ratio [HR]: 1.53; 95% confidence Interval: 1.14-2.07; P = .005) and showed a borderline remarkable connection with all-cause death (HR: 1.21; 95% confidence Interval: 1.00-1.46; P = .05). Short sleep time (<7 hours) did not significantly correlate with either death outcome. The analysis revealed U-shaped association of sleep time with overall mortality (P for nonlinearity = .0017). In the end, sleep time in patients with advanced CKM syndrome exhibited a U-shaped or J-shaped connection with death rates. Sleeping too much (>8 hours) has been deemed a pronounced risk indicator for both CVD and overall mortality. According to these results, sleep time ought to be seen as an essential health marker in managing advanced CKM syndrome clinically and long-sleepers require additional clinical assessment.

papers.title: The overall effects of virtual reality interventions on ICU patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients frequently experience psychological distress, pain, sleep disruption, and motor impairments. Virtual reality (VR) has emerged as a promising nonpharmacological adjunct to improve these outcomes, yet existing evidence remains fragmented and inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized recent clinical trials to evaluate the effectiveness of VR on mental health, pain, sleep, functional outcomes, and delirium in adult ICU patients. This review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (2020) guidance and was registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42023482529). Eight databases were searched for randomized controlled trials published between January 2000 and September 2025. Eligible studies included adult ICU patients receiving immersive or non-immersive VR interventions. Primary outcomes were anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD); secondary outcomes included pain, sleep quality, lower-limb function, and bedside balance. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB tool, and certainty of evidence was graded using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Twenty randomized controlled trials were identified, involving a total of 1551 patients. This meta-analysis showed that VR intervention helped improve anxiety (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -0.67, 95% confidence interval [CI: -1.00 to -0.35], P < .0001), depression (SMD = -0.46, 95% CI [-0.72 to -0.21], P = .0004), PTSD [mean difference = -5.48, 95% CI (-9.36 to -1.59), P = .006], lower-limb function score [mean difference = 2.83, 95% CI (1.99 to 3.67), P < .001] and sleep quality (SMD = 0.70, 95% CI [0.47 to 0.92], P < .0001), but had no significant effect on pain score (SMD = -0.57, 95% CI [-1.49 to 0.36], P = .23) and bedside balance score (SMD = 0.61, 95% CI [-0.44 to 1.66], P = .25). Most studies were assessed as having varying degrees of risk of bias. All evidence was rated from very low to moderate. VR interventions may confer meaningful benefits for anxiety, depression, PTSD, and sleep quality in adult ICU patients, and may improve lower-limb function in selected populations. However, evidence for analgesic effects and bedside balance remains inconclusive. Standardized VR protocols, objective outcome assessment, and adequately powered multicenter trials are needed to clarify the clinical value of VR in ICU care.

papers.title: Sleep duration, sarcopenia, and incident depressive symptoms in Chinese middle-aged and older adults: A prospective cohort study based on CHARLS.
papers.abstract: Sarcopenia and depressive symptoms are prevalent health issues in middle-aged and older adults, yet the mechanisms linking them remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between sarcopenia and incident depressive symptoms and to examine the potential mediating role of sleep duration. We conducted a prospective cohort study using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study from 2011 to 2015. A total of 5346 participants aged 45 years and older without baseline depressive symptoms were included. Sarcopenia was defined according to the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia 2019 criteria. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the 10-item Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression Scale, with a cutoff of ≥10 indicating depression. Sleep duration was self-reported. Cox proportional hazards models, restricted cubic spline regression, and bootstrap mediation analysis were employed. During a 4-year follow-up, 1482 participants (27.72%) developed incident depressive symptoms. After adjusting for confounders, both possible sarcopenia and confirmed sarcopenia were significantly associated with an increased risk of depressive symptoms (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.21, 95% confidence interval [CI]:1.02-1.44 and HR = 1.36, 95% CI:1.04-1.78, respectively). Longer sleep duration was independently associated with a lower risk of depression (HR = 0.93, 95% CI: 0.90-0.96). However, the mediating effect of sleep duration became non-significant after covariate adjustment (P = .302). Sarcopenia was independently associated with incident depressive symptoms, but sleep duration did not significantly mediate this association after adjustment. These exploratory findings should be interpreted cautiously. These findings suggest that interventions targeting sarcopenia prevention and management may confer beneficial effects on mental well-being in aging populations.

papers.title: Effect of Kinesio Taping on Clinical Parameters in Pregnant Women with Mechanical Low Back Pain.
papers.abstract: During pregnancy, low back pain (LBP) is frequent and affects daily activities and sleep. Fetal safety concerns limit pharmacological options, increasing the use of non-pharmacological approaches such as exercise and kinesio taping (KT). This study aimed to evaluate the effects of exercise combined with KT or sham KT on clinical outcomes in pregnant women with LBP. This randomized controlled study included pregnant women with low back pain between 20 and 32 weeks of gestation and a Visual Analog Scale (VAS) score of ≥3. Participants were randomly assigned to an experimental group (exercise with KT) or a control group (exercise with sham KT). Pain intensity, sleep quality, and functional disability were assessed using VAS, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire (RMDQ). Both groups demonstrated statistically significant improvements in pain intensity (experimental: P < 0.001; control: P = 0.003), with greater reductions observed in the experimental group compared with the control group ( P = 0.044). Sleep quality improved in both groups (PSQI: P < 0.001 and P = 0.008). However, functional disability scores increased significantly in both groups (Roland-Morris: P < 0.001). Exercise combined with KT was associated with improvements in LBP and sleep quality during pregnancy, although functional disability increased over time in both groups, likely reflecting the natural progression of pregnancy. KT may be a supportive non-pharmacological option for pregnancy-related LBP.

papers.title: Obesity and allergic diseases in children: childhood asthma as a model for integrated management.
papers.abstract: Obesity and allergic diseases are highly prevalent in childhood. Asthma represents the best-characterized model in which excess adiposity modifies disease presentation, clinical burden, and treatment response. This review summarizes the recent pediatric evidence, with a focus on clinically actionable mechanisms, obesity-associated asthma phenotypes, and integrated management strategies. Obesity-associated asthma is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous disease phenotype rather than simple comorbidity. Recent pediatric data highlight altered oxidative stress, IL-6-related immunometabolic pathways, distinctive CD4+ T-cell transcriptional programs, and specific lung function patterns, such as dysanapsis and preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm)-like physiology. These mechanisms suggest that persistent symptoms may reflect a combination of airway inflammation, altered lung mechanics, deconditioning, sleep-disordered breathing, and metabolic dysfunction. Interventional studies support structured aerobic training and anti-inflammatory dietary approaches as part of obesity management. Evidence on metabolic pharmacotherapy, including metformin and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists, is emerging and suggests potential respiratory benefits, although current pediatric data remain largely observational and randomized asthma-specific trials are lacking. In children, obesity should be considered a treatable trait requiring an integrated assessment of asthma control, lung mechanics, physical conditioning, sleep-disordered breathing, diet quality, and metabolic health. Current evidence supports multidisciplinary lifestyle interventions, whereas phenotype-driven pediatric therapeutic trials are needed to determine whether targeted metabolic, nutritional, exercise-based, digital, or pharmacological strategies can improve long-term respiratory outcomes.
papers.journal: Current opinion in allergy and clinical immunology

papers.title: Mental Health Outcomes Among Migrant Caregivers: A Systematic Review of Prevalence, Associated Factors, and Supportive Interventions.
papers.abstract: Migrant caregivers play an essential role in addressing global shortages in long-term and domestic care. However, demanding working conditions, social isolation, and migration-related stressors may adversely affect their mental health, while evidence on prevalence, determinants, and effective interventions remains fragmented. This systematic review aimed to synthesize global evidence on the prevalence of mental health outcomes among migrant caregivers, identify associated risk factors, and summarize supportive interventions targeting their mental health. Eight databases were searched for studies published between January 2015 and October 2025. Eligible studies quantitatively assessed mental health outcomes among migrant caregivers or evaluated supportive mental health interventions using validated measurement tools. Due to substantial heterogeneity in study design, populations, and outcome measures, results were synthesized qualitatively. A total of 48 studies were included (42 cross-sectional, 6 interventions). Prevalence of depression, anxiety, psychological distress, sleep problems, and caregiver burden varied widely across settings and measurement tools. Mental health outcomes were consistently associated with sociodemographic, occupational, environmental, physical health, psychosocial, migration-related, and COVID-19-related factors. Evidence on interventions was limited to six small trials, showing modest and inconsistent effects, with more consistent improvements in coping and mental health literacy than in depressive symptoms, varying by design and caregiver characteristics. Migrant caregivers experience a substantial mental health burden associated with employment conditions, workplace social environments, and migration-related factors. Addressing their mental health requires both improved research designs and policy responses that extend beyond individual-level interventions to structural and social conditions.
papers.journal: The International journal of social psychiatry

papers.title: Early Post-Operative Quantitative EEG Central Beta Power Predicts Futile Recanalization After Endovascular Treatment in AIS-LVO.
papers.abstract: Despite successful endovascular recanalization in acute ischemic stroke, approximately 50%-55% of patients experience 90-day futile recanalization (FR). We evaluated the prognostic value of central relative beta power derived from early postoperative quantitative electroencephalography (QEEG) and explored QEEG associations with brain edema and parenchymal hemorrhage. This retrospective, single-center subgroup analysis of the prospective multicenter DETECT2-China registry included 56 patients with acute ischemic stroke due to large-vessel occlusion. Patients underwent 20-30-min EEG recordings approximately 24 h after successful endovascular treatment. Multivariable logistic regression adjusting for seven clinical covariates, Firth and reduced-model sensitivity analyses, and leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) with the DeLong test were performed. An additional sensitivity analysis repeated QEEG feature selection within each training set. Feature reliability was evaluated using split-half intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Of 56 patients, 31 (55.4%) developed 90-day FR. Higher central relative beta power was independently associated with lower odds of FR (adjusted OR: 0.28 per 1-SD increase, 95% CI: 0.11-0.74, p = 0.010). Integrating central beta power into the clinical model increased the fixed-feature LOOCV area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.557 to 0.719 (DeLong p = 0.007). In exploratory analyses, delta-band Brain Symmetry Index specifically tracked parenchymal hemorrhage (PH vs. no intracranial hemorrhage [No ICH], p = 0.006). Exploratory graph analysis also showed macro-scale network disintegration in FR patients. All QEEG features demonstrated high split-half reliability (ICC ≥ 0.75). Central relative beta power recorded approximately 24 h after endovascular treatment was independently associated with 90-day FR and showed potential incremental prognostic value. Exploratory associations with postoperative complications suggest that QEEG may provide a non-invasive bedside "brain window" for neurocritical care.

papers.title: Ketone monoester intake attenuates exercise performance decline in normobaric hypoxia: A post-hoc subgroup analysis of 5 young male adults without acute mountain sickness.
papers.abstract: In hypoxia, endurance performance, sleep, and cognitive function are impaired. Ketone ester (KE) intake can elevate blood, brain, and skeletal muscle oxygenation, making it an interesting strategy to attenuate hypoxia-induced impairments. Given that acute mountain sickness (AMS) influences these parameters, we evaluated the effects of KE intake in non-AMS developing individuals. In a larger project, 14 young, healthy, male participants performed a 29-h protocol at a simulated altitude of 4000-4500 m, involving regular KE or placebo intake. Five participants completed both sessions without developing severe AMS. They completed two maximal incremental cycling tests after 1.5 and 25 h (EXMAX1 and EXMAX2, resp.) and a combined maximal-submaximal test after 26.5 h (EXCOMBO), while resting blood, brain, and skeletal muscle oxygenation and cognitive function were regularly (5-6x) evaluated, and sleep was analyzed. KE did not alter peak power output (PPO) during EXMAX1 or EXMAX2, but increased PPO by 36 W during EXCOMBO. KE increased blood oxygenation before EXMAX1, EXMAX2, and EXCOMBO and increased muscle oxygenation only before EXCOMBO. Sleep and cognitive function were not affected by KE intake. In a non-AMS developing subgroup, KE appears effective to attenuate high-intensity endurance performance decline during subacute hypoxic exposure accompanied by repeated exercise until exhaustion.

papers.title: Making Brain Health Actionable for Older Persons in Primary Care: The Proposed SHAPES Framework.
papers.abstract: Brain health is increasingly recognised as a life-course priority, but its translation into routine primary care for older persons remains uncertain. Vascular risk, sensory function, mobility, nutrition, sleep, mood, environmental exposure, and social participation are often addressed separately, leaving people with multiple recommendations but no coherent plan. We propose SHAPES-Sensory access; Heart, vessels, and movement; Appetite, food, and nutrition; Pollution, tobacco, and alcohol; Emotional health and sleep; and Social connection, purpose, and learning-as a conceptual implementation framework for co-design and feasibility testing. The workflow begins with a brief scan of all six domains. Findings are classified as Protect, Notice, or Investigate using explicit safety criteria. Notice is reserved for a mild, uncertain, non-progressive concern; any persistent, recurrent, progressive, function-limiting, or red-flag change requires clinical assessment. Safety signals take priority; otherwise, one person-valued priority is selected according to importance, likely benefit, modifiability, feasibility, and structural context. The next step may be behavioural, clinical, social/supportive, or service/system. Behavioural actions may be converted into small cue-linked actions, and meaningful success is agreed before follow-up. SHAPES is not a diagnostic test, decision rule, or validated risk score. SHAPES has not yet demonstrated content or face validity, feasibility in routine consultations, or acceptability to older persons or clinicians; its safety, equity and effectiveness also require prospective evaluation.
papers.journal: Journal of primary care & community health

papers.title: Turkish adaptation of the Chrononutrition Profile-Questionnaire (CP-Q): Validity and reliability study.
papers.abstract: The Chrononutrition Profile-Questionnaire (CP-Q) is a behavioral tool for assessing nutrition timing in relation to the sleep-wake cycle. This methodological cross-cultural adaptation and validation study aimed to adapt the CP-Q into Turkish and evaluate the validity and reliability of the Turkish version (CPQ-TR). Cross-sectional data were collected from 271 healthy adults aged 19-64 years, and a randomly selected subgroup (n = 40) completed a two-week reassessment and a 3-day dietary assessment. In a bilingual group (n = 18), ICC values for non-categorical items ranged from 0.57 to 0.97, indicating moderate-to-excellent cross-language agreement. Known-groups analyses yielded the expected chronotype-related differences in nutrition timing, including later wake and eating event times and a wider work/school day eating window in evening types (p < 0.01), consistent with construct validity. Night Eating Questionnaire scores correlated with last eating event timing (r = 0.59-0.69) and night eating frequency (r = 0.55) (p < 0.01), supporting convergent validity. CPQ-TR timing variables correlated strongly with dietary-record-derived meal timings (r = 0.92-0.97; p < 0.01), whereas agreement for the largest meal of the day was low (κ = 0.12, p = 0.27). Test-retest analyses showed good-to-excellent temporal stability (ICC = 0.86-0.98). In conclusion, the CPQ-TR showed generally favorable validity and reliability findings for timing-related variables in this sample, whereas the largest-meal item should be interpreted cautiously.

papers.title: Priority domains, design and contextual considerations for a rehabilitation program addressing the daily living functioning of people diagnosed with borderline personality disorder: a modified nominal group technique.
papers.abstract: People diagnosed with borderline personality disorder (BPD) experience persistent functional impairment, yet no manualised rehabilitation program addressing daily living functioning currently exists, creating opportunity for program development. This study aimed to identify: 1) priority domains of daily living functioning to include in a rehabilitation program, and 2) how such a program could support functional recovery. Five focus groups using a modified nominal group technique captured consumer (n = 9), caregiver (n = 7), mental health clinician (n = 3) and occupational therapist (n = 5) perspectives. Priority domains were ranked to structure discussions. Transcripts were analysed using conventional content analysis. Seven priority domains were identified: 1) Finding purpose and identity through roles, values and milestones; 2) Sleep and energy management; 3) Coping strategies to support emotional regulation; 4) Relationships, social connection and interpersonal skills; 5) Structured routines and balanced living; 6) Self-care, household and financial management; and 7) Help-seeking and self-advocacy. Participants envisioned a modular, graded program adjunctive to psychotherapy, addressing foundational domains before values-aligned roles. Design considerations included caregiver involvement, facilitator training, and responsiveness to stigma and comorbidities. Findings provide priority domains, design and contextual considerations to inform co-production of a rehabilitation program.

papers.title: Representation and differentiation of audiology interventions within the international classification of health interventions.
papers.abstract: Standardised intervention coding supports service visibility, reimbursement, resource planning and health-system analytics. The International Classification of Health Interventions (ICHIs) provides a standardised framework for representing health interventions, but its ability to capture the breadth and clinical specificity of contemporary audiology practice requires evaluation. To evaluate the extent to which contemporary audiology interventions can be represented and differentiated within ICHI and identify limitations in coding granularity that may affect health information management, service reporting and reimbursement. An inventory of audiology interventions was derived from historical and current South African tariff schedules, scope-of-practice documents, university curricula and contemporary clinical practice. A total of 105 interventions spanning hearing and vestibular assessment, electrophysiology, device-related procedures, and counselling and rehabilitation were independently mapped to ICHI using a structured coding rubric aligned with the Target-Action-Means framework. Interrater agreement was calculated for a predefined subset. All included interventions could be represented within ICHI. Most (92.3%) demonstrated direct one-to-one alignment with an ICHI stem code. The remainder required approximate ('best-fit'), postcoordination, or composite coding using multiple descriptors and/or extension codes. Clinically distinct interventions frequently converged under identical stems, particularly within rehabilitation, counselling, device management and tele-audiology. This convergence reduced coding granularity and differentiation of clinical intent, service complexity and resource utilisation. ICHI provides broad structural coverage of contemporary audiology interventions; however, limited granularity constrains its utility for detailed health-system reporting, reimbursement modelling and service evaluation. Greater differentiation within rehabilitation- and technology-related categories is warranted to better represent contemporary audiology practice and support person-centred ear and hearing care within universal health coverage frameworks.Implications for health information management practice:High-level ICHI stems may obscure clinically meaningful variation in audiology services, reducing data precision for funding, workload measurement, service evaluation and national reporting. Implementation guidance and standardised composite coding protocols may improve specificity where existing stems are insufficient. Identified classification gaps may inform formal submissions to the World Health Organisation Family of International Classifications Network. Improved specificity could strengthen interoperability, secondary data analytics, reimbursement modelling, and evidence-based hearing-care planning.
papers.journal: Health information management : journal of the Health Information Management Association of Australia

papers.title: Oscillatory dynamics driven by nonreciprocal cross-transport.
papers.abstract: We show that nonreciprocal cross-transport can generate damped spatiotemporal oscillations in the local concentrations of non-reactive multicomponent systems. Using a minimal two-species model, we analyse the oscillatory relaxation that formally emerges when the cross-coupling coefficients have opposite signs and sufficient magnitude, provided that spatial concentration gradients are initially present. A spectral analysis of the transport operator provides the general condition for the emergence of complex eigenvalues and, in the fully antisymmetric limit, analytical expressions relating the oscillation period and damping to the cross-coupling strength and the size of the spatial domain. We further investigate this mechanism under nonequilibrium forcing by considering a system in which thermodiffusion and thermally driven natural convection act concurrently, and the cross-diffusion matrix serves as the effective cross-transport operator. In this case, thermodiffusion and convection spontaneously generate concentration gradients from initially homogeneous conditions, providing a driven environment in which nonreciprocal cross-transport can produce oscillatory concentration dynamics. This framework is discussed in connection with oscillatory scenarios recently observed in thermodiffusive multicomponent systems.

papers.title: Direct and Indirect Pathways Associated with Self-Rated Health Among Older Adults with Diabetes in China: A Path Analysis of CHARLS 2020.
papers.abstract: Using data from the fifth wave of CHARLS, this paper applies path analysis to examine the determinants and mechanisms of self-rated health among elderly diabetic patients, aiming to inform individualized clinical health management and improve patients' health and quality of life. Analyses were conducted using SPSS 27.0 and Mplus 8.3. A path analysis model was developed based on the Andersen behavioral model, and parameters were estimated with the WLSMV estimator given the categorical outcome variables. A cross-sectional study design was adopted, and the final analysis sample included 1440 elderly people diagnosed with diabetes. Among them, 835 cases (accounting for 58.0%) rated their self-health as good or average, and 605 cases (accounting for 42.0%) rated their self-health as poor. The path analytic model showed an adequate fit to the empirical data. The path coefficient indicates that the degree of pain is relatively mild (β=0.212, P<0.001), the number of comorbid chronic diseases is relatively small (β=0.400, P<0.001), there is no experience of falling (β=0.291, P=0.001), and the ability of daily activities is relatively strong (β=-0.624, P < 0.001). Elderly diabetic patients who had fewer hospitalizations in the past year (β=0.204, P<0.001), consumed alcohol (β=-0.347, P<0.001), and had longer sleep duration (β=-0.257, P<0.001) had better self-rated health conditions. Beyond their direct effects, pain, comorbidity burden, daily activity capacity, and fall history also exert indirect influences on self-rated health, mediated through three variables-hospitalization frequency, sleep duration, and alcohol consumption. The health management of elderly diabetic patients should not be limited to the regulation of blood glucose indicators. Instead, a comprehensive assessment system covering physical function maintenance, symptom relief and sleep behavior intervention should be constructed to enhance patients' subjective sense of health gain in a more targeted manner.
