papers.title: Electroacupuncture for Residual Insomnia in Remitted Depressive Disorders: Evidence Boundaries and Chronotherapeutic Hypothesis.
papers.abstract: Residual insomnia is the most common residual symptom after remission of depressive disorder and is an important marker for predicting recurrence and insufficient functional rehabilitation. Even when core depressive symptoms improve, difficulty falling asleep, nocturnal awakenings, early morning awakening, and non-restorative sleep may persist, closely linking to anxiety, reduced quality of life, and relapse risk. Thus, residual insomnia should be viewed as a clinical signal that the sleep-mood-circadian system has not yet fully stabilised. Electroacupuncture has been reported to modulate several sleep-related pathways, including the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, melatonin secretion, core clock genes, and autonomic activity. However, the current evidence base, mostly derived from animal studies, indirect mechanistic reports, or non-residual-insomnia populations, is insufficient to prove that electroacupuncture reconstructs human circadian rhythms. Most clinical trials rely on subjective scales and lack objective phase markers such as dim-light melatonin onset, cortisol curves, actigraphy, or polysomnography. This article explicitly distinguishes between "subjective sleep improvement" and "objective rhythm reconstruction". We propose a testable research framework that stratifies residual insomnia by circadian phenotypes, uses electroacupuncture as a non-photic time cue, and combines timed intervention to evaluate rhythm-restoring effects. The traditional Midnight-Noon Ebb-Flow (Ziwu Liuzhu) theory is integrated into this chrono-electroacupuncture hypothesis as a heuristic tool for symptom-time recording and protocol design. Future research should adopt rigorous phenotyping, objective circadian biomarkers, and long-term follow-up to advance electroacupuncture from empirical sleep aid towards a precise rhythm-guided intervention.

papers.title: Baseline Cognitive Status and 12-Month Response to Short-Term Spinal Cord Stimulation versus Bipolar Pulsed Radiofrequency for Zoster-Associated Pain: A Propensity Score-Matched Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: While short-term spinal cord stimulation (stSCS) and bipolar pulsed radiofrequency (bPRF) are used for zoster-associated pain (ZAP), their comparative outcomes and baseline cognition's prognostic value remain underexplored. We compared 12-month pain response and secondary pain, sleep, and cognitive outcomes at multiple follow-up visits, and explored baseline response predictors. After excluding 63 craniofacial cases from 284 retrospectively evaluated patients, 1:1 propensity score matching yielded 100 patients (50 pairs). The primary outcome was a ≥50% reduction in Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) score at 12 months. Secondary NRS, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores were analyzed using adjusted linear mixed-effects models. Ridge models with and without baseline MoCA were internally validated using 1000 matched-pair bootstrap resamples. Response rates were 66.0% with stSCS and 52.0% with bPRF (risk difference, 14.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -6.0 to 34.0; P = 0.178). stSCS was associated with lower NRS scores at 1 week and higher MoCA scores at 3, 6, and 12 months (12-month adjusted difference, 1.24; 95% CI, 0.69-1.80). PSQI differences were not significant. Higher baseline MoCA (penalized odds ratio, 2.113; bootstrap 95% CI, 1.146-3.427), higher baseline NRS, and older age were associated with response. The optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.802 versus 0.717 without MoCA. stSCS was associated with higher follow-up MoCA scores, although 12-month response rates did not differ significantly. Baseline cognition showed prognostic potential, supporting further evaluation of cognitive assessment in ZAP. The nomogram showed promising internal performance; prospective studies incorporating standardized assessment and medication monitoring are needed to confirm these findings and externally validate the model.

papers.title: Improving obstructive sleep apnea screening in patients with atrial fibrillation (SLEEP-AF project).
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) contributes to negative cardiac remodeling and worsened atrial fibrillation (AF) outcomes, yet screening remains suboptimal despite guideline recommendations. This quality improvement project aimed to improve screening, diagnosis, and treatment of OSA in patients with AF. A pre- and postintervention design evaluated an OSA screening protocol with home sleep apnea testing (HSAT) and positive airway pressure (PAP) initiation for new patients with AF in the electrophysiology (EP) clinic over 3 months. Patients were screened with an OSA questionnaire; those with elevated scores underwent HSAT coordinated by the EP clinic. Patients with moderate to severe OSA were initiated on PAP therapy. The sample included 141 patients (pre, n = 81; post, n = 60) with no significant baseline differences. The OSA screening rate increased from 49.3% to 96.7% (P < .001), and the sleep study completion rate increased from 2% to 25% over 3 months (P < .001). The mean time to diagnosis decreased from 151.5 to 22 days. 15 patients were diagnosed as having OSA; 3 initiated PAP therapy. This protocol with HSAT and PAP delivered by the EP clinic improved OSA detection and treatment. Further study is needed to understand the impact on patient outcomes.

papers.title: Durability and reconnection patterns at time of repeat ablation after first-time pulmonary vein isolation by monopolar focal pulsed field ablation.
papers.abstract: Reconnection patterns and durability after pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) or cavotricuspid isthmus block (CTIB) using monopolar focal pulsed field ablation (FPFA) at repeat ablation have not previously been evaluated. This study aimed to characterize electrophysiological findings during repeat procedures in real-world patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). Patients undergoing repeat ablation (n = 23) for symptomatic recurrent arrhythmias after first-time FPFA-guided PVI (n = 212) between October 2022 and April 2026 underwent 3-dimensional high-density mapping and ad hoc re-ablation using radiofrequency or FPFA. At index ablation, persistent AF was present in 13 of 23 (57%) patients, and CTIB was performed in 13 of 23 (57%) patients. Mean time to repeat procedure was 379 ± 282 days. Complete durable PVI was observed in 11 of 23 patients (48%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 27%-69%), corresponding to durable isolation in 74 of 94 veins (79%; 95% CI, 69%-87%). Regular atrial tachycardia was the predominant mechanism for recurrence, occurring in 17 of 23 patients (74%; 95% CI, 52%-90%). 17 conduction gaps were identified, predominantly clustered in carina regions (13 of 17 [76%]; P = .002). Reconnection occurred exclusively ipsilaterally, without significant differences between veins (17%-26%, P = .796). Durable CTIB was observed in 9 of 13 patients (69%; 95% CI, 39%-91%). After repeat ablation, 15 of 23 patients (65%; 95% CI, 43%-84%) remained free from atrial arrhythmia recurrence during 285 ± 204 days of follow-up. Approximately half of patients demonstrated durable PVI at repeat procedures. Reconnection gaps clustered mainly in carina regions, highlighting the need for further studies evaluating chronic lesion durability after PFA.

papers.title: Cardiovascular outcomes in COPD, obstructive sleep apnoea and the overlap syndrome.
papers.abstract: COPD and obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) are both independently associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. It is not clear whether this risk is further increased in COPD-OSA overlap. We aimed to determine whether COPD-OSA overlap has a higher cardiovascular burden compared with COPD or OSA alone. This was a matched cohort study using electronic health records from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum database (England). Exposures of interest were a diagnosis of COPD, OSA or both based on validated code lists. Our primary outcome of interest was cardiovascular mortality defined using ICD-10 codes. Our secondary outcomes of interest included: all-cause mortality, incident acute coronary syndrome (ACS), incident stroke and incident heart failure. The initial study cohort consisted of 365 667 people with COPD (mean±sd) age 68±11 years, 59 526 with OSA age 57±11 years and 11 040 with COPD-OSA age 65±10 years. Cardiovascular mortality was significantly higher in patients with COPD-OSA overlap compared with OSA alone (adjusted hazard ratio 1.72 (1.58-1.88); p<0.001) but not compared with COPD alone. People with COPD-OSA overlap had 27% and 58% increased risk of developing ACS compared with COPD and OSA alone respectively, and 69% and 101% increased risk of developing heart failure compared with COPD and OSA respectively. We have demonstrated that people with COPD-OSA overlap have a significantly higher cardiovascular burden compared with COPD or OSA alone with real-world implications. Earlier and targeted treatment with cardiovascular optimisation can potentially reduce downstream sequelae.

papers.title: Correction: Physiological synchrony in heart rate and electrodermal activity predicts decreased vigilant attention induced by sleep deprivation.

papers.title: Sex-related differences in cardiovascular physiology and pathology: insights from cardiac imaging.
papers.abstract: Although cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of mortality in women, CVD in women has long been understudied and underdiagnosed. This is largely based on a misconception that hearts in women are similar to those in men with regard to physiological characteristics and physiological responses. Nonetheless, in an era characterized by rapid advances in diagnostic cardiac imaging modalities, there is a greater need to understand sex differences in cardiac anatomy and function, and how these might influence CVD patterns. Such differences include observations that women have greater left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction and more pronounced LV hypertrophy compared with men using echocardiography and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) respectively. Imaging can help reveal microvascular dysfunction and heart failure, both of which have different characteristics in women compared with men. This review aims to provide a brief summary of the sex differences in cardiovascular pathophysiology among men and women observed across various imaging modalities, including echocardiography, MRI, coronary computed tomography angiography, positron emission tomography, and stress testing, while also referencing sex differences in electrophysiology with respect to cardiac anatomy.

papers.title: Quantitative trait loci associated with flowering time in wild chrysanthemum (Chrysanthemum seticuspe).
papers.abstract: The mechanisms of flowering-time (FT) regulation in cultivated chrysanthemum (Chrysanthemum morifolium) are essential for breeders owing to their significant effects on cultivation. The wild diploid Chrysanthemum seticuspe has the same short-day flowering habits as cultivated chrysanthemum. We investigated an F2 segregating population derived from crosses of accessions with differences in FT for quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping. Three major QTLs for FT were mapped, each overlapping with QTLs for other flowering traits: one QTL associated with a longer critical daylength and two QTLs linked to the ability to flower rapidly following floral transition under short-day conditions, one of which also contributes to flowering competence at high temperatures. These traits collectively influence the regulation of FT. Altered expression patterns of circadian-clock-related genes in SoS4-4, the early-flowering parental line, suggested altered rhythmicity of the circadian clock. Circadian-clock-related genes and a photoreceptor gene were also found in the FT QTL interval. These genes may be responsible for altering the circadian clock and causing variation in FT by changing the critical daylength.

papers.title: Prevalence and prognostic significance of obstructive sleep apnea in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: A prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a recognized comorbidity in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF); however, its true prevalence remains uncertain, and its prognostic implications have not been fully elucidated. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of and risk factors for OSA in patients with IPF and to evaluate its impact on disease progression. This prospective study enrolled 50 patients with IPF followed at a tertiary care center. All patients underwent polysomnography (PSG), and OSA was classified as mild, moderate, or severe. The Berlin Questionnaire and the Epworth Sleepiness Scale were administered prior to PSG. Forced vital capacity (FVC) and diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLCO) were measured at baseline and at 1 year. Disease progression was defined as a ≥10% decline in FVC and/or a ≥15% decline in DLCO. The mean age was 67.8 ± 6.7 years, and 80% were male. OSA prevalence was 90.0% (95% confidence interval: 78.2-96.7), with mild, moderate, and severe disease each present in 30% of patients. Moderate-to-severe OSA was associated with significantly greater pulmonary function decline (P = 0.030). Hypertension and high-risk status on the Berlin Questionnaire were significantly associated with the presence of OSA. OSA prevalence in IPF is remarkably high, with the majority having moderate-to-severe disease. The Berlin Questionnaire may serve as a reliable screening tool for PSG candidacy in this population. These findings suggest that OSA may contribute to functional disease progression in patients with IPF.

papers.title: Diagnostic delay length and disease severity are the main predictors of sleep apnea in acromegaly patients.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects up to 80% of patients at diagnosis of acromegaly and often persists despite treatment. Currently, patients at risk for OSA are recommended to be identified to offer polygraphy evaluation. To study the prevalence and risk factors for OSA in patients with acromegaly. Prospective, single-center study; polygraphy was performed on 36 patients with acromegaly (age 54.1 ± 12.9 years). OSA was found in 17 patients (47.2%), mostly mild (64.7%). Patients with OSA were older both at diagnosis (p = 0.02) and at polygraphy (p = 0.008), had a longer diagnostic delay (p = 0.003) and higher BMI (p = 0.03). Patients with uncontrolled acromegaly exhibited a significantly higher number of apneas (p=0.02) and obstructive apneas (p=0.04) and had significantly lower minimum oxygen saturations (p=0.02) and a higher percentage of time spent with oxygen saturation <90% (p=0.03) as compared to those with full disease control. Diagnostic delay was the best predictor of apnea-ipopnea index (AHI, p=0.04) and oxygen desaturation index (ODI, p=0.04) scores, independently on BMI. Insulin resistance (p = 0.05), glucose profile impairment (p = 0.05) and STOP-Bang score (p=0.001), but not Epworth Sleepiness Scale score (p = 0.96), were significantly higher in patients with OSA as compared to those without. Diagnostic delay and patients' age, rather than disease status, appear to predict the development of OSA and influence its severity. These findings reinforce the importance of early identification of patients at higher risk for OSA.

papers.title: Next-Generation Brain Health Monitoring Enabled by Integrated Wearable AI Infrastructure.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are difficult to detect during their pre-symptomatic stages, when intervention is most effective. Advances in wearable biosensors, artificial intelligence (AI), and neuroscience now enable continuous monitoring of brain-related physiological signals in real-world settings. However, progress in sensing technologies, signal analytics, and machine learning remains fragmented, limiting the biological specificity, robustness, and clinical translation of many digital biomarkers. This review presents an integrated framework that links molecular pathology and neural circuit dysfunction to sensor-detectable digital phenotypes across sleep, autonomic regulation, gait, speech, and ocular dynamics. We evaluate emerging wearable platforms, including bioelectric, optical, and neuromotor sensors, and discuss critical design considerations such as signal quality, user-centered form factors, and ultra-low-power edge AI systems. We further examine how self-supervised learning, federated AI, mechanistic modeling, and fairness-aware validation can improve biomarker reliability, interpretability, and generalizability. To facilitate clinical deployment, we introduce the Personalized Brain-Health Operating System (pBH-OS), a privacy-preserving reference architecture for scalable digital phenotyping. The framework maps conceptual layers to existing technologies while identifying key validation gaps. We also address practical challenges, including adherence, device dropout, informative missingness, regulatory compliance, and accountability. Together, these advances provide a pathway toward biologically grounded and regulation-ready systems capable of identifying neurodegenerative risk years before clinical symptom onset.
keywords: bio‐signal monitoring, and remote patient monitoring

papers.title: Effects of Sleep Deprivation on Oral Health: A Literature Review.
papers.abstract: Oral health and sleep health are rarely discussed in the same clinical conversation, yet the biological evidence linking them is both substantial and growing. Chronic sleep deprivation triggers a cascade of systemic disruptions, including immune dysregulation, hormonal imbalance, and oxidative stress, which leave unmistakable marks on the oral cavity. Despite this, sleep analysis remains largely absent from routine dental assessment, and its role as an independent driver of oral disease has yet to receive the clinical attention it deserves. This article provides a comprehensive narrative review of the mechanisms through which sleep deprivation compromises oral health, organized around five interconnected domains: the immunological consequences of sleep loss, including its role in periodontal destruction and impaired mucosal healing; disruptions to the salivary environment and their downstream effects on caries, xerostomia, and halitosis; behavioral and lifestyle mediators such as glycemic dysregulation, tobacco use, and caffeine consumption; neuromuscular and structural consequences encompassing bruxism, temporomandibular dysfunction, traumatic dental injuries, and dysphagia; and obstructive sleep apnea as a major oral health comorbidity that both reflects and reinforces sleep deficiency. The article further addresses the practical implications of these findings for clinical dental practice, outlining how dentists can incorporate sleep-related screening into routine assessments through validated questionnaires, anatomical risk evaluation, and recognition of characteristic oral markers, and when referral to a sleep medicine specialist is warranted. The evidence reviewed here positions sleep deprivation as a significant, independent risk factor for a broad range of oral conditions and supports the integration of sleep health into a more comprehensive, patient-centered model of dental care.

papers.title: Circadian patterns of device-detected postoperative atrial fibrillation during 2.5 years of continuous monitoring after cardiac surgery: The RACE V-Tissue Bank Study.
papers.abstract: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is common after cardiac surgery. AF in non-surgical patients exhibits distinct circadian patterns (adrenergic/daytime and vagal/nocturnal), but such patterns for new-onset POAF and recurrent AF remain undefined. This study aimed to characterize circadian AF patterns and relate chronotypes to clinical, biochemical, histological, and outcome features. Patients undergoing first cardiac surgery, with and without preoperative AF, were continuously monitored for 2.5 years with an implantable loop recorder. Early AF was defined as AF within 30 days. Patients with sustained AF (≥20 episodes) were chronotyped via circular statistics and local regression of episode duration and ventricular rate (Vrate), and classified as adrenergic, vagal, mixed, or non-rhythmic. Preoperative imaging, electrocardiography, biomarkers, and paired atrial histology were compared across chronotypes. Of the 98 patients (71 without and 27 with preoperative AF), 53 (54.1%) developed POAF (3607 episodes). Patients with prior AF showed a morning onset peak, whereas new-onset POAF showed a uniform 24-hour distribution. Of 26 patients with sustained AF, 20 were rhythmic (9 adrenergic, 7 vagal, 4 mixed), and 6 were non-rhythmic; 27 had incidental AF (<20 episodes). Rhythmic AF correlated with larger atrial volumes, prolonged PR intervals, higher bone morphogenetic protein-10 levels, and greater right-atrial endomysial fibrosis and asymmetry, most pronounced in the mixed chronotype. Adrenergic AF was associated with more arrhythmia-related emergency visits and cardioversions. AF after cardiac surgery comprises distinct circadian subtypes. New-onset POAF and recurrent AF display different circadian patterns, and individual chronotypes are associated with varying degrees of atrial remodeling and clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Commentary: The impact of 24-h shift on cardiac anesthesia fellows.
Selection of Low-Density EEG Montages for Optimal Seizure Detection Performance.
papers.abstract: Multi-channel electroencephalography (EEG) is widely recognised for its ability to non-invasively capture dynamic brain activity with high temporal resolution. However, conventional EEG systems require meticulous setup, expert interpretation and specialised infrastructure, which limits their applicability in real-time, resource-constrained environments such as critical care and emergency settings. As wearable and point-of-care EEG technologies gain traction, there is increasing demand for low-density, automated seizure detection methods that are clinically reliable and scalable. This study presents a data-driven pipeline for an EEG-based task, seizure detection, that identifies compact and clinically relevant four-channel electrode configurations. Using standard 10-20 EEG recordings, the pipeline integrates clinical domain knowledge, preprocessing, feature extraction, and ensemble boosted classification to evaluate seizure detection performance across multiple electrode combinations. The approach was validated on both a heterogeneous local paediatric EEG dataset and an open-source adult dataset. Our results show that several four-channel montages achieve robust patient-independent performance, with central and temporal electrodes frequently appearing in the top-performing configurations. These findings support the feasibility of accurate seizure detection using low-density EEG, even across diverse clinical populations. The primary contribution of this work is a generalisable pipeline for selecting compact EEG montages, which balances domain insight and data-driven optimisation. This framework can be readily adapted to other EEG-based tasks and offers a practical path toward real-time wearable EEG monitoring in resource-constrained environments.

papers.title: Health literacy and cardiovascular health in early pregnancy and postpartum.
papers.abstract: Health literacy is a key social determinant of health. Adequate health literacy has been associated with better obstetric and general adult health outcomes. However, its relationship with cardiovascular health during and after pregnancy is not well known. We aimed to estimate associations between health literacy and cardiovascular health in early pregnancy and postpartum. This is a secondary analysis of the Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring Mothers-to-be (nuMoM2b) study and its prospective follow-up phase, the nuMoM2b Heart Health Study. Participants who completed the Rapid Estimate of Adult Literacy in Medicine-Short Form (REALM-SF) in the second trimester (16-21 weeks of gestation) and a 2-7 year postpartum study visit were included. Health literacy was classified as inadequate (REALM-SF score <7) or adequate (≥7) using standard scoring procedures. The primary outcomes were cardiovascular health in early pregnancy and 2-7 years after the first birth, assessed using a modified Life's Essential 8 (LE8) score, which includes health behaviors (diet, physical activity, sleep health, and nicotine exposure) and health factors (body mass index, blood pressure, blood glucose, and lipid levels). Secondary outcomes included LE8 subcomponents. Multivariable linear regression models, which adjusted for maternal age, insurance type, and family income, were used to evaluate associations of health literacy with LE8 overall scores and its subcomponents. Among 4424 participants eligible for analysis, 3599 (81.4%) had adequate health literacy. Those with adequate health literacy were older, more likely to identify as non-Hispanic White, and more likely to have higher income, higher education, and private insurance coverage. Participants with adequate health literacy had higher early pregnancy LE8 scores (79.9 ± 13.3 vs. 73.0 ± 14.2, p < 0.001), a relationship that persisted after adjustment (aβ 3.6, 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.8-5.4). This association was driven by body mass index, diet, physical activity, and sleep subcomponents. Similarly, LE8 scores 2-7 years after birth were higher among those with adequate health literacy (80.1 ± 13.8 vs. 72.9 ± 14.6, p < 0.001; aβ 3.2, 95%, CI, 0.8-5.6), primarily due to healthier measures of body mass index, diet, physical activity, nicotine exposure, and sleep. Among nulliparous women, adequate health literacy scores in early pregnancy were associated with better cardiovascular health during pregnancy and several years after first birth.

papers.title: An exploratory study of gut microbiota and serum metabolite profiles in type 2 diabetes patients with sleep disorders.
papers.abstract: To characterize gut microbiota composition and serum metabolites in T2DM patients with and without sleep disorders. This single center cross sectional study enrolled 40 T2DM patients with sleep disorders (Group I), 40 T2DM patients without sleep disorders (Group N) and 30 age and sex matched healthy controls (Group ZC). Fecal and serum samples were collected for 16S rRNA gene sequencing and untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry metabolomics, respectively. Gut microbiota composition, serum metabolites and metabolic pathways, and microbe-metabolite correlations were analyzed. Compared with T2DM patients without sleep disorders, T2DM patients with sleep disorders showed reduced gut microbial diversity and evenness, as indicated by lower Shannon, Simpson, and Pielou's evenness indices. Beta diversity analysis showed a small but statistically significant difference in microbial structure between Groups I and N. At the genus level, nominal differences were observed between the two groups, including higher relative abundances of TM7x, Achromobacter, and Pseudomonas and lower relative abundances of Eubacterium_eligens_group, Lachnospiraceae_UCG-001, and Negativibacillus in Group I. Metabolomic results revealed 17 nominally differential metabolites between Groups I and N, involving caffeine metabolism and porphyrin and chlorophyll metabolism. Spearman analysis revealed that stercobilin abundance positively correlated with Lachnospiraceae_UCG-001 (R = 0.381, P < 0.001, Q = 0.095), Lachnospiraceae_ND3007 (R = 0.354, P = 0.002, Q = 0.121), and Odoribacter (R = 0.280, P = 0.01, Q = 0.301). T2DM patients with sleep disorders showed modest differences in gut microbial community structure and exploratory changes in serum metabolite profiles. Stercobilin and caffeine-related metabolic features may represent exploratory characteristics associated with sleep disorders in T2DM. These findings suggest potential microbiota-metabolite associations and provide a basis for future longitudinal and mechanistic studies.

papers.title: Assessment of night eating syndrome and circadian-related characteristics among university students of Rawalpindi and Islamabad.
papers.abstract: Non-communicable diseases are associated with lifestyle behaviors such as diet, meal timing, levels of stress, quality of sleep, and disruption of circadian rhythms. Night Eating Syndrome (NES) is an abnormal eating behavior characterized by eating at night and/or eating after the last meal of the day. NES may be associated with sleep disturbances and/or circadian-related characteristics. University students are particularly susceptible to the development of NES due to academic stress, irregular schedules, increased exposure to screens, and late nights. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and severity of Night Eating Syndrome and to examine the relationships between Night Eating Syndrome and sleep-related characteristics, circadian-related characteristics (diurnal preference), and mood among university students in Rawalpindi and Islamabad, Pakistan. A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted on 335 undergraduate university students at four universities in Rawalpindi and Islamabad using a multistage sampling method. Data were collected using structured questionnaires including sociodemographic questions, the Night Eating Diagnostic Questionnaire, and the Sleep, Circadian Rhythm, and Mood questionnaire. Data analysis was performed using SPSS Version 27. Descriptive statistics, one-way ANOVA, Welch's ANOVA with Games-Howell post-hoc comparisons, multiple linear regression, Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test, and Pearson chi-square test were used, with significance set at p < 0.05. The Prevalence of Night Eating Syndrome was 6% (n = 18; 95% CI: 3.2-8.4%). Severity-based classification showed that 51.0% had normal scores, 26.3% had mild symptoms, 17.3% had moderate symptoms, and 6% met the NEDQ criteria for NES. There were significant differences between NES severity groups in Morningness and Good Sleep scores (p < 0.001), while there were no significant differences in Depressed Mood scores (p = 0.159). In adjusted regression models, NES status was significantly associated with Good Sleep scores, while sex was associated with Morningness and BMI was associated with Depressed Mood. BMI category was significantly associated with NES status (Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test, p = 0.002) and NES severity (p < 0.001). Night Eating Syndrome and related symptoms were present among university students, with increasing symptom severity associated with differences in Morningness and Good Sleep scores, while Depressed Mood did not differ significantly across severity categories. These findings suggest the possible significance of health promotion initiatives conducted through universities emphasizing good sleep hygiene, regular meal time and early identification of night eating symptoms.

papers.title: Natural products in insomnia: Molecular mechanisms, action targets, and therapeutic potential.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is a disorder characterized by sleep disturbances and daytime impairments. It can be alleviated with conventional clinical medications, but considerable individual variability and adverse effects (AEs) remain persistent challenges. Many natural products are known for their low toxicity and multi-target properties. These products offer distinct advantages in treating insomnia by modulating its underlying pathological mechanisms. Although previous reviews have summarized the effects of natural products on insomnia, systematic classification based on natural products and comprehensive exploration of their interactions with multidimensional pathological mechanisms remain insufficient. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms by which natural products modulate insomnia. It also offers an in-depth discussion of the current limitations and challenges. The goal is to establish a theoretical foundation and technical framework to optimize treatment strategies and advance the clinical translation of natural product research.

papers.title: Sequence effects and SSD are associated with N2 and P3 signals during stopping in a visual stop signal task.
papers.abstract: Studies combining the stop signal task (SST) with Electroencephalogram (EEG) have often asked whether the frontocentral N2 and P3 components are influenced by failed versus successful stopping. Estimates of the N2 and P3 commonly reflect averages across experimental trials per individual allowing for assessing mean-level effects. The probability of responding to a stop trial is influenced by task parameters such as the stop signal delay and the asymmetric presentation frequency of Go and Stop trials. Trial-by-trial variation in task parameters like the stop signal delay have been shown to influence brain activity differences between stop outcomes in fMRI data but have not been investigated in EEG data. Changes in the global frequency of Go and Stop trials have been shown to influence behavioral performance and the N2 and P3 components but potential influences of local sequential dependencies that may arise on a trial-by-trial basis have simply been ignored. It is possible that both the SSD and local sequential dependencies arising from past trial histories systematically influence N2 and P3 amplitudes or latencies during stopping. This study used mixed effects modeling to assess associations between SSD, sequential dependencies, and single trial estimates of latency and amplitude of the N2 and P3 components during failed and successful stopping. We specified interactions between both predictor variables and the two stop outcomes. The results showed complex curvilinear associations between the latency of the N2 and P3 components with SSD. Longer SSDs were associated with shorter latencies while only the N2 showed significant interaction with stop outcomes. Sequential dependencies were significantly associated with the N2 and P3 amplitudes. A longer series of go trials was associated with more negative N2 amplitudes and more positive P3 amplitudes. The N2 amplitude was larger after having recently encountered a stop trial, while the P3 amplitude increased at a similar rate during both failed and successful stopping. Together, these results indicate that accounting for the influence of SSD and sequential dependencies on ERP estimates of the N2 and P3 components is of high importance, particularly in studies comparing clinical to healthy control participants.

papers.title: Contralateral delay activity during dynamic spatial updates in working memory.
papers.abstract: Working memory (WM) enables us to maintain and directly manipulate mental representations, yet we know little about the neural implementation of this privileged online format. We recorded electroencephalography data as human subjects engaged in a task requiring continuous updates to the locations of objects retained in WM as well as in a visually identical task with WM demands removed. Analysis of neural data suggested WM-related contralateral delay activity reversed polarity as objects held in WM moved to the opposite hemifield. The control task suggested this was partially but not fully explained by visual attention demands. Thus, the spatial location of activity related to both attention and WM was updated to meet behavioral demands as the spatial location of remembered objects changed.

papers.title: Synthesized cardiometabolic, pulmonary, and sleep outcomes after bariatric surgery in adolescents with severe obesity: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: To synthesize cardiometabolic, pulmonary, sleep-related, anthropometric, and safety outcomes after metabolic and bariatric surgery in adolescents with severe obesity. This was a systematic review and meta-analysis conducted according to PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261354795). Five databases were searched for studies of adolescents aged approximately 10-19 years undergoing recognized metabolic or bariatric procedures. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analysis was used when studies were sufficiently comparable. Of 5110 records, 147 reports representing 101 unique studies or cohorts published from 1995 to 2026 were included. Follow-up ranged from 30 days to approximately 15 years. Across three independent randomized cohorts, surgery reduced body mass index by 9.39 kg/m2 at 2 years versus non-surgical care (95% CI -13.90 to -4.89; I2 = 88%; low certainty). Randomized evidence indicated lower triglycerides (mean difference -0.36 mmol/L, 95% CI -0.57 to -0.14; low certainty), whereas blood-pressure effects were indeterminate (very low certainty). Observational cohorts reported improvement or remission of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and obstructive sleep apnea. Weight reduction was durable after gastric bypass and sleeve gastrectomy but smaller and less durable after gastric banding. Repeat objective sleep testing was reported in three studies and postoperative spirometry in one. No included report documented use of a validated asthma-control instrument, ambulatory blood-pressure monitoring, or vascular imaging as a pre- and postoperative outcome; diastolic function was reported once; diastolic function was reported once. Perioperative mortality and serious 30-day complications were uncommon, whereas reoperation and micronutrient deficiency remained important during extended follow-up. Metabolic and bariatric surgery produces large body mass index reductions and multisystem improvement in adolescents with severe obesity; serious short-term complications and perioperative mortality were uncommon, but lifelong nutritional and multidisciplinary surveillance remains important. Most effect estimates remain uncertain, particularly for objective long-term sleep and pulmonary outcomes.

papers.title: The electro-MICA toolbox for integrating electrophysiology within multimodal imaging and connectomics workflows.
papers.abstract: The integration of electrophysiological recordings with multimodal neuroimaging data holds great promise for advancing our understanding of brain function and neurological disorders. To facilitate this endeavor, we present electro-MICA, an open-access Python toolbox designed to project electrophysiological features from scalp and intracranial electroencephalography (EEG) onto cortical and hippocampal surfaces generated by validated multimodal imaging ecosystems. The toolbox comprises two pipelines: one for intracranial EEG (iEEG) recorded with stereo-EEG depth electrodes and one for scalp EEG source localization. Both pipelines are grounded in numerical solutions to the electromagnetic equations governing electric activity in the brain, solved using the Boundary Element Method. A key methodological contribution is the use of a current density double layer model for neural generators, which avoids the mathematical singularities introduced by conventional dipole-based models when electrodes are near the cortical surface, a situation that can arise in iEEG. Electrode contacts are additionally modeled with non-zero length, improving physical realism. Scalp EEG source localization is performed using eLORETA on a subject-specific three-layer head model derived from the anatomical input. Validation against empirical gamma-band iEEG data from 32 subjects demonstrates that the distributed generator model outperforms both distance-based and dipole-based alternatives. An illustrative clinical example demonstrates the toolbox's capacity to reveal associations between intracranial spike rates, cortical thickness, and anatomical connectivity in an epilepsy patient. Electro-MICA requires no parameter selection from the user, facilitating straightforward multimodal analyses. The toolbox is available at http://github.com/MICA-MNI/electromica with extensive online documentation at http://electromica.readthedocs.io.

papers.title: Explainable machine learning for identifying high-risk Alzheimer's disease and key health characteristics among community-dwelling adults.
papers.abstract: To develop an interpretable machine learning model to identify individuals with AD8-defined high-risk status for Alzheimer's disease among community-dwelling adults, identify key health characteristics and their association patterns with high-risk status, and to inform community-based cognitive health promotion. Based on health survey data from 6,267 community-dwelling adults, AD8-defined high-risk status for Alzheimer's disease was assessed using the Alzheimer's Disease Screening Scale (AD8). LASSO logistic regression, random forest, and decision tree models were constructed, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to analyze the importance of key health characteristics and their association patterns. A total of 6,267 community-dwelling adults were included, of whom 1,454 (23.2%) were classified into the AD8-defined high-risk group. The random forest model showed the highest discriminative performance among the three models. SHAP analysis indicated that fruit intake, age, snoring, mean grip strength, and sleep duration were important health characteristics associated with AD8-defined high-risk status for Alzheimer's disease. SHAP dependence plots further revealed a graded negative association between fruit intake and high-risk status, a U-shaped association for sleep duration, a U-shaped association for mean grip strength, and a positive graded association between snoring frequency and high-risk status. Random forest combined with SHAP identified key health characteristics associated with AD8-defined high-risk status among community-dwelling adults and revealed non-linear association patterns involving health behaviors and physical function. These findings may provide useful information for community-based risk stratification and targeted cognitive health promotion.

papers.title: Digital biomarkers derived from wearable and portable devices in prodromal Parkinson's disease and at-risk populations: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: Prodromal Parkinson's disease (pPD) represents a pre-diagnostic stage during which subtle and heterogeneous changes may be difficult to detect through conventional clinical assessments. Digital biomarkers derived from wearable or portable devices offer opportunities for objective and longitudinal assessment. This scoping review aimed to map the current evidence on digital biomarkers in individuals with formally defined pPD or populations at increased risk of Parkinson's disease (PD), focusing on measurement approaches, analytical methods, types of evidence, and methodological gaps. A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and ACM Digital Library was conducted from database inception to August 31, 2026. Studies investigating digital biomarkers derived from wearable or portable devices in individuals with formally defined pPD or populations at increased risk of PD were included. Study characteristics, digital biomarker domains, measurement and analytical approaches, and types of evidence were synthesized descriptively. Forty-three studies were included, primarily involving individuals with iRBD or other high-risk states associated with α-synucleinopathies, population-based or broader prodromal-risk cohorts, genetic high-risk populations, and individuals with idiopathic hyposmia/anosmia. Digital biomarkers encompassed motor, speech, sleep/activity, and multidomain features, with motor-related measures, particularly gait and mobility, being the most extensively investigated. Machine-learning approaches were applied across several domains, whereas genuinely multidomain studies remained limited. Most studies provided cross-sectional evidence of group differences or discriminative performance, whereas prospective evidence regarding future PD diagnosis or phenoconversion was less extensive. Considerable heterogeneity was observed in measurement protocols, analytical approaches, and validation strategies. Wearable- and portable-device-derived digital biomarkers represent promising candidate tools for characterizing and monitoring individuals across the prodromal PD risk spectrum. However, evidence supporting clinical prediction of phenoconversion remains limited by methodological heterogeneity and a lack of sufficient longitudinal and external validation. Future research should prioritize standardized assessment, large, multicenter longitudinal cohorts, independent external validation, and integration with established clinical and biological markers.

papers.title: Digitally delivered full plate living: associations with diet quality, body mass index, and participant-reported health measures among participants with paired assessments.
papers.abstract: Nutrition counseling is often limited by time, staffing, and resources. Full Plate Living (FPL) is a free, self-guided digital nutrition program that encourages a whole food, plant predominant, fiber-rich eating pattern. This study examined baseline-to-follow-up changes in diet quality, body mass index (BMI), dietary fiber intake, and participant-reported health measures among adults with eligible paired Diet ID/FPL assessments. This secondary analysis used de-identified observational records from July 2023 through January 2026. Baseline was the first available record, and follow-up was the first subsequent record at least 60 days later. Baseline characteristics were compared between participants with and without eligible paired records. Within-participant changes were evaluated using paired analyses, with Bonferroni-adjusted sensitivity analyses for multiple outcomes. Regression analyses examined whether follow-up interval was associated with outcome change. Among 4,359 participants with 7,077 records, 392 (9.0%) had eligible paired records. The paired-assessment cohort was predominantly female (87.5%), White (81.1%), mean age was 57.7 years. Compared with participants without eligible follow-up records, paired-assessment participants were older and had higher diet quality and dietary fiber intake and lower estimated energy intake. Among participants with paired data, Diet ID Quality Score increased from 7.20 to 7.91 (Cohen d=0.26), Healthy Eating Index-2015 increased from 73.87 to 80.24 (d=0.27), BMI decreased from 31.62 to 31.03 kg/m² (d=-0.17), and dietary fiber intake increased by 5.0 g/d (d=0.28). After Bonferroni adjustment, improvements in diet quality, healthy food choice confidence, weight-loss confidence, energy level, general health, dietary fiber intake, and food group measures remained significant, along with the modest BMI reduction; sleep duration category did not remain significant. Longer follow-up interval was weakly associated with smaller improvements in Healthy Eating Index-2015 and dietary fiber intake and was not associated with BMI change. DISCUSSION: Among participants with eligible paired assessments, baseline-to-follow-up improvements were observed in diet quality, dietary fiber intake, participant-reported health measures, food group measures, and BMI; effect sizes were small. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory repeated-observation changes rather than causal evidence of program effectiveness. These findings may guide evaluation of FPL as a no-cost digital nutrition resource for individuals, clinics, and communities.

papers.title: Wave-function formalism for evolving neural dynamics: a mathematical framework informed by EEG.
papers.abstract: The organization of distributed neural activity remains one of the central challenges in computational neuroscience. Contemporary frameworks, including Integrated Information Theory, Global Workspace Theory, entropy-based approaches, and electromagnetic field theories, have advanced our understanding of neural coordination but employ different mathematical descriptions of large-scale brain dynamics. This study investigates whether wave-function formalism provides a useful mathematical framework for representing evolving neural dynamics measured using electroencephalography (EEG). Rather than introducing a new electrophysiological measure or proposing a new mechanism of consciousness, the framework represents complementary EEG observables within a common state-space description of neural activity. Mathematical inspiration is drawn from Everett's representation of evolving state spaces, although no claims are made regarding quantum computation or quantum processes in the brain. Electroencephalographic recordings from interictal, preictal, and ictal seizure states (150 EEG segments) were analyzed using complementary measures of signal amplitude, spectral organization, entropy, phase dynamics, cross-frequency coupling, and recurrence quantification. Statistical comparisons employed nonparametric analyses, effect-size estimation, confidence intervals, and post hoc testing. Significant differences were observed across all major electrophysiological domains. Ictal recordings exhibited increased signal amplitude, redistribution of spectral power toward lower frequencies, reduced entropy, altered phase organization, changes in cross-frequency coupling, and increased recurrence structure, indicating coordinated changes in evolving neural dynamics during seizure progression. These findings are interpreted within a mathematical framework that treats established EEG observables as complementary descriptors of a single evolving neural state. The principal contribution of this work is the proposal of a mathematically grounded and experimentally testable representation of evolving neural dynamics. Whether this formalism provides new insight into cognition or conscious experience remains an empirical question for future investigation.

papers.title: Influencing the exposome, patient macroenvironment, tumor microenvironment through-line to improve clinical outcomes.
papers.abstract: Previous studies have identified an association between a tumor microenvironment characterized by a predominance of T helper cell type 2 (Th2) system cells (Th2 cells, M2 macrophages, innate lymphoid cells type 2), regulatory T cells, and myeloid derived suppressor cells with poorer cancer prognosis. In contrast, a tumor microenvironment characterized by Th1 system cells (Th1 cells, M1 macrophages, natural killer cells, CD8+ cells, innate lymphoid cells type 1) is associated with a more favorable prognosis. T2-high asthma, a quintessential Th2-dominance-based disease, is associated epidemiologically with more than double the incidence of lung, breast, prostate, and colon cancers, suggesting a connection between the Th2 immune dominant patient macroenvironment and the Th2 immune dominant tumor microenvironment. Stress, air pollution, toxicants, sleep disruption, obesity, and many other influences from the exposome are known to drive the patient into Th2 dominance. Thus, the authors hypothesize that there is a through-line connecting the exposome, patient macroenvironment, and tumor microenvironment. With this context in mind, specific defects in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle produce oncometabolites that drive oncogenic development in tissues. However these same TCA cycle defects drive macrophages to the M1 phenotype, which activates the Th1 system. Th1 system cells are responsible for clearance of oncogenically transformed cells. This should represent a check against the oncogenic influence of the oncometabolites created by the TCA cycle breaks. The authors hypothesize that, in Th2 dominant patients, the TCA cycle breaks fail to shift macrophages to the M1 phenotype, the Th1 system fails to upregulate, and the normal check against oncogenic development fails to occur. If confirmed by subsequent studies, this model may help explain the more than doubled incidence of common cancers in asthma and potentially other Th2 atopic diseases. The authors discuss clinical implications and approaches for operationalizing existing knowledge of the exposome and its impact on patient immunology.

papers.title: Sex differences in sleep and memory relationships in older adults at risk for Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Biological sex is an important modifier of aging and Alzheimer's disease risk, yet the sleep-related mechanisms through which sex and genetic risk interact to influence memory remain poorly understood. We examined whether associations among non-rapid eye movement sleep physiology, overnight memory retention, and apolipoprotein E ϵ4 (APOE ϵ4) status, a genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's disease, differed by sex in cognitively unimpaired older adults enriched for Alzheimer's disease risk. Eighty participants completed overnight polysomnography with high-density electroencephalography, and 65 also completed an evening encoding/immediate recall and morning delayed recall word-pair memory task. Overnight memory retention did not differ by sex. However, exploratory analyses of the proportional overnight retention measure suggested a sex × APOE ϵ4 interaction, such that female APOE ϵ4 carriers may exhibit reduced overnight forgetting relative to female non-carriers and male carriers. Although counterintuitive, this pattern may reflect compensatory or resilience-related sleep-memory mechanisms in cognitively unimpaired women at genetic risk for Alzheimer's disease rather than a protective effect of APOE ϵ4 itself. Women spent more time in N3 sleep and had higher non-rapid eye movement delta and slow sigma power than men. Sleep-memory associations also differed by sex: greater N2 duration was more strongly associated with better overnight retention in men, whereas greater frontal slow sigma power and fronto-central fast sigma power were positively associated with retention in women. Exploratory APOE-stratified analyses suggested sex-specific differences in sleep stage-memory relationships, with more positive N2-memory associations in male than female APOE ϵ4 carriers and more positive N3-memory associations in female than male carriers; both differences remained significant after FDR correction. TFCE-corrected analyses further identified positive associations between NREM delta and sigma activity and overnight memory retention in female APOE ϵ4 carriers. These findings highlight sex-specific patterns in NREM sleep physiology and sleep-memory relationships in cognitively unimpaired older adults at risk for Alzheimer's disease. More broadly, the results suggest that sex and APOE ϵ4 status may jointly shape the neurophysiological pathways linking sleep and memory, underscoring the importance of considering sex as a biological variable when studying sleep, cognitive aging, and Alzheimer's disease vulnerability.

papers.title: Breaking limits: rapid sea-to-summit ascent of Mount Everest (8,848 m) in 3 days 23 hours following normobaric-hypoxic pre-acclimatization and staged supplemental oxygen in a non-elite athlete.
papers.abstract: Traditional ascent of Mount Everest (8,848 m) typically requires 40-50 days of on-mountain acclimatization. Normobaric hypoxia (NH) pre-acclimatization is a practical home-based alternative; however, no peer-reviewed case report has described a sea-to-summit Everest ascent completed in under four days by a non-elite individual without prior on-mountain acclimatization rotations. A 40-year-old male recreational mountaineer (baseline VO2max 40.8 ml·kg-1·min-1; BMI 30.1 kg·m-2) completed an 18-week structured NH pre-acclimatization program comprising 48 nights of hypoxic sleep (~377 h at simulated altitudes of 1,850-5,486 m; FiO2 16.7-10.5%) and 16 hypoxic exercise sessions (34 h at 3,085-6,000 m; FiO2 14.3-9.8%). Hypoxic dose was calculated as Σ[(95/SpO2 - 1) × h × 100]. During the climb, peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) and heart rate (HR) were recorded at each camp, and acute mountain sickness (AMS) was assessed using the 2018 Lake Louise Score (LLS). Supplemental oxygen (O2) was initiated at 0.5 L·min-1 at the start of the ascent from Everest Base Camp (EBC, 5,360 m) and titrated to SpO2 and symptoms up to 3.0 L·min-1 during the summit push. The program yielded a combined hypoxic exposure of 411 h and a cumulative hypoxic dose of 4,779%·h (sleep 4,353%·h; exercise 426%·h). VO2max increased from 40.8 to 51.0 ml·kg-1·min-1, and body mass decreased from 118.1 to 101.5 kg. The subject departed New York at 00:30 local time (EDT; 10:15 Nepal Standard Time, NST) on 15 May 2025 and reached the summit at 09:22 NST on 19 May 2025, a total sea-to-summit time of 3 days, 23 hours and 7 minutes; the ascent from EBC to the summit took 60 hours and 22 minutes. SpO2 was 75% at Camp 3 (7,100 m; HR 95 bpm) and 70% on arrival at Camp 4 (7,950 m; HR 105 bpm) and at the summit (HR 105 bpm). On descent, SpO2 recovered to 80% at Camp 4 and 85% at Camp 2 (6,750 m; HR 110 bpm), and was 85% on room air on return to EBC (HR 62 bpm). No AMS was diagnosed during the ascent (LLS 0-1 at all ascending checkpoints); mild AMS criteria were met on descent (LLS = 3), resolving by return to EBC. No high-altitude cerebral or pulmonary edema occurred. To our knowledge, this case documents the fastest recorded sea-to-summit ascent of Mount Everest by a non-professional athlete. The combination of a structured 18-week NH pre-acclimatization program, objective physiological monitoring, and staged supplemental oxygen, together with the absence of severe altitude-related complications, suggests that rapid ascent without traditional on-mountain acclimatization may be feasible in a well-prepared, closely supervised non-elite individual. Controlled prospective studies are required to quantify the relative contributions of hematological, ventilatory, and mitochondrial adaptations induced by high-dose NH exposure.

papers.title: Regular napping mitigates the onset of cognitive fatigue and protects against stress-inflammatory responses to real-world sleep debt.
papers.abstract: Chronic sleep debt impairs cognitive processes, stress regulation, and immune homeostasis, while sustained cognitive engagement induces mental fatigue. However, it remains unclear how chronically insufficient sleep in real-life conditions accelerates the onset of mental fatigue during prolonged cognitive activity-and whether daytime napping can buffer these effects. This study investigated the combined effects of chronic sleep debt and extended cognitive engagement on cognitive fatigue and salivary neuro-immune and neurotrophic markers in an ecologically valid context. Compared with controls, participants with chronic sleep debt showed pronounced declines in Psychomotor Vigilance Task performance (reaction time and number of lapses) across both time-on-task and time-on-week and showed higher commission rates in the executive Go-NoGo task. These morning impairments were partially attenuated in the participants who practiced afternoon chronic naps, and the reduction in lapses was correlated with nap frequency. Biologically, chronic sleep debt was associated with a blunted morning cortisol response, an increase in IL-1β and IL-6, and a reduction in BDNF levels, but not observed in either the Control or Sleep-Debt + Nap groups. In the Sleep-Debt group, IL-1β levels were positively correlated with sustained attention deficits. Chronic sleep debt increased attentional fatigability without exacerbating executive decline, an effect that may be driven by neuro-inflammatory processes and effectively alleviated by regular daytime napping. Importantly, these findings indicate that chronic afternoon napping may confer protective and long-lasting restorative benefits observable in morning assessments, reflecting effects that persist over a 24-h period.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics reveal the impact of different light spectra on lateral branching and growth of medicinal plant Artemisia argyi.
papers.abstract: Light quality is a decisive environmental regulator of growth and secondary metabolism in medicinal plants, yet the spectral requirements of Artemisia argyi, a species prized for bioactive metabolites such as artemisinin, eupatilin, and jaceosidin, remain poorly defined. This study integrated physiological, transcriptomic, and metabolomic analyses to evaluate the response of A. argyi to 4 weeks of supplemental light-emitting diode (LED) lighting of three spectral compositions: blue-red (BR, 3:1), red-blue (RB, 3:1), and white (control), with three biological replicates per treatment. Physiologically, BR light produced the tallest stems, the largest and densest foliage, and the greatest stem diameter, shoot fresh and dry weight, and number of lateral branches; relative to RB and white light, plant height increased by 109%, 100%, 78%, and 8.6% and leaf number by 51.61%, 58.33%, 37.20%, and 4.2% across weeks 1-4, accompanied by higher antioxidant enzyme activity and reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels. RNA sequencing yielded 44.18-50.75 million raw reads per sample with a mapping ratio of 83.47%-87.06% and Q30 > 94%. Pairwise analysis identified 2,025 differentially expressed genes (DEGs; 1,173 upregulated and 852 downregulated) for BR vs. RB, 974 (652 upregulated and 322 downregulated) for BR vs. white, and 601 (141 upregulated and 460 downregulated) for RB vs. white, enriched in light-responsive, photosystem, chlorophyll- and proline-metabolism and circadian pathways. Key regulators included the two-component response regulator-like APRR1 (a CheY-like phosphoacceptor), proline dehydrogenase (ProDH), the chlorophyll b reductase NOL, and terpenoid-backbone (isoprene) genes. Metabolomic profiling detected 174, 129, and 81 differentially accumulated metabolites in BR vs. RB, BR vs. white, and RB vs. white, respectively, with 486 metabolites up- and 459 downregulated in BR vs. RB and pronounced enrichment of amino acid, carbohydrate, lipid, and secondary-metabolite (flavonoid, terpenoid, and alkaloid) biosynthesis. Collectively, these results demonstrate that BR supplemental light coordinately enhances growth, lateral branching, and bioactive-compound biosynthesis, offering a practical basis for the precision cultivation of A. argyi and the targeted production of its medicinal compounds.

papers.title: Editorial: Understanding conscious experiences during sleep.
Latent class analysis of intrinsic capacity and its association with quality of life in hospitalized older people with stroke: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify latent classes of intrinsic capacity among hospitalized older people with stroke and to examine the associations of these classes with stroke-specific quality of life. A cross-sectional design was used, and 314 hospitalized older people with stroke were consecutively recruited. Stroke severity was assessed using the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), comorbidity burden using the Age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index (ACCI), perceived social support using the Perceived Social Support Scale (PSSS), intrinsic capacity across five domains using the Intrinsic Capacity Assessment Tool, and stroke-specific quality of life using the Stroke-Specific Quality of Life Scale (SS-QOL). Latent class analysis identified intrinsic-capacity profiles, and multivariable logistic regression was used to examine factors associated with latent-class membership, and ANOVA was used to compare SS-QOL scores across the identified classes. LCA identified three latent classes of intrinsic capacity among hospitalized older people with stroke: the low motor-low vitality group (27.70%), the low cognitive-moderate vitality, psychological, and sensory group (17.20%), and the function maintenance group (55.10%). Multinomial logistic regression showed that age, stroke severity, sleep duration, and social support were associated with membership in the low motor-low vitality group, whereas education level was associated with membership in the low cognitive-moderate vitality, psychological, and sensory group. Significant differences were observed in most stroke-specific quality-of-life domains across the identified groups (p < 0.05). Three distinct intrinsic-capacity profiles were identified among hospitalized older people with stroke, and these profiles were associated with different levels of stroke-specific quality of life. Both clinical and psychosocial factors were associated with profile membership, highlighting the need for targeted interventions to preserve intrinsic capacity and improve quality of life.

papers.title: Wearable-derived sleep and circadian features associated with electronic health record-documented persistent postsurgical pain.
papers.abstract: A substantial percentage of surgical patients develop persistent postsurgical pain, and sleep disruption is an established, modifiable contributor. We examined temporal dynamics linking sleep and circadian rhythms to persistent postsurgical pain, using longitudinal Fitbit and electronic health record (EHR) data from the NIH All of Us Research Program to track sleep and circadian changes preceding EHR documentation of pain beyond expected surgical recovery. Patients later documented with persistent pain showed systematic shifts in wake timing and in heart rate circadian rhythms (elevated amplitude and mesor), with wake timing decoupled from heart rate circadian timing. These changes were absent in a comparison cohort without persistent pain documentation, indicating specificity to persistent postsurgical pain rather than a postoperative or clinical-encounter effect. Findings align with evidence linking altered sleep to pain outcomes and identify cardiac circadian disruption as a distinct marker, suggesting wearable-derived features could capture physiological changes before documentation and inform intervention.

papers.title: Maternal Microvascular Calcium Sparks Are Reduced in Preeclampsia.
papers.abstract: Maternal microvascular dysfunction is a hallmark of the hypertensive pregnancy disorder preeclampsia, but the mechanism(s) have not been fully defined. Within vascular smooth muscle cells, the principal pressure-induced vasodilatory pathway depends on localized Ca2+-release events from the sarcoplasmic reticulum ryanodine receptors (Ca2+ sparks), which stimulate BKCa (large-conductance Ca2+-activated potassium channels) to cause spontaneous transient outward currents and vasorelaxation. Here, the Ca2+ sparks-BKCa axis is assessed in preeclampsia for the first time. Pressurized omental resistance arteries from normotensive pregnant women and women with preeclampsia were imaged by high-speed spinning-disk laser confocal microscopy to assess Ca2+ sparks (20-110 mm Hg) and caffeine-evoked Ca2+ release (10 mmol/L; 80 mm Hg). Electrophysiology was used to assess spontaneous transient outward currents (-60 to 0 mV) and BKCa currents (-100 to +100 mV) in isolated vascular smooth muscle cells. A liquid chromatography-selected reaction monitoring-tandem mass spectrometry assay measured SERCA2 (sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase-2) and unphosphorylated/phosphorylated proteoforms of regulatory PLN (phospholamban). Vasoactive effects of the BKCa-dependent vasorelaxant HBD2 (human β-defensin-2; 0.01-10 nmol/L) were assessed by wire myography. In microvascular arteries from women with preeclampsia, there was reduced Ca2+ spark frequency (P=1.1×10-10) and spontaneous transient outward current frequency (P=0.023). There was also reduced sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ release in response to caffeine (P=0.0013), reduced sarcoplasmic reticulum refilling (P=2.0×10-4), and decreased ratio of SERCA2 to inhibitory unphosphorylated PLN (P=0.030), implicating increased SERCA2 inhibition. HBD2 (0.01-10 nmol/L) caused BKCa-dependent relaxation (P=4.6×10-10) of omental arteries without affecting Ca2+ spark frequency. In microvascular arteries from women with preeclampsia, there is a striking reduction in Ca2+ spark frequency and spontaneous transient outward currents, likely secondary to increased inhibition of SERCA2 by unphosphorylated PLN and reduced sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ load. These defects may provide novel therapeutic targets to restore physiological control of the vasculature. BKCa-mediated relaxation by HBD2 was independent of Ca2+ sparks, supporting vasodilatory strategies bypassing disrupted microvascular mechanisms in preeclampsia.

papers.title: [Quantitative electron microscopic assessment of the mitochondrial apparatus of hepatocytes during aging: Effect of constant illumination and melatonin correction.].
papers.abstract: Chronic circadian rhythm disruption, particularly constant light exposure (dark deprivation), is considered a factor that accelerates aging. However, the role of mitochondrial dysfunction in this process and the possibilities of its pharmacological correction remain insufficiently understood. The aim of this study was to perform a quantitative ultrastructural assessment of the mitochondrial apparatus of rat hepatocytes during aging under constant light exposure and with exogenous melatonin supplementation. Male Wistar rats (n=480), starting from 3 months of age, were divided into three groups: control (10:14 h light/dark cycle), constant light group, and constant light group with melatonin added to drinking water (12 mg/L, 5 times/week). At 6, 12, 18, and 24 months of age, electron microscopic examination of the liver was performed with assessment of numerical density, area, perimeter, cristae count, form factor (circularity, C), and mitochondrial inner membrane coefficient (MIMC). Constant light exposure induced progressive accelerated mitochondrial aging: decreased numerical density, cristae number and length, organelle deformation, and massive hepatocyte death by 24 months. Melatonin administration prevented these alterations: the form factor was maintained at 0.80, while mitochondrial density and cristae count remained comparable to control. Chronic desynchronosis induces mitochondrial dysfunction as a key mechanism of accelerated liver aging. Exogenous melatonin exerts a potent mitochondria-protective effect, stabilizing the ultrastructure and energy apparatus of hepatocytes, which substantiates its further investigation as a geroprotector in circadian disorders.

papers.title: Neurophysiological and Behavioural Effects of Combined Cannabis Concentrates and Alcohol Among People Who Regularly Use Alcohol and Cannabis.
papers.abstract: Increasingly potent concentrated cannabis products containing high levels of Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) are being consumed with alcohol. This combination is known to acutely impair cognitive and psychomotor abilities, although few studies have evaluated alcohol and cannabis co-use using neural measures. This naturalistic feasibility study explored the acute effects of co-intoxication on behavioural performance and brain activity, measured via electroencephalography (EEG), during a performance monitoring task administered three times over a 4.5-h period. Participants (N = 17, 65% male) were heavy drinking community members (age M = 31.7 years; SD = 10.27) who regularly use cannabis. EEG was recorded while participants completed a speeded visual-flanker task at baseline (sober) before consuming a standardized dose of alcohol and a cannabis concentrate product, followed by EEG recordings 1-h (intoxicated) and 4-h post co-consumption (recovery). Recordings were processed to obtain six event-related potential components: the stimulus-locked N1, P2, N2 and P3 and response-locked error-related negativity (ERN) and error positivity (Pe). Repeated measures ANOVAs revealed that behavioural measures at the intoxicated timepoint showed an increase in errors (p < 0.005; η2 p = 0.35) and significant decrease in response time (RT) (p < 0.001; η2 p = 0.50) compared to sober and recovery periods. Measures of brain activity also demonstrated significant change across time with largest amplitudes when sober, smaller amplitudes when intoxicated, then an increase in amplitude to near sober levels at recovery for stimulus-locked (P2, N2 and P3) and response-locked components (ERN and Pe). Thus, compared to sober and recovery periods, the behaviour at the intoxicated timepoint revealed significantly greater impulsivity (RT) leading to significantly higher error rates, while measures of cognitive processing (i.e., decision-making, error detection, performance monitoring/adaptation) showed significantly diminished levels of brain activity. Performance and neurophysiology measures remained diminished at recovery compared to baseline. Understanding neurocognitive functioning during co-intoxication may provide insights into specific cognitive processes that may impact function in everyday activities such as driving. Trial Registration: NCT06259916.

papers.title: Predicting organ age with multimodal data identifies ageing-associated plasma proteins and behavioural traits.
papers.abstract: Ageing progresses unevenly across organs, making it difficult to capture organ-specific physiological decline using a single organism-level measure. We developed a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts framework integrating MRI and anthropometric measurements to estimate brain, heart, liver and pancreas age in 46 734 individuals. Organ age gap (OAG) was defined as predicted age minus chronological age. UK Biobank proteomic, behavioural, disease and phenotypic data were used to characterise OAGs. Predicted and chronological age were strongly correlated across organs (average Pearson correlation coefficient [PCC] 0.861 ± 0.0245). OAGs were organ-specific yet clinically informative across 20 age-related diseases and 16 age-related phenotypes and improved prediction for both organ-matched and cross-organ outcomes. Comparison with plasma-protein-based proteomic age gap showed only weak correlations, supporting partial overlap rather than redundancy and integrated age models improved chronological-age prediction without consistently outperforming organ-specific OAG in downstream disease prediction. Plasma proteomic analyses identified 54-154 OAG-associated proteins per organ, including nine shared across all four organs that were also associated with all-cause mortality. Temporal analyses showed structured but non-uniform proteomic changes, with relative enrichment between ages 55 and 70. Behavioural analyses highlighted robust smoking-related associations across organs, together with more selective associations involving alcohol intake, sleep duration and physical activity. This framework quantifies organ-specific age and supports systematic interpretation of OAGs across clinical, molecular, temporal and behavioural dimensions. Multimodal OAG and proteomic age gap capture partially overlapping but complementary ageing information.

papers.title: Light-entrained chromatin priming poises rapid metamorphosis in a marine sponge.
papers.abstract: The most widespread animal life cycle includes a planktonic larval stage that is environmentally induced to settle and rapidly metamorphose into a benthic juvenile. Although this transition is critical for survival, how planetary cues such as light interact with local ecological signals to prepare the genome for such rapid reprogramming remains poorly understood. Here, using the sponge Amphimedon queenslandica, we integrate time-resolved transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility profiling across larval competence, settlement, and the first hours of metamorphosis. We show that diminishing light at sunset is associated with extensive chromatin remodelling in swimming larvae prior to settlement despite relatively modest changes in gene expression. Upon environmental induction by a coralline alga, metamorphosis is accompanied by the rapid and transient activation of a large suite of deeply conserved transcription factors (TFs), including AP-1/bZIP family members, whose binding motifs are enriched in newly accessible regulatory regions near differentially expressed genes. Larvae prevented from experiencing sunset by constant light fail to settle and instead adopt an alternative transcriptional and chromatin state characterised by widespread loss of accessibility and repression of competence-associated TFs, including the circadian regulator CLOCK and other bHLH-PAS factors. These observations support a model in which light-entrained transcriptional activity establishes an anticipatory, permissive chromatin landscape that enables immediate and coordinated transcriptional reprogramming upon environmental induction. We propose that such chromatin priming may represent a broadly deployed regulatory strategy underlying the speed and robustness of metamorphosis in biphasic animal life cycles.

papers.title: Motivational Biases in Go and Nogo Learning From Immediate Versus Delayed Feedback.
papers.abstract: Motivational biases in decision-making describe the phenomenon that individuals are more likely to perform an action to receive a reward and to withhold an action to avoid punishment. These biases likely originate from reward-related modulations of the striatum, presumably reflecting biased action selection and/or learning, the latter with facilitated learning from rewarded actions and impaired learning from punished inactions. As striatal engagement during learning depends on whether feedback is presented immediately or delayed, the present study examined whether motivational biases are similarly sensitive to feedback timing. Moreover, based on the idea that motivational biases arise through biased learning, we tested whether they manifest as biased feedback processing for action over inaction. Fifty-six healthy participants performed an orthogonalized go/nogo task learning whether to execute or withhold a response in both reward obtainment and loss-avoidance contexts-either receiving immediate (n = 28) or delayed feedback (n = 28). Applying computational modeling of choice behavior and using electroencephalography (EEG), we assessed biased instrumental learning and its neural signature in feedback processing, focusing on the feedback-related negativity/reward positivity and the P3 in the event-related potential (ERP). Behavioral results demonstrated robust motivational biases across learning from immediate and delayed feedback. Importantly, motivational biases were best explained in terms of biased action selection rather than biased learning, aligning with our ERP findings that did not provide evidence for action-biased feedback processing. Taken together, these results highlight motivational biases as a robust hallmark of decision-making, relying on common mechanisms involved in both learning from immediate and delayed feedback.

papers.title: UK Medical Cannabis Registry: A Two-Year Prospective Observational Cohort Study of Clinical Outcomes in Insomnia.
papers.abstract: Insomnia disorder affects approximately 10% of people. The persistence of insomnia, despite treatment, remains high. Cannabis-based medicinal products (CBMPs) have been proposed as a potential treatment for insomnia. This study aims to use data from the UK Medical Cannabis Registry to analyze changes in self-reported sleep quality in patients prescribed CBMPs for insomnia. A prospective cohort study of patients treated with CBMPs for insomnia was completed. The primary outcome was the Single-Item Sleep Quality Scale (SQS).
